On the evening of December 5, at around 7 p.m., while he was returning home, his bicycle tyre got punctured near Bhattapar village. On the way, he approached some people sitting by bonfire, asking about any puncture shop nearby,” Mr. Shakib said.
He further said, “Those people asked his name and as soon as he revealed his name, Mohammad Athar Hussain, they began hitting him with a burning piece of wood. They then cut off his ear, feet, and fingers with pliers. They dragged him to a room and beat him up brutally, hitting him on the head and chest. They even inserted an iron rod into his anus. When he got unconscious due to excessive beating for hours, they threw him on the roadside at midnight.”
Mr. Hussain had also recounted his trauma before being taken to the Primary Health Centre (PHC) in Roh, from where he was referred to Nawada Sadar Hospital and later to Pawapuri, where he died.
Ms. Parveen also claimed that her husband was beaten up after being asked about his religion.
“He was the sole bread winner for the family, and I have three small children. How will I now take care of my children? There is no source of income. The way he was beaten up was inhumane; even animals are not beaten up like that. All the criminals should be hanged till death,” Ms. Parveen told the press on Monday (December 15, 2025).
In a press note issued on December 13, 2025, the office of Nawada Superintendent of Police (SP) Abhinav Dhiman stated, “In view of the seriousness of the incident, a special team was formed under the leadership of the Sadar SDPO [sub-divisional police officer] and directed to arrest the accused. The constituted team arrested four named accused involved in the incident under 24 hours and sent them to judicial custody.”
It further stated, “On December 13, 2025, based on further investigations, four more accused involved in the case were arrested. To date, a total of eight accused have been arrested in the case. All of them have subsequently been remanded to judicial custody.”
The police said that continuous raids were being conducted to arrest the remaining accused.
Opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) spokesperson Ejaz Ahmed slammed the State government, saying Home Minister Samrat Choudhary often talked big about law and order, while in reality, mob lynchings were being carried out based on religion and caste, and people were being beaten to death in inhumane ways.
Meanwhile, in Muzaffarpur district, a man, along with his three daughters, died by suicide early morning on Monday (December 15, 2025) in Mishrauliya village under Sakra police station limits.
The 40-year-old man was identified as Amarnath Ram and his three daughters were aged between 7 and 12. The man also tried to hang his two minor sons but they survived. According to the police, he was going through tough financial situation after the death of his wife last year.
Those in distress can seek counselling from national mental health helpline Tele MANAS at toll-free number 14416.

title: Veteran leader Shamanur Shivashankarappa laid to rest with state honours
summary: Veteran leader Shamanur Shivashankarappa laid to rest with state honors, drawing thousands in mourning, including top political figures.
content:
Veteran politician, educationist, and industrialist Shamanur Shivashankarappa was laid to rest with state honours, with thousands of people, seers, eminent personalities, including Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, AICC President Mallikarjun Kharge, and others paying last respects and participating in the funeral in Davangere on Monday.
A host of seers from various communities, other leaders including Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, Speaker U.T. Khader, Chairman of Legislative Council Basavraj Horatti, former Chief Ministers B.S. Yediyurappa, Jagadish Shettar, Basavaraj Bommai, a host of Ministers including Eshwar B. Khandre and M.B. Patil, legislators from various political parties and others paid last respects.
Prior to the State funeral, the mortal remains of the veteran politician were taken in a procession across the city, starting from the residence of the late leader. The body was kept at High School Grounds for people to pay their last respects. The funeral procession then began from the Ground to Kalleshwara Rice Mill, where the mortal remains were laid to rest.
The whole city seemed to be in mourning with roads wearing a deserted look as most of the shops and commercial establishments remaining closed as a mark of respect to the veteran Congress leader and Lingayat strongman.
The funeral was conducted with state honours and as per Veerashaiva Lingayat tradition in the presence of the family members, Chief Minister Siddaramaih, and a host of other leaders. The mortal remains were buried next to the samadhi of Shivashankarappa’s wife Parvathi on the premises of Kalleshwara Rice Mill.
A host of seers from Veerashaiva Lingayat community were present, seers of other communities including Immadi Siddarameshwar Swami, Madar Channayya Swami, Srikrishna Yadavanand Swami, Shanthaveer Swami, Keteshwar Swami and others were among those who paid last respects.

title: Home Minister offers prayers at ‘Padamara Veedhi Ganganamma Jatara’ in Eluru
summary: Home Minister Vangalapudi Anitha offers prayers at Eluru's Padamara Veedhi Ganganamma Jatara, accompanied by local officials and family.
content:
State Home Minister Vangalapudi Anitha, along with family, offered prayers at the ‘Padamara Veedhi Ganganamma Jatara’ in Eluru, on Monday.
The Home Minister was given a ceremonial welcome at the temple by Jatara Committee chairpersons Chode Balasubrahmanyam and Chode Venkaratnam. As part of the festivities, Ms. Anitha visited the decorated ‘mandapams’ and offered prayers to Sri Ganganamma, Sri Mahalakshmamma, Sri Vinukonda Ankamma and Sri Pothuraju Babu, and presented sare (offerings) to the deities.
Eluru MLA Badeti Chanti and Mayor Sheikh Noorjahan accompanied the Minister and presented a sari to the presiding deity and participated in special pujas.
Several public representatives and officials were present during the visit, including Eluru Municipal Corporation co-option member S.M.R. Pedababu, RTC Regional Chairman Reddi Appalanaidu, Eluru Agricultural Market Committee Chairman Mamillapalli Parthasaradhi, temple priest Niranjan, and other local leaders.

title: Priest protests in Delhi, seeks development and recognition of Srimukhalingam temple
summary: Priest protests in Delhi, urging government support for Srimukhalingam temple's development and UNESCO recognition.
content:
A birds eye view of the Srimukhalingam temple on the banks of the Vamsadhara River in Srikakulam district. 
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                File Photo
The chief priest of the Srimukhalingam temple Naidugari Rajasekhar has urged the Union and State governments to take up the development of the one of the oldest Lord Shiva temple located in Srimukhalingam village of Srikakulam district.
Mr Rajasekhar staged a two-day protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on Sunday and Monday, and appealed to the government to sanction funds for the development of the temple surroundings. His demands include the development of connecting roads, underground drainage system, street lights, cottages near temple, and dedicated staff for maintenance of the temple.
Mr. Rajasekhar said that developing Srimukhlaingam as a model village would attract more pilgrims and tourist from across the country. He also urged the government to initiate steps for obtaining UNESCO recognition for the temple believed to have been constructed 1,500 years ago in the district.

title: Banks urged to balance growth with risk management amid rising fintech competition
summary: Banks must balance growth and risk management amidst rising fintech competition and evolving financial behaviors in India.
content:
About 73% of the total credit in India is provided by Reserve Bank of India-regulated entities, with commercial banks alone accounting for nearly half of this share. But mutual funds and fintech firms are increasingly participating in credit provision and the competition is intensifying, former RBI Governor and chancellor of ICFAI Foundation for Higher Education C. Rangarajan noted on Monday (December 15).
Highlighting the current trends in the evolving structure of India’s banking and financial system here at the two-day ‘Academicians and Practitioners Summit on Banking and Finance’, he said performance of financial institutions must be assessed across operational efficiency (cost of functioning) and allocative efficiency (equitable spread of credit).
Mr. Rangarajan also noted that household investment behaviours are evolving; bank deposits see a decline as there is an increasing participation in shares and debentures.
While commending improvements in NPA management and prudential regulation in the system, he warned that excessive reliance on loan write-offs could distort the true picture of asset quality. He stressed that banks must match their growth aspirations with prudent risk management, and ensure that credit allocation aligns with sustainable, inclusive economic development.
According to former CEO of Reserve Bank Innovation Hub Rajesh Bansal, digitally native generations such as Gen Z and millennials are redefining financial behaviour and expectations, and in a few decades, half of all money spent in India will be by Gen Z. Despite India’s strong digital infrastructure, he noted that only 35% of Indians actively use digital banking, compared to higher adoption rates in smaller economies like Kenya.
He also advocated greater inclusivity in digital finance through voice-enabled interfaces in regional languages, AI-driven credit scoring models, predictive analytics for cash-flow forecasting and tailored financial planning tools.

title: 20 disputes settled, ₹6.81 lakh collected at Yadgir Lok Adalat
summary: Yadgir Lok Adalat resolves 20 disputes, collecting ₹6.81 lakh from vehicle owners in a successful settlement session.
content:
The Lok Adalat organised to settle disputes between the Transport Department and vehicle owners concluded in Monday with a collection of ₹6.81 lakh in tax.
The Lok Adalat was organised after a direction came from Principal and Sessions Judge Marulasiddaradhya and Road Transport Officers and vehicle owners participated in it.
“As many as 20 cases were settled amicably and ₹6,81,259 in tax was collected from vehicle owners. Documents related to vehicles, like registration certificate, insurance, fitness certificate, emission test certificate and permit, were inspected,” an officer said.
Advising vehicle owners to adhere to the law, Mr. Marulasiddaradhya said that the documents should be kept ready when sought for and also ensure that the tax is paid to the government well within time.

title: UDF comeback to reshape political balance in Malabar
summary: UDF's surprising comeback in Malabar local body polls signals a potential shift in the region's political landscape.
content:
The performance of the three major fronts in the three-tier local body polls last week reveals that the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) has scripted a surprising comeback that could potentially reshape the political balance in Malabar.
However, the results across the six districts have not eroded the base of the ruling Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI-M]-led Left Democratic Front (LDF), which is politically strong in Kasaragod, Kannur, Kozhikode, and Palakkad districts.
This was evident in the number of seats won by the Left parties in the district panchayats, undoubtedly attributed to political mandate, which were nine out of 18 in Kasaragod, 18 out of 25 in Kannur, 13 out of 28 in Kozhikode and 19 out of 31 in Palakkad.
The same voting pattern could be seen in block panchayats - Kasaragod four out of six, Kannur - eight out of 11, Kozhikode eight out of 12 and nine out of 13 in Palakkad.
Such an uptrend was not seen in Wayanad where the UDF converted what had been a closely balanced contest last time into a decisive lead in the district panchayat and clock panchayats.
Nevertheless, like in most parts of the State, the UDF drastically overturned the ruling LDF’s hegemony established in the previous local body polls in 2020. The resurgence of the front has been particularly witnessed in Kozhikode, Wayanad and Kasaragod districts.
Malappuram remained the Congress–Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) bulwark like in the previous elections, with the front tightening its grip on grama and block panchayats as well as municipalities in the district. The LDF drew a blank in the district panchayat.
With the LDF receding from its 2020 levels, trends pointed to a clear UDF advantage across both rural and urban segments in Kasaragod. Likewise,  Kannur, long regarded as the citadel of the Left, witnessed UDF breakthroughs across multiple local bodies.
These advances have sharply reduced the LDF’s traditional advantages, signalling a weakening of its once-formidable cadre base.
Anti-incumbency sentiments, allegations of Sabarimala gold theft, disenchantment and consolidation among Muslim community have been attributed to voters favouring the UDF.
Regarding the two Corporations in the region, the UDF retained the Kannur civic body, while the LDF failed to get a majority on its own in the Kozhikode council. Besides, the UDF also registered major electoral gains, particularly in the Corporation and municipalities, eroding the Left’s earlier edge.
Incidentally, the BJP-led NDA’s visible strength remains largely confined to urban pockets and some rural areas in Kasaragod and Palakkad districts. Overall, the party’s performance continued to garner only a token share of support across north Kerala.
However, its vote share has markedly improved, especially in Kozhikode Corporation, but it failed to achieve an outright majority in Palakkad municipality. The party won the lone district panchayat seat in Kasaragod.
With the political equilibrium realigned in the local body polls, the stage has been set for a high-voltage contest in the Assembly polls in April next year.

title: Tributes paid to Amarajeevi Potti Sriramulu on his death anniversary
summary: Tributes were paid to Amarajeevi Potti Sriramulu on his death anniversary in Kurnool and Nandyal, honoring his sacrifice for a separate State.
content:
Rich tributes were paid to Amarajeevi Potti Sriramulu on his death anniversary, in Kurnool and Nandyal on Monday (December 15, 2025).
Minister for Industries and Commerce T.G. Bharath, District Collector Dr. A. Siri, Kurnool Urban Development Authority (KUDA) chairperson Somiseetty Venkateswarlu and others paid floral tributes to the statue of Potti Sriramulu at Poola Bazar in Kurnool city. Mr. Bharath said that the sacrifice made by Potti Sriramulu for a separate State for Telugu people will be remembered forever.
Mr. Bharath said that the NDA government had been organising the birth and death anniversary celebrations of the freedom fighter as a State function, and had even allocated 6.8 acres of land for installing a statue of Potti Sriramulu at Amaravati. He said that the TGV Group will donate ₹1 crore for development works at the proposed statue in Amaravati and promised to develop the existing Potti Sriramulu statue in Kurnool city.
Mr. Bharath said that the youth should follow the ideologies of Potti Sriramulu and serve the State and country. “Potti Sriramulu sat on an indefinite fast on October 19, 1952 in Madras and breathed his last on December 15, 1952 for the sake of a separate linguistic State for Telugu people,” he said.
Dr. Siri said that Potti Sriramulu’s sacrifice will be remembered forever and his life should be a role model to others.
In Nandyal, Collector Rajakumari Ganiya paid tributes to Potti Sriramulu’s portrait in the district Collectorate.

title: CM to open labour conclave on December 19
summary: Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan to inaugurate a labour conclave on December 19, addressing rights against new Labour Codes.
content:
Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan will inaugurate a labour conclave being organised by the State government to formulate an alternative policy that protects the rights of the State and its workers against the four Labour Codes newly notified by the Union government.
The day-long conclave will begin at Lemon Tree Premier hotel, Thycaud, at 10 a.m. on December 19.
Addressing a press conference here on Monday (December 15, 2025), Minister for Labour V. Sivankutty said Punjab Labour Minister Tarunpreet Singh, Tamil Nadu Labour Minister C.V. Ganesan, Jharkhand Labour Minister Sanjay Prasad Yadav, and Telangana Labour Minister Vivek Venkatswamy would attend the conclave as part of a united struggle against the Labour Codes being “imposed” on States.
Minister for Finance K.N. Balagopal and Minister for Industries P. Rajeeve would also participate in the conclave.
Two technical sessions to be attended by former Supreme Court judges, Advocate General, national and State trade union representatives, legal experts, and academics would be held as part of the conclave, the Minister said.
The first session will be on the impact of Labour Codes. Former Supreme Court judge V. Gopala Gowda will deliver the keynote address. It will be presided over by Advocate General K. Gopalakrishna Kurup.
Another session will be on alternative strategies to deal with the Labour Codes against the backdrop of the State’s labour policy.
Shyam Sundar, Professor, will deliver the keynote address in the session to be presided over by CPI(M) leader Elamaram Karim.
Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU) general secretary Tapan Sen, All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) general secretary Amarjit Kaur will take part in the discussions.
A policy for protecting the State’s interests will be announced at the valedictory of the conclave.
The Minister said he, along with representatives of national trade unions, would meet and hand over to the Union Labour Minister a letter containing demands that include the philosophy of the policy.

title: Kudumbashree launches brand for Sabarimala forest harvests
summary: Project aims to collect products such as honey, camphor, ginger, Dantha Pala (Dyer’s Oleander), and Ponkarandi (Salacia oblonga)
content:
The sweet taste of entrepreneurship is now taking root deep within the Sabarimala forests.
The District Kudumbashree Mission has rolled out a new programme titled ‘Vana Shuddhi’, which seeks to turn the traditional livelihood of Malaipandaram, a semi-nomadic tribal community into a sustainable and market-ready livelihood.
Implemented under the 2024 Malaipandaram Microplan, the project aims to collect forest products such as honey, camphor, ginger, Dantha Pala (Dyer’s Oleander), and Ponkarandi (Salacia oblonga) directly from the tribal community. With the support of HortiCorp, these products are scientifically processed, branded and sold through dedicated kiosks, the first of which is already operational in Pathanamthitta
Most Malaipandaram families live on the forest fringes of Ranni, Perunad, Seethathode, Aruvappulam, and Thannithode, relying on forest resources for daily sustenance. “The project is also about preserving traditional knowledge, empowering around 100 families, and giving their skills the recognition they deserve,” says Adhila. S, Kudumbashree district mission coordinator,  Pathanamthitta.
According to her, traditional practices of honey collection followed by the tribal community preserves its natural flavour, aroma, and medicinal properties. Likewise, all forest products sources by this community from the forest maintain purity, quality and health benefits, she pointed out.
Guided by Kudumbashree consortium members and ST animators and with direct market access via kiosks, the initiative seeks to cut off intermediaries and ensures fair returns.
In the long run, Vana Shuddhi promises to strengthen livelihoods, amplify the value of forest produce, and turn the ancestral knowledge of the Malaipandaram into a thriving enterprise, she added.
As per a survey by the Kudumbashree held last year, the Malaipandaram community in the district consists of just 837 members across 12 settlements. Of these, 109 families remain without permanent housing despite land allocations in their name.

title: ‘Bhavani Deeksha Viramana’ concludes with ‘Poornahuti’ at Indrakeeladri
summary: Over 5.15 lakh devotees celebrate Bhavani Deeksha Viramana's grand conclusion with Poornahuti at Indrakeeladri temple.
content:
The ‘Bhavani Deeksha Viramana’ (relinquishment of deeksha) concluded on a grand manner with the performance of ‘Poornahuti’ at Sri Durga Malleswara Swamy Varla Devasthanam atop Indrakeeladri, on Monday.
The temple priests performed Poornahuti at the ‘yagasaala’ near Sivalayam, which marked the end of five-day ritual this year. Amid the chanting of Vedic hymns, the temple priests offered a silk sari, sandalwood pieces, ghee, flowers and fruits to the ‘homam’, and ‘ashirvachanam’ (blessings) were given to the devotees.  The Poornahuti was performed  under the supervision of temple sthanacharya Siva Prasad, chief priest Durga Prasad, and members of the Vedic committee.
Thousands of Bhavani devotees, after taking a holy dip in the Krishna river, made a beeline for the Kanaka Durga temple since midnight and offered special pujas to the goddess to mark the relinquishment. The devotees also undertook mandatory ‘giri pradakshina’ as part of Bhavani Deeksha Viramana ritual.
The giri pradakshana was done by some devotees even on Monday and the roads were painted red with devotees turning up in the traditional red dress. The vicinity of Indrakeeladri reverberated with chants and slogans of ‘Bhavani Mata Ki Jai’, ‘Jai Bhavani Jai Jai Bhavani’ as Bhavanis stormed in large numbers to relinquish ‘deeksha’.
According to official statistics from December 11 to 11 a.m. on December 15, over 5.15 lakh devotees visited the temple during the Bhavani Deekshas. Nearly 21.20 lakh laddus were distributed, while 2,03,645 devotees had annaprasadams. Additionally, 51,435 devotees offered hair at the Kalyanakatta.
Meanwhile, addressing a press conference at Indrakeeladri, NTR District Collector Lakshmisha said the Bhavani Deekshas concluded successfully. He attributed the success to meticulous planning and coordinated efforts from all departments, including Revenue, Police, Endowments, and Municipal wings.
The Collector highlighted innovative arrangements such as unlimited laddu distribution, uninterrupted annaprasadam, and enhanced drinking water facilities. He also invited feedback from devotees to further improve services in the future and thanked all departments and media representatives for the support.
Devasthanam Chairman Borra Radhakrishna (Gandhi), Executive Officer V.K. Seena Naik, Festival Officer Murthy (EO, Dwaraka Tirumala), trust board members, and temple staff participated in the programme.

title: After DKS remarks, BNP says apartment residents’ anger stems from years of govt. inaction
summary: After Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said that there was no need to ‘threaten’ him, the Bengaluru NavaNirmana Party said residents’ anger was a natural outcome of years of government inaction on basic issues affecting people living in apartment complexes
content:
After Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said that there was no need to “threaten” him, the Bengaluru NavaNirmana Party (BNP) on Monday said residents’ anger was a natural outcome of years of government inaction on basic issues affecting people living in apartment complexes.
Mr. Shivakumar made the remarks during a recent interaction with members of the Bangalore Apartments’ Federation (BAF), when he read out a letter that “cautioned” him about the continued neglect of their issues. Responding to the letter, Mr. Shivakumar said that such language reflected a lack of basic common sense and argued that if he were indifferent to people’s problems, he would not have invited them or sought their suggestions.
Responding to this, the party said such expressions of frustration were inevitable when repeated appeals to the government fail to bring any relief. The party argued that apartment residents have been flagging the same problems for several years, but their concerns have largely been ignored.
Srikanth Narasimhan, founder and general secretary of BNP and also the founder of the BAF, said BNP had been raising issues related to the basic needs of apartment residents for the past three years, without any response from either the government or the Deputy Chief Minister. These were not minor administrative inconveniences, he said, but systemic problems that place unfair financial and logistical burdens on a large section of Bengaluru’s population. The government, he added, must first demonstrate its commitment to good governance by resolving these basic issues before seeking votes from residents.
BNP said it had repeatedly represented these matters to politicians and bureaucrats and has met several of them, including the Deputy Chief Minister on multiple occasions. Among the key grievances highlighted by the party is what it described as a discriminatory water tariff, under which apartment residents are charged three to five times more than individual house owners despite consuming similar quantities of water. The party also flagged what it termed an unfair solid waste management user fee, which it said has resulted in double charging of residents who manage their own waste.
BNP further alleged that apartment owners have received illegal property tax show-cause and demand notices for parking slots that they do not even own. Another major issue raised was the high cost imposed on residents for converting properties from B-Khata to A-Khata, which the party said arose from past collusion between builders and politicians.
In addition to these, BNP said several fundamental issues remain unresolved, including delays in implementing the apartment Act, improper implementation of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act (RERA), and continuing problems related to mutation and transfer of property ownership. The party said unless these issues are addressed, dissatisfaction among apartment residents is likely to continue.

title: Raghu Vamsi opens new facility, unveils six UAV, autonomous defence products
summary: Raghu Vamsi Aerospace Group launches a ₹100 crore facility, unveiling six UAVs and autonomous defence products in Hyderabad.
content:
Raghu Vamsi Aerospace Group on Monday formally launched its ₹100 crore DeepTech design, production and integration facility at Hardware Park, near Hyderabad international airport.
Six indigenous UAV and autonomous defence products under a new subsidiary and brand, Arrobot, were unveiled by the Group in the presence of Vice Chief of the Naval Staff Vice Admiral Sanjay Vatsayan; Bharat Dynamics CMD Commodore A. Madhavarao (retd.); Maj. Gen. Shivendra Kumar, ADG–EME, Indian Army; former Scientific Advisor to Defence Minister and former Chairman of DRDO G. Satheesh Reddy and others. Jet-powered loitering munitions, tethered surveillance drones, air-based missile launchers and micro turbojet engines form part of the products, with range exceeding 300 km and speeds up to 650 kmph.
The Group also signed four MoUs, including one with the 515 Army Base Workshop of the Indian Army for co-design, development, testing and validation of advanced drone platforms and associated system. Others MoUs were with Bharat Dynamics for co-development and supply of fully indigenised 200 kgf thrust-class engines to power next-generation autonomous fighter-aircraft platforms; with IIIT Hyderabad for co-development of advanced AI-based autonomy, intelligent perception, swarm intelligence and mission systems to accelerate smart UAV development for defence applications; and with ARCI for collaborative development of laser cladding, additive manufacturing, and thermal barrier coating applications in advancing new aero engine technologies.
Located near a clutch of other Raghu Vamsi as well as a ₹300 crore plant the Group announced last year, the new, 25,000 sq ft facility will house design-to-assembly manufacturing for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), engines and advanced defence systems unit.
The new facility strengthens its ability to support Indian strategic programmes and global customers with faster turnaround times and scalable production, Raghu Vamsi Aerospace Group said. The Group, which has 10 manufacturing sites in three countries and more than 1,000 employees, expects the ₹300 crore manufacturing facility to be ready by 2026. It will comprise three buildings totalling 2.5 lakh sq ft feet on eight acres and estimated to generate employment for over 2,000 people over three years.
Founder and MD Vamsi Vikas said the Group order book for the next three years is around ₹1,500 crore and given the growing demand for the products a new bigger manufacturing facility could not be ruled out. The Group revenues are expected to cross ₹500 crore this year.

title: Driver Sensitisation Tab launched to educate drivers on road safety behaviour
summary: Diageo India launches Driver Sensitisation Tab Lab in Vijayawada to promote road safety awareness among new drivers.
content:
Deputy Transport Commissioner Meera Prasad inaugurated a new Driver Sensitisation Tab Lab set up by Diageo India (United Spirits Limited), in partnership with BharatCares and the Andhra Pradesh Transport Department, at the RTO office, here on Monday.
New drivers will be educated on road safety behaviour at the lab through a mandatory 45-minute module featuring interactive video content and behavioural assessments designed to promote safe driving habits. By simulating real-life scenarios, the programme emphasises the importance of safety, making a tangible impact on driver behaviour and road safety.
Addressing the gathering, Mr. Meera Prasad said road safety was a key priority for the State government and that it was committed to reducing accidents through sustained awareness and behavioural-change initiatives.
The Driver Sensitisation Tab Lab will strengthen the government’s efforts by equipping new drivers with practical, simulation-based learning, he said, appreciating Diageo India and BharatCares for advancing responsible driving and helping build safer roads for all.
Diageo IndiaCorporate Relations head Devashish Dasguptaand Mayank Pathak of BharatCares were among those present.

title: UDF will have ‘easy walkover’ in Assembly polls in Kerala, says IUML
summary: IUML predicts an easy victory for UDF in Kerala Assembly polls, citing public frustration with the ruling LDF government.
content:
The Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) seems to be confident of an “easy walkover victory” for the United Democratic Front (UDF) in the next Assembly polls in Kerala in view of the Congress-led coalition’s impressive performance in the just concluded elections to the local bodies.
IUML State general secretary P.M.A. Salam said here on Monday that the people of the State and the UDF “were on the same page” over their antagonism towards the Left Democratic Front (LDF) government. He was addressing the media after a meeting of the party’s State functionaries, leaders of affiliate units, and MLAs.
Mr. Salam claimed that the people were fed up with the misgovernance, nepotism, corruption, and communal attitude of the ruling party in power. The voters exercised their franchise to express their frustration, he said. “The government and the ruling party deliberately tried to create a communal division in society. They also honoured people who unleashed a communal propaganda. Efforts were also made to tarnish the image of a particular place and its residents,” Mr. Salam alleged.
Asked if he was referring to some of the comments made by Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam general secretary Vellappally Natesan, the IUML leader said that some of those remarks could have adversely affected the electoral performance of the LDF. “The government did not have anything to talk about development and social welfare in the past 10 years. That is why it tried to divide the people on communal lines,” Mr. Salam said.
He clarified that the UDF never had any alliance with the Jamaat-e-Islami Hind. However, in certain places, there were some local-level understanding with the Welfare Party of India, he said.
Earlier, IUML State president Panakkad Syed Sadikali Shihab Thangal and national general secretary P.K. Kunhalikutty said that efforts would be made to strengthen the UDF by adding more like-minded parties into the coalition.

title: Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s bronze statue unveiled in Nellore
summary: A bronze statue of Atal Bihari Vajpayee was unveiled in Nellore to honour his centenary and contributions to India.
content:
On the occasion of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s centenary, his bronze statue was unveiled by BJP State president P.V.N. Madhav along with local ministers, MPs, MLAs and public representatives at Harnathapuram Circle in Nellore on Monday (December 15, 2025) as a part of Atal Sandesh Yatra (Atal-Modi Suparipaalana Bus Yatra).
Ministers Satya Kumar Yadav and Anam Ramanarayana Reddy, Lok Sabha Member Vemireddy Prabhakar Reddy, Rajya Sabha Member Beeda Masthan Rao, MLAs Vemireddy Prashanti Reddy and Somireddy Chandramohan Reddy and other leaders and officials were present at the programme.
Lauding the services of the former Prime Minister, Mr. Madhav said, “Atal Bihari Vajpayee was a selfless leader who had set the right direction for the country. He had initiated several steps towards good governance and development in the country. His reign in the history of India is worth writing in golden letters.”
MP Vemireddy said, “In his 50-year long political career, Vajpayee had served the country as an MP for 11 times and as the Prime Minister three times. He had established road connectivity to the mega cities of Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai and Mumbai through the prestigious Golden Quadrilateral project. He is known for his unwavering commitment to the country.
He further said, “It is good that his birth anniversary has been declared as Good Governance Day. Similar to the earlier combination of Vajpayee and Nara Chandrababu Naidu as the PM and CM, Andhra Pradesh is moving forward on the path of development today, under the leadership of Narendra Modi and Naidu.”

title: Chandrababu Naidu unveils ‘A Tale of Two States’ book
summary: Chandrababu Naidu launches ‘A Tale of Two States,’ exploring the history of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana's political journey.
content:
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu unveiled ‘A Tale of Two States’, authored by senior journalist I. Venkata Rao, at his residence here on Monday. The book is an English translation of ‘Vileenam -Vibhajana’, translated by N. Anuradha.
The work chronicles the historic journey of the Telugu States from their unification to the eventual bifurcation into Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. It also profiles all 22 Chief Ministers who have led these States, starting from Burugula Ramakrishna Rao to the present Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy.
Originally well-received in Telugu, the author and translator expressed hope that this English edition will serve as a valuable resource for non-Telugu readers interested in the political and cultural history of the region.
Congratulating N. Anuradha for her efforts, Mr. Chandrababu Naidu remarked that the book would be an important reference for researchers and future generations.
I. Venkata Rao, N. Anuradha, writer and former IRS officer K. Chandrahas, and publishers I. Venu and I. Raghu were present.

title: Government urged to include lesson on Potti Sriramulu in schoolbooks
summary: Srikakulam leaders urge inclusion of Potti Sriramulu's legacy in schoolbooks to honor his sacrifice for Andhra State.
content:
Leaders of the Amarajeevi Potti Sriramulu Pavitra Smruti Parirakshana Samithi in Srikakulam have urged the government to include a lesson on Potti Sriramulu in schoolbooks so that future generations learn about his sacrifice for the creation of a separate Andhra State in 1953.
The  association’s Srikakulam district president Tammana Bhaskar and district secretary Mandavilli Swami Srinivas Gupta on Monday made the appeal on Monday after paying floral tributes to the statue of Potti Sriramulu in Gandhi Park to mark his death anniversary.
They  recalled Sriramulu’s contribution to the creation of  linguistic States in India following his hunger strike held between October 19 and December 15, 1952, which eventually .  Mr. Bhaskar urged the government to release funds for the development of a memorial building in Chennai where Potti Sriramulu had  breathed his last while fasting to achieve a separate State for the people of Andhra region.
The association leaders Pasumarthi Appala Raju, Manda Nageswara Rao, Mamidipaka Sudhakar, Tammana Jagadish, Patnala Anand, Anantapalli Nageswara Rao participated in the event.

title: GBA targets vaccination of over 11.34 lakh children during pulse polio drive
summary: The Greater Bengaluru Authority has set a target of administering pulse polio drops to over 11.34 lakh children under the age of five during the National Pulse Polio Campaign scheduled from December 21 to 24, GBA Chief Commissioner M. Maheshwar Rao said
content:
The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) has set a target of administering pulse polio drops to over 11.34 lakh children under the age of five during the National Pulse Polio Campaign scheduled from December 21 to 24, GBA Chief Commissioner M. Maheshwar Rao said on Monday.
Chairing a virtual review meeting on the preparedness for the campaign, Mr. Rao directed officials across all five city corporations to take necessary steps to ensure 100% coverage. He emphasised the need for intensive awareness drives and instructed officials to deploy additional mobile vaccination teams in densely populated areas, including bus stands, markets, railway and metro stations, malls, major parks, tourist spots, slum areas, and other venues where people are expected in large numbers.
The GBA Chief also called for the involvement of students from nursing, medical and paramedical colleges as volunteers to support the campaign. He said that apartment associations also had been contacted and urged to actively participate in ensuring that all eligible children are vaccinated.
Chief Health Officer S.S. Madani said that pulse polio booths would function across the city on December 21 from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., followed by door-to-door vaccination from December 22 to 24.
Over 11.34 lakh children are targeted for vaccination across the five corporations. The campaign will be carried out through 4,452 vaccination points, including 3,391 fixed booths.

title: LDF has the political heft to return to power in 2026, says Govindan
summary: CPI(M) asserts LDF's strength to retain power in 2026, dismissing local poll results as opposition propaganda and anti-incumbency claims.
content:
The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] State secretariat on Monday countered the narrative of the Congress and the Bharatiya Janata Party, in the aftermath of the local body poll results, comparing the Left Democratic Front to a ‘sinking ship’ floundering to stay politically afloat in the run-up to the 2026 Assembly elections.
After a preliminary post-poll stocktaking at the AKG Centre here, CPI(M) State secretary M.V. Govindan said the LDF possessed the political heft to retain power for a third consecutive term in the 2026 Assembly polls. He denied that the local body polls’ outcome was a verdict against the government. “The LDF remains the dominant force in 58 Assembly constituencies. It retains a fighting chance to win back those lost to the UDF by a relatively narrow margin. There is no anti-incumbency wave as touted by the Opposition,” he said.
Mr. Govindan denied that UDF’s “overtures” to Kerala Congress (M) and other minor allies had rendered the ruling alliance shaky. “The LDF’s unity will endure transient triumphs and setbacks,” he stated.
Mr. Govindan countered the UDF’s take that the CPI(M) had experimented with ‘Left Hindutva’ by courting “Muslim-baiting” Hindu leaders. (Notably, the UDF had bandied around the term at the hustings as an euphemistic political coinage to portray LDF’s criticism of the ‘revanchist’ drift in the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) leadership and its ‘Congress-backed affinity’ towards the ‘Islamist’ Jamaat-e-Islami as patently anti-Muslim and pro-Hindutva). “The LDF polled 10 lakh votes in Malappuram,” Mr. Govindan underscored.
Mr. Govindan dismissed as mere hyperbole the Bharatiya Janata Party-led National Democratic Alliance’s (NDA) claim that it had become a winning alliance in Kerala. He said the NDA registered a modicum of success with the UDF’s help in the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation. However, the alliance made no impact in the district panchayat polls. The NDA won just a single district panchayat seat in Kasaragod.
Mr. Govindan denied that the Sabarimala gold theft scandal and the contentious Global Ayyappa Sangamam in September had pushed the Hindutva agenda, arguably dormant since the emotive Save Sabarimala Campaign in 2018, to the centre of the election debate, catalysing communally coloured identity politics and relegating other issues, including livelihood matters, welfare, and development, to the back-burner.
“Sabarimala and Ayyappa faith scarcely benefited the Hindutva forces. The LDF wrested the Pandalam muncipality, a region that lies at the heart of the Sabarimala lore, from the NDA. The BJP lost the Sabarimala ward and the panchayats of Kulanada, Cherukol, and Mutholi in the Ayyappa heartland to the LDF. The NDA’s bid to wrest control of the temple cities, chiefly Guruvayur, Kodungaloor, Taliparamba, Thrissur and Parassini Kadavu, failed,” he stated.

title: Special NSS wing conducts special camp in Sanambatla
summary: SPMVV's NSS unit conducts a transformative camp in Sanambatla, focusing on sanitation, health, and skill development for villagers.
content:
Sri Padmavati Mahila Viswa Vidyalayam (SPMVV), through its National Service Scheme (NSS Unit 17), conducted a special camp aimed at ensuring the overall transformation of Sanambatla village in Chandragiri mandal.
The week-long camp that concluded on Sunday (December 14, 2025) focussed on ‘Swachh Andhra – Swarna Andhra’, ensuring garbage clearance and created awareness on the hazards of open defecation, plastic use and keeping the water bodies clean.
The camp in collaboration with the Postal Department also conducted a special drive on Aadhaar enrolment, updation and KYC verification etc. “Besides, the numerous schemes like postal life insurance and other savings schemes were explained to the villagers to promote thrift,” said NSS programme officer S. Santhi Sree.
Similarly, a medical camp was conducted under the aegis of Government Maternity Hospital, Tirupati, led by its Medical Officer Dr. T. Srinivasulu, where medicines for seasonal flu and allied ailments were distributed to the villagers.
As part of skill development, the women were trained in block printing, painting on pots and saris. “This will surely help us make money during our free time,” said resident A. Swetha.

title: Peddapalli MP alleges bias by Centre, urges establishment of semiconductor facility
summary: Peddapalli MP Gaddam Vamsi Krishna accuses the Centre of bias, urging a semiconductor facility in Telangana instead of Andhra Pradesh.
content:
Congress MP from Peddapalli, Gaddam Vamsi Krishna, met Union Minister for Railways, Electronics and IT Ashwini Vaishnaw in New Delhi on Monday, demanding the establishment of a semiconductor manufacturing unit in the Peddapalli-Mancherial region of Telangana.
Finding fault with the Centre’s decision to set to up a semiconductor manufacturing facility — Advanced System in Package Technologies Private Limited (ASIP) — in the neighbouring Andhra Pradesh, he said, “Instead of prioritising merit and regional capability, the Union government chose politics over progress by shifting the semiconductor project to Andhra Pradesh.”
He submitted a detailed representation highlighting the region’s strategic advantages. He pointed out that the region offers ample water resources from the Godavari, robust industrial infrastructure with units like RFCL, SCCL and NTPC, and a skilled workforce capable of supporting high-tech projects.
The MP argued that setting up the unit in Peddapalli-Mancherial would generate large-scale employment, curb unemployment in the region, and enable skilled youth to contribute to national growth.
Telangana leaders, including Ministers, however, also accused the Centre of discrimination, claiming the State had offered land, subsidies and investor commitments, only to see the project diverted to Andhra Pradesh, which reportedly had no land allocated for it at the time. Vamsi also cited past instances, such as Micron’s relocation to Gujarat, as evidence of a pattern of bias against Telangana.

title: Governor hails progress of PJTAU in past one year
summary: Governor Jishnu Dev Varma pats administration of Prof. Jayashankar Telangana Agricultural University (PJTAU) for making good progress on the academic, research and extension fronts this year.
content:
HYDERABAD
Governor Jishnu Dev Varma appreciated the administration of Prof. Jayashankar Telangana Agricultural University (PJTAU) for making good progress on the academic, research and extension fronts during 2025.
He unveiled the progress report of the university presented to him by Vice-Chancellor Aldas Janaiah at Lok Bhavan here on Monday. Registrar of the university G.E.Ch. Vidyasagar and Controller of Examinations M. Malla Reddy were also present.
The Governor hailed the university administration for allocating 15% seats in various courses to the children of farm workers. He complimented the authorities for improving the National Institute of Ranking Framework rank of the university from 37 to 24 in one year and wished further improvement in standards.
On the plea of university authorities to allow convocation for the last three pass-out batches in 2026, the Governor assured to finalise the dates soon. Mr. Janaiah said about 2,800 UG, PG and Ph.D degree holders would attend the convocation likely to be held in February.

title: PRSI, Hyderabad Chapter bags ‘PRSI Best Chapter Award -2025’
summary: PRSI Hyderabad Chapter wins ‘Best Chapter Award - 2025’ at the All India Public Relations Conference in Dehradun.
content: PRSI, Hyderabad Chapter bagged the ‘PRSI Best Chapter Award -2025’ during the valedictory ceremony of 47th All India Public Relations Conference held at Dehradun, Uttarakhand from December 13-15. Uttarakhand Minister of Parliamentary affairs and Forest Subodh Uniyal handed over the award to chairman, PRSI, Hyd chapter Yadgiri Kambhambati, secretary K. Rajesh and others. About 300 plus delegates from around 25 chapters of PRSI representing various States took part in the three-day conference which was inaugurated by Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, said a press release on Monday.

title: Tributes paid to Amarajeevi Potti Sriramulu
summary: Police officers honor Amarajeevi Potti Sriramulu on his 73rd death anniversary for his sacrifice in forming Andhra Pradesh.
content:
Police officers of different cadres paid tributes to Potti Sriramulu on his 73th death anniversary, on Monday. Revered as ‘Amarajeevi’,  Potti Sriramulu sacrificed his life for the formation of Andhra Pradesh.
Director General of Police (DGP) Harish Kumar Gupta paid homage to Amarajeevi Potti Sriramulu at the A.P. police headquarters at Mangalagiri. Meanwhiile, NTR Police Commissioner S.V. Rajasekhar Babu garlanded the portrait of Potti Sriramulu at the Commissionerate, and recalled the sacrifice made by the leader.
In Eluru district, Superintendent of Police (SP) K. Pratap Kishore offered tributes to the freedom fighter at the district police headquarters. Speaking on the occasion, the SP said the State achieved separate Statehood after Potti Sriramulu sacrificed his life observing fast unto death for 58 days.
Eluru District Additional SP (Armed Reserve) G. Muniraju and other officers were also present during the occasion.

title: Tirupati makes helmet compulsory for motorcyclists
summary: Tirupati enforces mandatory helmets for motorcyclists with a 'No Helmet – No Petrol' rule to enhance road safety.
content:
The Tirupati district police made helmets compulsory for motorcyclists starting Monday (December 15, 2025). After conducting awareness drives, sloganeering, and issuing warnings for a week, the rule came into force, with 700 policemen—wearing helmets—taking out a motorcycle rally.
After flagging off the event, District Collector S. Venkateswar rode pillion with Superintendent of Police L. Subbarayudu, who led the motorcycle rally, with both officials wearing helmets.
The Collector described the rule as essential, citing the tragic number of road deaths among people aged 18–35 and the need to ensure that young people follow safety norms. “Do not wear helmet with the fear of getting caught, but with the responsibility towards your family,” he advised the motorcyclists.
The implementation of the ‘No Helmet – No Petrol’ rule will ensure that fuel stations provide petrol only to motorcyclists who are wearing a helmet. “This tightens the law further and makes our enforcement easy,” said Mr. Subbarayudu.
Meanwhile, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu appreciated the drive and lauded the district police. Taking to ‘X’, Mr. Naidu in a post lauded the ‘No helmet – No petrol’ rule as having the capability to ensure compliance.
The law came into force simultaneously in all police sub-divisions of the district. In Sri City, the police, along with Sri City’s in-house security force, announced the implementation of the ‘No Helmet – No entry into Sri City’ rule to ensure better adherence to the culture of ‘responsible and secure commuting’.
Circle Inspector Srinivas and Sri City’s security chief Y. Ramesh appealed to riders to wear helmets as a crucial safeguard.

title: BJP says rural support rising as sarpanch wins cross 600 in Telangana
summary: BJP claims rising rural support in Telangana with over 600 sarpanch victories, boosting confidence for future local elections.
content:
The Telangana BJP has expressed confidence that it will significantly increase its strength in the villages, having already secured more than 600 sarpanch posts, up from 163 earlier, in the ongoing local body elections on Monday.
BJP State president N. Ramchander Rao told party leaders and cadre gathered at the State office on the occasion of Sardar Patel’s  death anniversary that while the Congress and BRS are boasting about their victories, some of which were allegedly achieved through intimidation, people have genuinely supported the BJP.
“We are confident of winning many more seats in the third phase. We believe our tally in rural areas will increase by more than 300 seats. More than 45,000 ward members have already won on behalf of the party,” he claimed. Mr. Rao expressed gratitude to rural voters for placing their trust in the BJP and electing its ward members and sarpanches.
He also congratulated the Adilabad, Nirmal and Karimnagar district BJP presidents and their respective MLAs for the party’s performance. Winning a significant number of sarpanch positions, he said, reflects the growing public support for the party’s leadership, its commitment to grassroots development and its dedication to public service.
Turning to Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy’s speech in Delhi during the Congress protest, Mr. Rao questioned why the Chief Minister was showing concern about alleged infiltrators from Pakistan and Bangladesh.
“Whose votes will be lost? Certainly not those of Indian citizens. Why this compassion for infiltrators from Pakistan and Bangladesh? Nowhere in the Constitution is there a provision allowing non-Indian citizens to have their names on the voters list. Only genuine Indian citizens must appear on the voter list, and eligible voters names will never be removed,” maintained the former MLC.
He accused the Congress, having lost the recent elections, of now trying to provoke people using caste, religion and regional sentiments. He asserted that the Constitution is safe only under a BJP government. “It is ironic that the Congress is preaching about constitutional values after violating and disrespecting the Constitution and weakening the institutions,” said the BJP leader.
The Congress is now left with only one or two States, and the day is not far when the people of India will completely reject the party, he added.  Earlier, Mr. Rao, general secretary Goutham Rao, former MLAs Ch. Ramachandra Reddy and N.V.S.S. Prabhakar, chief spokesperson N.V. Subhash, and others paid tributes to Sardar Patel for ensuring the integration of the country, including Telangana. They accused the Congress of having ‘completely forgotten’ such a towering national leader.

title: Willing to quit party if Anbumani and Ramadoss resolve differences: G.K. Mani
summary: G.K. Mani expresses willingness to leave PMK if Anbumani and Ramadoss reconcile, denying accusations of disloyalty.
content:
Former PMK president G.K. Mani on Monday said he is willing to quit the party if PMK leader Anbumani and his estranged father and PMK founder S. Ramadoss resolve their differences.
Addressing journalists in Chennai, Mr. Mani said it was unfair to label him a traitor and he has never thought or has been disloyal to Dr. Anbumani.
“Many, including myself, convinced Dr. Ramadoss that Dr. Anbumani should become a Union Minister when he was just 35. He (party founder) was very angry with me and said he would stay true to his promise (of not allowing his family members and himself to assume any governmental posts),” he said, adding that he prevailed upon Dr. Ramadoss.
Mr. Mani further said he was also instrumental in Dr. Anbumani becoming a Rajya Sabha member thereafter. “I am really sad and disappointed at the accusations thrown against me. In fact, whenever I tell Dr. Ramadoss to be patient with Dr. Anbumani...he has been extremely dismissive of what I have said...stating I should ask Dr. Anbumani to co-operate with everyone,” he said.

title: Railway officials address pensioners’ grievances at All India Pension Adalat 2025
summary: Railway officials resolve pensioners' grievances at Mysuru's All India Pension Adalat, ensuring timely redressal of concerns.
content:
Railway officials addressed grievances of railway pensioners during the All India Pension Adalat 2025 of the Mysuru Division of South Western Railway held in Mysuru on December 15.
According to a press statement here, the adalat was chaired by Mudit Mittal, Divisional Railway Manager, Mysuru, at his office in the city.
“A total of 47 pensioners attended the adalat. A total of 32 cases were taken up for discussion and two new cases were represented. Of these, 16 cases were disposed off on the spot while the remaining cases are under examination and will be redressed at the earliest,” read a statement from the Railway.
The adalat was also attended by senior Railway officials including Vishnu Gouda, Harshavardhana, and Pruthvi S. Hullati.
Parthasarathy, president of Railway Pensioners’ Welfare Association, Mysuru, expressed satisfaction over the expeditious manner in which the pensioners’ grievances were addressed and resolved. G.S. Swaminathan, the association’s general secretary, was also present.
Mr. Mittal has assured that all pending grievances will be resolved at the earliest.

title: YSRCP holds rally in Parvatipuram over privatisation of medical colleges in State
summary: YSRCP rallies in Parvatipuram against medical college privatization, highlighting its negative impact on marginalized students' access to education.
content:
YSR Congress Party’s Parvatipuram-Manyam district president Sathrucharla Parikshit Raju said that the privatisation of the 18 newly constructed medical colleges in Andhra Pradesh would adversly affect the students from Backward Classes, Scheduled Castes, and tribal communities, as their parents would not be able to afford medical education if the colleges were handed over to private managements.
Mr. Raju along with former deputy chief minister Pamula Pushpa Srivani, former Parvatipuram MLA Alajangi Jogarao and other leaders, took part in a protest rally in Parvatipuram on Monday opposing the privatisation of medical colleges in the State.
Speaking at the rally, he said that the ‘one crore signature’ campaign launched by the YSRCP has received good response from the people as they understand the importance of government run medical colleges,  which would have superspecialty hospitals in near future.
Ms. Srivani and Mr. Jogarao said that privatisation would reduce convener quota seats, while the payment seats under the B and C category would increase, making medical education more expensive for poor and middle-class families.  Despite restrictions imposed by the police department, the party held massive agitations in Vizianagaram and Srikakulam districts.

title: Ricky Kej to inaugurate Mysuru Yoga Utsava-2025
summary: Join Mysuru Yoga Utsava 2025, inaugurated by Ricky Kej, celebrating global yoga heritage from December 18 to 21.
content:
Mysuru, one of the country’s major yoga hubs, will host Mysuru Yoga Utsava 2025 from December 18 to 21, celebrating the city’s rich yoga heritage. This will be the third edition of the Yoga Utsava, which has been organised with the theme ‘Tapas’ and aims to bring the global yoga community onto a common platform.
Renowned music composer and Grammy award winner Ricky Kej will inaugurate the Utsava at the Jagannatha Centre for Art & Culture here on December 18 at 11 a.m. Industrialist M. Jagannath Shenoy will attend the event as the chief guest, while S. Sridharan, vice-president of the Indian Yoga Association, along with other dignitaries, will participate.
The valedictory ceremony will be attended by Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, Mysuru MP, on December 21.
Yoga exponents from over 30 countries are expected to participate in the Utsava. About 500 yoga enthusiasts will perform yoga under the guidance of experienced gurus.
The four-day festival will feature yoga demonstrations and practice sessions, lectures by eminent yoga gurus and scholars, nearly 50 yoga instructors and experts leading various sessions, and more than 40 special programmes and workshops, a press release read.

title: APCRDA allocates 282 returnable plots to Amaravati LPS farmers
summary: APCRDA allocates 282 returnable plots to Amaravati farmers via e-lottery, benefiting 177 landowners with residential and commercial options.
content:
The Andhra Pradesh Capital Region Development Authority (APCRDA) on Monday allotted 282 returnable plots to farmers of the capital region through an e-lottery system at its headquarters in Rayapudi, Amaravati.
The allotment was made to farmers from villages including Krishnayapalem, Nowlur, Kuragallu, Velagapudi, Mandadam, Nidamarru, Penumaka, Thulluru, Nekkallu, Ananthavaram, Rayapudi, Venkatapalem, Dondapadu, Ainavolu, Lingayapalem, Uddandarayunipalem and Malkapuram, who had contributed land for the development of capital Amaravati.
Of the 282 plots allotted, 167 are residential and 115 commercial, benefiting a total of 177 farmers and landowners. The allocation was carried out through an online random system after conducting a trial run in the presence of farmers to ensure transparency.
APCRDA Additional Commissioner A. Bhargava Teja distributed provisional certificates to the beneficiaries.
Special Grade Deputy Collector and Director (Lands – Capital City) N.S.V.B. Vasantharayudu said GIS staff and village surveyors have been deployed to explain the exact geographical location of the allotted plots to farmers.
He urged beneficiaries to complete the registration process at the earliest, clarifying that no registration fee would be charged.

title: Farmers’ body opposes free trade agreement with U.S. in farm sector
summary: Farmers in Mysuru protest against the proposed US free trade agreement, citing concerns over agricultural impacts and local livelihoods.
content:
Activists of Karnataka Rajya Raita Sangha and Green Brigade held a demonstration outside the office of Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, Mysuru MP, in the city on December 15. They voiced their opposition to the Government of India’s proposed move to enter a free trade deal with the United States in the farm sector.
The activists, belonging to the ‘Collective Leadership’ faction of the farmers’ body,  gathered in front of the MP’s office on the Command Area Development Authority premises holding green flags and placards while shouting slogans against any possible free trade deal with the U.S.
In a memorandum addressed to Mr. Yaduveer, the body pointed to the distress among farmers across the country owing to various reasons, including the lack of remunerative prices for their crops, impact of climate aberrations, rising cost of cultivation, and domination of the middlemen in the markets, all of which have led to the farmers finding themselves trapped in the vicious cycle of loans from banks and private finance companies.
The memorandum, signed by Chukki Nanjundaswamy, Honnur Prakash, and Manju Kiran, among others, also cites data from the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) about the high number of suicides among farmers in the country, including Karnataka.
Expressing concern over reports suggesting that the Government of India is preparing to enter into an agreement with the U.S. to allow the import of agricultural products like maize, rice, cotton, soybean, pulses, besides diary products and chicken on a “duty free” or “very low duty” basis, the farmers’ body claimed that the prices of maize had fallen in the country merely owing to the circulation of such news.
Claiming that pulses were also heading in the same direction, the Collective Leadership faction  said it would be difficult to imagine the extent of damage caused to farmers’ interests if western countries begin flooding Indian markets with farm products which are produced abundantly in their countries at very low prices.
The farmers’ body claimed that the Union government was yielding to U.S. pressure to allow duty-free or low-duty imports of its dairy products, maize, rice, cotton, soybeans, and other grains as American farmers were under pressure.
It further stated that the agriculture sector provides employment to about 46% of the population in India, while the figure was only about 10.4% in the U.S.
“Entering such ill-conceived and logic-defying free trade agreements related to agriculture would completely destroy not only the agriculture sector, but also the employment sector and the overall economy of the country,” warned the farmers’ body.
In their memorandum, the farmers’ body expressed to Mr. Yaduveer: “As a public representative of our constituency, we urge you to raise your voice in the Parliament about the grave harm that a free trade agreement would cause to the farming community and firmly assert that the Government of India should not sign a free trade agreement with the United States in the farm sector.”

title: Writer M. Raghavan passes away in Mahe
summary: He was born in Mahe in 1930
content:
Writer M. Raghavan passed away at Mahe early morning on Monday. Mr. Raghavan is known for his short stories ‘Nanavu’, ‘Vadhu’, ‘September Akaleyalla’ and‘Iniyumethra Kaatham’; and novels‘Nankis’,‘Avan’,‘Yathra Parayathe’and‘Chithariya Chithrangal’. He has also penned a few plays such asKarkkidakam andChathurangam. He has translated the playDoraby French feminist writer Helen Cixous to Malayalam under the titleDorayude Katha. He is the elder brother of writer M. Mukundan.
Born in Mahe in 1930, Mr. Raghavan worked in the French consulate in Mumbai and the French Embassy in Delhi. He retired as the Secretary of Cultural Affairs from the embassy in 1983.
He was awarded the Malayala Ratnam award by the Puducherry government for his contributions to Malayalam literature and language. He also received the Vaikom Mohammed Basheer award from the State Institute of Languages in 2008 and the Abu Dhabi Shakti award.

title: P.V. Anvar’s candidates  fail to make any impact in local body polls in Malappuram
summary: P.V. Anvar’s candidates fail to secure seats in Malappuram local body polls, marking a disappointing electoral impact for AITC.
content:
All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) State convener P.V. Anvar has failed to make any electoral impact in the local body polls in the eastern part of Malappuram district. None of the dozen-odd candidates he fielded in the Nilambur municipality and neighbouring panchayats as Independents succeeded in securing seats.
Although Mr. Anvar extended unsolicited support to the United Democratic Front (UDF) in some areas and fielded Independent candidates in others, neither strategy had any positive impact.
The Left Democratic Front (LDF) captured the Thannikkadavu and Narokkavu wards of the Vazhikkadavu panchayat despite Mr. Anvar having declared support for the UDF there.
Mr. Anvar had secured his highest vote share from the Thannikkadavu ward in the Nilambur Assembly byelection held in June 2025. Traditionally UDF strongholds, Thannikkadavu and Narokkavu shifted away from the front for the first time despite Mr. Anvar’s backing.
None of the eight Independent candidates fielded by Mr. Anvar in the Nilambur, Karulai and Moothedam civic bodies secured even a second-place finish. In a particularly stark outcome, Shajahan Pathipara, an Independent candidate for whom Mr. Anvar campaigned in the Mummulli ward of the Nilambur municipality, polled just seven votes.
Although Mr. Anvar had earlier declared that the Trinamool Congress was in the fray, he made a U-turn after the elections, claiming that the party had not contested the civic polls at all and that he had merely extended support to the UDF. However, no UDF leader acknowledged receiving such support from the Trinamool Congress.
Expressing satisfaction with the election outcome, Mr. Anvar described it as a setback for the policies pursued by Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan and CPI(M) State secretary M.V. Govindan.
“The government led by Mr. Vijayan has lost its moral mandate. But one cannot expect any moral or political rectitude from a leader like him, who is challenging the people of Kerala,” said Mr. Anvar. “Even the BJP is talking about developing Kerala, yet Mr. Vijayan and Mr. Govindan continue to dwell on communal rhetoric.”
He said the LDF’s debacle would be repeated in the upcoming Assembly elections too. The UDF would  sweep all 16 seats in Malappuram, he said.

title: Govt. approves construction of ₹61-crore resort in Bapatla district
summary: Andhra Pradesh government approves ₹61-crore resort in Bapatla, promising 250 jobs and significant incentives for development.
content:
The Andhra Pradesh government approved a package of incentives for M/s Yaganti Estates to develop a resort at Pandurangapuram in Adavi village in Bapatla district, under the Andhra Pradesh Tourism Policy 2024-2029.
According to G.O.Ms. No.48 issued on December 13 by Tourism and Culture Department Special Chief Secretary Ajay Jain, the proposed Radisson resort will involve an investment of ₹61.32 crore and is expected to generate employment to 250 people. The project was cleared following recommendations of the State Investment Promotion Committee and the State Investment Promotion Board (SIPB).
As part of the incentives, the government has approved reimbursement of 100% net State Goods and Services Tax for a period of 10 years or until recovery of 100% of the fixed capital investment, whichever is earlier. In addition, the developer will receive an incentive equal to 10% of the fixed capital investment, capped at ₹10 crore, to be disbursed in five equal annual instalments from the commencement of operations.
The project will also be eligible for electricity at industrial tariffs and reimbursement of electricity duty for five years. While reimbursement of stamp duty paid earlier will not be considered, 100% reimbursement of stamp duty on mortgage and hypothecation has been allowed accordingly.

title: President Droupadi Murmu to sojourn in Hyderabad from December 17 to 20
summary: President Droupadi Murmu visits Hyderabad from December 17-20 for official events during her winter sojourn at Rashtrapati Nilayam.
content:
President Droupadi Murmu will be in Hyderabad from December 17 to 20 as part of her winter sojourn at the Rashtrapati Nilayam in Bolarum. According to a media release from the President’s Secretariat, President Murmu will arrive at the Rashtrapati Nilayam on December 17 after concluding her visit to Tamil Nadu.
During her stay, the President will inaugurate the National Conference for the Chairpersons of Public Service Commissions on December 19. The conference is being organised by the Telangana Public Service Commission (TGPSC) in Hyderabad and will bring together heads of public service commissions from across the country.
On December 20, the President will address a conference titled ‘Timeless Wisdom of Bharat: Pathways of Peace and Progress’, being organised by Brahma Kumaris Shanti Sarovar in Hyderabad to mark its 21st anniversary.

title: AIDSO stages protest in Belagavi against merger of rural schools
summary: AIDSO protests in Belagavi against rural school mergers, warning that 40,000 schools may face closure amid government plans.
content:
AIDSO members took out a protest rally in Belagavi on Monday, against the State government’s plans to start magnet Karnataka Public Schools, saying that the government is closing rural schools in the name of merger.
Protestors gathered at Dharwad Naka on the Pune-Bengaluru National Highway near the Suvarna Soudha.
They raised slogans against the State government and expressed the fear that nearly 40,000 government schools in rural areas faced closure in this exercise.
AIDSO State vice-president Abhaya Diwakar said that Primary and Secondary Education Minister Madhu Bangarappa has been repeatedly making false claims about the scheme.
“The Minister has said that no government school will be closed. But this is far from truth. Already, Education Department officials are closing down rural schools in Yadgir, Channapatna, Chitradurga, Chikkaballapur and other districts. An estimated 2,000 schools are likely to be closed in Belagavi district. This is condemnable,’’ she said.
Meanwhile, Subhash Bettadakoppa of AIDSO said that the State government is welcome to start Karnataka Public Schools as an alternative model and not by merging rural schools.
The State government is not worried about reducing the intake in government schools , issues like teacher vacancies, missing infrastructure and low quality of education in public schools, he said.
Studies have indicated that most of the dropouts are from deprived communities, particularly girls from backward and minority communities.
The State government has claimed that the main attraction of Karnataka Public Schools is the English-medium instruction. However, it has not made proper preparations to train teachers in English-medium instruction. The State government has not shown enthusiasm in filling the over 60,000 vacancies in government schools, he said.
Leaders Rajashekar S., Mahantesh Bilur, Arun, Eeranna, Vaibhav and other activists were present.

title: Government committed to make all roads pothole-free by January end, says Minister
summary: Minister B.C. Janardhan Reddy pledges to make all Andhra Pradesh roads pothole-free by January, prioritizing quality and safety.
content:
Minister for Roads and Buildings, and In-charge Minister for Annamayya district, B.C. Janardhan Reddy on Monday (December 15, 2025) directed the officials to complete all road projects on a fast-track basis without compromising on quality.
The Minister held a review meeting with senior R&B officials in Madanapalle. He said that the coalition government was committed to making all roads in the State pothole-free by the end of January.
The Minister said around 27,000 km of roads across Andhra Pradesh had suffered severe damage and that works worth nearly ₹3,000 crore were being undertaken for pothole-free roads, maintenance, and development of C-category roads. “Additional tenders worth ₹200 crore will be floated shortly to further strengthen road infrastructure on the high traffic roads in the State,” Reddy said.
The Minister alleged that routine road renewals were grossly neglected during the previous YSR Congress Party government, and said that the present administration had cleared several pending bills left unpaid earlier. He observed that recent heavy rains had damaged repaired stretches, making fresh maintenance inevitable. “Priority is given to roads with high vehicular movement to ensure safety and smooth connectivity,” he said.
The Minister said, despite financial stringency, the government has allocated ₹123 crore for road development in Annamayya district alone. The allocation would cover 2,148 km of roads, which were riddled with potholes, while maintenance works was currently underway on 2,721 km of roads across seven Assembly constituencies in the district, and the remaining works would be started shortly. He further directed the officials to prepare estimates for new road proposals.
Referring to the road works in Madanapalle division, the Minister said that ₹18 crore had already been released for the projects, in addition to ₹3 crore funding from the DMF category.
The Minister further announced the release of ₹3 crore for developing Chinna Tippa Samudram (CTM) Road into a double road, for which tenders would be called for shortly. He said that another ₹5 crore had been sanctioned each for Nimmalapalle, Ramasamudram, and Bengaluru roads in the division. “By creating excellent road infrastructure, we want to give a phenomenal boost to investments, industry, and tourism in the Madanapalle region,” he said.

title: Secunderabad man loses ₹75 lakh to online betting fraud
summary: A Secunderabad man lost ₹75 lakh to online betting fraud, prompting a cybercrime police investigation and public advisory against illegal platforms.
content:
A 32-year-old resident of Secunderabad has approached the cybercrime police after losing ₹75 lakh to illegal online betting and casino platforms between 2021 and 2025, police said.
The chain of events began in 2021 when the victim received a WhatsApp message from a number claiming to represent an online betting platform. He was encouraged to play games such as cricket betting, Teen Patti and casino games, and was promised easy profits through a game described as ‘Fivestar Cricket Aviator Flight Game’. After initially depositing ₹10,000 and receiving a small return, he was persuaded to deposit larger sums, the complainant said.
An officer from the cybercrimes wing said the victim transferred ₹10 lakh in multiple transactions to various bank accounts provided by the operators in 2021, eventually losing the entire amount.
“In March 2022, the same persons contacted him again, claiming they were operating on another platform with a lower minimum deposit. Trusting them, the victim resumed playing and, between 2021 and 2025, deposited a total of ₹75 lakh through bank transfers, UPI IDs, QR scanners and cash deposit machines across multiple betting websites. He later realised that withdrawals were blocked and the money was irretrievable,” explained the officer.
Police said the acts amounted to cheating, online fraud and illegal online betting. The victim has sought registration of a case and investigation into the operators behind the platforms.
Issuing a public advisory, the cybercrime police cautioned people against illegal online betting and casino websites and apps that promise assured or easy returns. They said fraudsters typically approach victims through messaging platforms or social media, show small initial profits to gain confidence, and later induce large deposits through multiple payment methods. “These platforms are unregulated and illegal, and participation can also attract legal consequences,” warned the officer.

title: Woman critically injured after falling from hotel balcony during party intercepted by police in Bengaluru
summary: A woman critically injured after falling from a hotel balcony during a police-intercepted party in Bengaluru; investigation ongoing.
content:
A 21-year-old woman suffered severe injuries after falling from the balcony of a fourth-floor room at a hotel in east Bengaluru’s HAL area on Sunday morning, when the police intercepted a late-night party. The injured woman is a private company employee from Kundalahalli.
Meanwhile, amid growing allegations of corruption in the Bengaluru police department, friends of the injured woman, who spoke to presspersons on Monday, have alleged that the police demanded a bribe of ₹8,000 from them after intercepting the party. However, the police have refuted the claims.
Vaishnavi and seven of her friends checked into the hotel, located in AECS Layout in HAL, around 1.30 a.m. on Sunday. They had booked three rooms for a weekend party and gathered in one room after dinner.
According to the police, the woman’s friends were playing loud music through the night until morning, prompting a neighbour to call the police helpline. “A neighbour called 112 around 5.15 a.m., complaining about loud music being played from the room. Our patrolling officers went to the room, recorded the scene as they were partying early in the morning, and asked them to disperse,” a police officer from the HAL police station toldThe Hindu.
The officer noted that the patrolmen had brought three of the woman’s friends to the common area to book a petty case when the alleged fall occurred.
K. Parushurama, Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP), Whitefield, toldThe Hinduthat they suspect the woman may have panicked on seeing the police and attempted to climb down from the balcony, leading to the incident.
“I interacted with the woman’s friends, but they did not mention any bribe demand at that time. We also checked the body camera footage worn by our officer, and it does not corroborate the claims. However, we will investigate the matter further,” Mr. Parushurama said.
However, no complaint regarding bribery has been filed by the woman’s friends. Instead, the father of the injured woman has lodged a police complaint against the hotel where she and her friends had checked in, alleging that the authorities failed to ensure adequate safety measures. He cited the absence of adequate safety grill coverage on the balcony, the police said.
An investigator toldThe Hinduthat the hotel had been operational for only three months and lacked several clearances. The police have registered a negligence case against the hotel and are continuing their investigation.

title: RJD slams Nitish after video shows CM removing woman’s hijab
summary: RJD criticizes Nitish Kumar after video surfaces of him pulling down a woman's hijab, questioning his mental state and political alignment.
content:
The Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) slammed Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar after a video emerged in which he is seen pulling down the hijab of a Muslim woman at a government function. The video was posted by the RJD onX,in which the party called Mr. Kumar a “sanghi”.
The video, shot at the function where Mr. Kumar was distributing appointment letters to AYUSH doctors, showed Mr. Kumar pointing towards the woman’s head scarf and then suddenly pulling it down.
