Minister of State for Home Nityanand Rai said in a written reply that 9.2 km of the total 1,643-km border with Myanmar had been fenced so far.
The reply stated that from 2014 to 2025 (till November 30), the number of infiltrators arrested along the Myanmar border stood at 45, 32, 20, 15, 39, 57, 58, 73, 173, 212, 441 and 437 respectively.
Parliament Winter Session:Follow highlights from December 16, 2025
In February 2024, months after the 2023 ethnic violence in Manipur, Home Minister Amit Shah announced that the entire Myanmar border will be fenced and the Free Movement Regime (FMR) along the north-eastern border will be scrapped. However, FMR, which allows cross-border movement of people to a certain distance without visas and passports, continued but was regulated. In December 2024, a new framework was implemented, under which the territorial limits of FMR was reduced from 16 km to 10 km. As many as 43 designated exit and entry gates were operationalised to regulate the movement of people and biometrics and gate passes were introduced.
The reply also added that in 2024 and 2025, the number of infiltrators who were arrested along the Bangladesh border stood at 2,525 and 2,556 respectively. Between the years 2014 and 2023, the number of such arrests stood at 2,160, 2,809, 1,601, 907, 884, 1,109, 955, 1,208, 2,076, and 2,617 respectively.
The reply added that 93.25% of the India-Pakistan border – which is 2,289.66-km-long – has been physically fenced. The remaining 154.524 km, i.e. 6.75% of the border, is unfenced. It added that of the 4,096.70-km India-Bangladesh border, 3,239.92 km – 79.08% – has been physically fenced. The remaining 856.778 km, i.e. 20.92% of the border, is unfenced.

title: A decade after division, Telangana emerges as an economic powerhouse of India
summary: Telangana transforms into India's economic powerhouse, showcasing remarkable growth in GDP, exports, and living standards over the past decade.
content:
Telangana’s upward march to an economic powerhouse has not stalled despite the Covid-19 pandemic shock, a high debt burden, and vagaries of weather; the RBI’s Handbook on Statistics of Indian States-2025 shows.
The Gross State Domestic Product has surged from 5,05,84,879 in 2014-15 to 16,40,90,143 in 2024-25 a 224.38% growth in Telangana. In comparison, Kerala, which had a similar base figure in 2014-15 saw 143% growth in GSDP.
The Per Capita Net State Domestic Product (NSDP) has similarly rocketed from ₹124,104 in 2014-15 to ₹3,87,623 in 2024-25 a growth of 212%. In the same period, Karnataka, which had a similar NSDP, saw a growth of 104.9% from ₹1,85,840 to ₹3,80,906. Telangana’s PCNSDP is the second highest in the country after Delhi.
The PCNSDP is the average economic output per person in a State, dividing the State’s total Net State Domestic Product (NSDP) by its population. It offers an insight into the average income of the citizens in a State and their living standards.
This growth has been bolstered on two fronts. The State’s inflation has been dropped below the national average for the first time in five years. In 2024-25, the inflation in the State was 3.7% while the national average is 4.6% thus making the personal money go a little further. The State has also seen its exports surge three times from $6,572 million in 2017-18 to $19,123 million. The rise in exports is linked to sharp uptick in services sector which logged 138% in Gross State Value Added between 2017-18 and 2024-25.
In the agriculture sector, foodgrain production has quadrupled over the past few years from 5,129 thousand tonnes in 2015-16 to 21,634.4 thousand tonnes in 2024-25. In comparison, A.P.’s grain production has remained stable in the same period from 10,633.7 to 11,722 thousand tonnes. However, this happened at a time when the factories sector reached a stagnation point. The number of factories in Telangana were 14,110 in 2013-14 and peaked at 15,342 in the pre-pandemic year of 20-21 and has dropped down to 13,446 in 23-24. These numbers are matched with the number of employees in the sector that has remained near stationary with 1,13,922 in 2013-14 to 1,35,338 in 2023-24.
Another key index showing a changing lifestyle is access to energy. Telangana’s per capita availability of power is now among the highest in the country among the larger States at 2,306.1 kilowatt-hour, just behind Punjab at 2,503.4 kWh.

title: Vast opportunities for content writing in digital era, says VSU V-C
summary: VSU Vice-Chancellor highlights vast opportunities for content writers in the digital era during a special course launch.
content:
Vikrama Simhapuri University (VSU) Vice-Chancellor Allam Srinivasa Rao said that the advent of the digital era augurs well for content writers as they will have vast and diverse opportunities.
He was speaking after launching the 12-day special certificate course offered by English department titled ‘Creating writing and professional content development’, here on Tuesday.
“The course is designed to enhance the students’ skills. Hence they are advised not to confine to textbooks, but sharpen their creative abilities through such skill-oriented programmes,” Mr. Srinivasa Rao said.
In his keynote address, international poet and SAARC Literature Award recipient Perugu Ramakrishna said there was no need to fear artificial intelligence (AI). “Our future lies in working alongside it. Human emotions such as a mother’s love, tears and solitude can never be fully replicated by machines,” he said, adding that human creativity would always remain supreme.
Registrar K. Suneetha called the course highly beneficial for learning various writing styles such as academic writing, media content, and for digital platforms.
The course covers content development, editing and blog writing and professional writing tools.

title: Enhanced TOEFL iBT test from January 21
summary: Educational Testing Service hosts a TOEFL Experience Day in Hyderabad, giving students and educators a first look at the enhanced TOEFL iBT test, which is set for launch on January 21.
content:
Educational Testing Service (ETS), the leader in educational assessment and creator of the TOEFL iBT test, on Tuesday hosted a TOEFL experience day event here, offering a preview of the enhanced TOEFL iBT test to be launched on January 21.
The event witnessed experts, advisers and partners explaining the changes, and offered participants an immersive deep dive into the upcoming changes. The focused sessions included the upcoming test enhancements, the educational and fairness principles behind each section, and how the redesigned test better supports today’s learners in a competitive global admissions landscape.
The new format is shorter, spans approximately two hours, features an adaptive testing experience for Reading & Listening sessions, a new 1-6 scoring scale, scores available within 72 hours, and AI-enhanced identity verification for easy check-in, among others.
ETS India currently operates two active test centres in Hyderabad including the Prometric facility. The centres cater to the city’s growing test-taker base. However, considering Hyderabad’s expanding education and study-abroad landscape, ETS India is planning further network expansion by the end of December 2025, its officials said.
Addressing the press, executive director-Global Partnerships & Sales, Sidnei Rodrigues de Souza explained the new features and said the newer format is being welcomed by educators for its expanded preparation resources.
Global General Manager, TOEFL, ETS, Omar Chihane said Hyderabad is a cornerstone market for ETS in southern India, particularly for study-abroad aspirants. The redesigned TOEFL iBT is designed to deliver a fairer, more intuitive, and tailored experience, he added.
According to ETS data, United States (55%) remains the top destination for students from Andhra Pradesh and Telangana for studying abroad, followed by Canada (16%), United Kingdom (12%) and Australia (10%).
Most TOEFL test takers, it added, were from Hyderabad (48%) and Vijayawada (18%), followed by Visakhapatnam (16%) and Guntur (10%).

title: Kerala High Court issues interim stay on notice issued by ED to KIIFB over masala bond issue
summary: Kerala High Court grants interim stay on ED's notice to KIIFB regarding masala bond fund usage for infrastructure projects.
content:
The Kerala High Court has issued a three-month interim stay on a notice issued by the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) to Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB) on the utilisation of funds raised through masala bonds for the board.
A Bench of Justice V.G. Arun issued the interim stay on further proceedings on the matter, in a plea filed by KIIFB challenging a notice issued against the board by the ED in connection with the usage of funds generated through masala bonds for infra development in the State. The ED had initiated proceedings under the Foreign Exchange Management Act.
The KIIFB had earlier this month approached the High Court seeking to quash the notice. Stating that the ED often issued such notices during election time, the board contended that there was no hassle in spending the funds to purchase land for infra development, and that everything was being done in adherence to Reserve Bank of India norms.
It further said that land acquisition for infra-projects cannot be equated with real estate activity, or land purchase for commercial use. Moreover, ₹90,000 crore worth infra projects that the KIIFB approved have been affected due to the ED action.
The ED opposed the plea of KIIFB, stating that it was not maintainable, since it had only issued notice, seeking explanation on the issue. It contended that the board had to approach the appropriate forum under the Foreign Exchange Management Act on the matter.

title: GBA Chief directs detailed survey for new road to reduce congestion near Bellandur lake
summary: Chief Commissioner of the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) M. Maheshwar Rao directed officials to conduct a detailed survey for the construction of a road within the Bellandur lake buffer zone to ease traffic congestion in the area.
content:
Chief Commissioner of the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) M. Maheshwar Rao directed officials to conduct a detailed survey for the construction of a road within the Bellandur lake buffer zone to ease traffic congestion in the area.
During an inspection of locations in the East and South City Corporation limits on Tuesday, Mr. Rao instructed authorities to assess the feasibility of constructing the road, examining the land parcels in the buffer zone and to submit a comprehensive report. The proposed road, approximately 1 km long and 24 metres wide, will include provisions for public movement and recreational use, and is expected to substantially reduce traffic along the Bellandur lake bund road.
The GBA Chief said that steps have been initiated for the construction of a 1.4 km-long buffer road as an alternative to Wind Tunnel Road. The land for this project belongs to HAL, whose authorities have given consent to the road. Tenders have been invited, and government approval is being sought, with officials instructed to commence work at the earliest.
Mr. Rao also inspected the ongoing construction of the 2.6 km buffer road connecting Ejipura Inner Ring Road to Sarjapur Outer Ring Road.

title: Peddapalli MP rides self-designed electric bike to Parliament, flags Delhi air pollution
summary: Peddapalli MP Gaddam Vamsi Krishna rides a self-designed electric bike to Parliament, highlighting air pollution and eco-friendly transport solutions.
content:
To draw attention to the worsening air pollution in the national capital, Congress MP from Peddapalli Gaddam Vamsi Krishna arrived in Parliament on an electric bike designed and built by him. The gesture was aimed at underscoring the need to adopt eco-friendly modes of transport.
Stating that vehicular emissions are a major contributor to Delhi’s growing air pollution, the MP said wider use of electric vehicles could significantly cut carbon emissions and reduce dependence on fossil fuels. He said public representatives should lead by example and called upon citizens to take an active role in environmental protection.
By riding a self-made electric bike to Parliament, Mr. Vamsi Krishna also highlighted the importance of promoting indigenous technology, innovation and the technical skills of the youth. His initiative has generated discussion among political circles and the public.

title: Commissioner inspects sanitary conditions in Kurnool
summary: Commissioner P. Viswanatha inspects Kurnool's sanitation, addressing negligence and urging prompt action for public health and cleanliness.
content:
Kurnool Municipal Corporation (KMC) Commissioner P. Viswanatha instructed officials to take action against two sanitary secretaries for negligence in discharging their duties.
Mr. Viswanatha visited various residential colonies in Joharapuram area in the city on Tuesday to take stock of the sanitation conditions and supply of water to the locals. He found piled-up garbage and unhygienic conditions at several places and expressed dissatisfaction over the Sanitary Inspector for failing to take proper action.
The Commissioner expressed unhappiness over leakages in drinking water pipelines and said people were facing severe problems due to the negligence of officials. He also questioned them for failing to issue notices to vacant plot owners to clear their premises.
He said that there should not be any laxity in issues concerning public health, cleanliness and supply of safe drinking water and asked officials to identify the problems at the ground level and resolve them.
The Commissioner also visited the Munagalapadu summer storage tank, where 130 acre land was available for development of recreational activities.

title: HPV vaccine training conducted in Hyderabad ahead of planned rollout in early 2026
summary: Hyderabad conducts HPV vaccine training for health officials ahead of the 2026 vaccination rollout to ensure effective implementation.
content:
A training programme on the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine was conducted for programme officers, senior public health officers, medical officers and supervisory staff of Hyderabad district on Tuesday, as part of preparations for the implementation of the HPV vaccination programme. The programme is likely to be implemented in the beginning of 2026, said a senior health official.
Addressing the participants, Hyderabad District Medical and Health Officer J. Venkati said it was essential for medical officers and supervisory staff to have clear awareness and technical understanding of the HPV vaccine to ensure smooth and effective implementation at the field level.
The training covered an overview of Human Papillomavirus and its link to cervical cancer, along with details on the vaccine schedule, eligibility criteria and dosage. Sessions were also held on cold chain management, vaccine safety, adverse events following immunisation surveillance and reporting, and the roles and responsibilities of medical officers and supervisory staff.

title: Singareni to sign MoU with Odisha on setting up 4,900 MW power plants tomorrow
summary: Singareni signs MoU with Odisha for 4,900 MW thermal and green energy projects, enhancing power generation capabilities.
content:
HYDERABAD
The Singareni Collieries Company Ltd (SCCL) will sign a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Industrial Promotion and Investment Corporation of Odisha (IPICOL) here on Thursday (December 18) for setting up 4,900 megawatt capacity thermal and green energy projects in Odisha.
In a statement issued here on Tuesday, the outgoing Chairman and Managing Director of SCCL N. Balram said Singareni would establish a 3×800 MW ultra super critical thermal power project near the Naini coal block in Odisha to generate power using the coal mined there as a captive power plant.
Another 2,500 MW capacity green energy projects planned would comprise 1,000 MW capacity solar power plants and 500 MW each of floating solar power, pumped storage power and wind power plants in Odisha.

title: Special 100-day awareness campaign on RWH pits from next week
summary: Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply & Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) announces 100-day awareness campaign to promote the construction of rainwater harvesting pits in all houses and residential complexes.
content:
The Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply & Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) on Monday announced a special 100-day awareness campaign starting next week to promote the construction of rainwater harvesting (RWH) pits in all houses and residential complexes.
Managing Director K. Ashok Reddy said RWH pits are necessary in houses measuring 200 square yards and is mandatory in houses measuring 300 square yards and above.
Addressing officials and residents in Madhapur on Monday, he said that despite receiving substantial rainfall annually; only a small fraction currently recharges the aquifers. The campaign aims to educate the public about the necessity of capturing rainwater and directing it into the ground through RWH pits.
The Board’s earlier surveys identified thousands of residential complexes without RWH pits. The special campaign will also specifically promote community RWH systems in gated communities and convert unused borewells into injection wells.
Mr. Reddy urged residents to participate actively in the campaign and said widespread adoption of RWH pits could reduce reliance on tanker water supply and future large-scale drinking water schemes, ensuring sustainable water availability for all.

title: Nitish was being fatherly when he pulled hijab off doctor's face: Bihar minister
summary: Bihar Minister Zama Khan defends CM Nitish Kumar’s controversial act of removing a hijab, calling it a fatherly gesture.
content:
Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar had acted in a "fatherly" manner when hepulled the hijab off a young woman's face, Minority Affairs Minister Zama Khan said on Tuesday (December 16, 2025).
The incident, which happened on Monday (December 15) at a function where AYUSH doctors were handed appointment letters, triggered a controversy.
"The CM is, perhaps, older than the father of the woman in question. I have a daughter, and I could sense the fatherly affection he had expressed," Mr. Khan said, when asked about the incident.
More than 1,000 AYUSH doctors were handed appointment letters at the function, and 10 of them, including one, Nusrat Parveen, who was wearing a hijab, received theirs from Mr. Kumar at the Chief Minister's Secretariat.
CM Kumar, who was standing on a raised platform, exclaimed upon seeing Nusrat Parveen, "What is this?" and pulled the veil down, exposing her face.
Mr. Kumar, the longest-serving CM of the State, has been facing flak from political opponents, who have been alleging that his behaviour was proof that he was not mentally sound and, hence, unfit to govern the State.
Mr. Khan hit back at the detractors, pointing out, "Only recently has the NDA secured a landslide victory in Assembly polls under his leadership. Those trying to create a scandal have a very twisted mindset."  	"The CM had simply tried to highlight the fact that girls of the minority community, too, are making progress in Bihar. But the mudslingers are causing embarrassment to the poor girl, too," he alleged.

title: Portraits of Param Vir Chakra awardees replace British ADCs at Rashtrapati Bhavan
summary: Rashtrapati Bhavan now honours Param Vir Chakra awardees, replacing British ADC portraits to celebrate India's rich culture and heritage.
content:
Portraits of all 21 Param Vir Chakra awardees are now on display at Rashtrapati Bhavan, replacing the previously  displayed portraits of 96 BritishAide-de-Camps(ADCs).
The Param Vir Chakra is India’s highest military honour, awarded for displaying the most exceptional acts of valour, courage and self-sacrifice during war.
The initiative aims to honour the memory of soldiers who have laid down their lives in the service of the nation. The President of India, Droupadi Murmu, inaugurated the ‘Param Vir Dirgha’ at Rashtrapati Bhavan on Tuesday, on the occasion of ‘Vijay Diwas’.
“The move will assist in educating visitors about our national heroes who displayed dauntless resolve and unconquerable spirit in defending our nation. The initiative to display portraits of Indian national heroes marks a step toward shedding the colonial mindset and embracing, with pride, the richness of India’s culture, heritage, and timeless traditions,’’ a release issued by the Rashtrapati Bhavan said.
The government had been working to restore pride in India’s “sanatan values”, with prominent changes including the renaming of the Rajpath to Kartavya Path, a senior Central government official said. Similarly, the Indian Navy’s ensign has shed the Saint George’s Cross, adopting instead a design featuring the National Flag and a Navy blue-gold octagon dedicated to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. The 2022 Republic Day Beating the Retreat Ceremony, part of the ‘Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav’, embraced Indian instruments, including the sitar, santoor, and tabla.
Across India, including in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, colonial nomenclature has been replaced, the official said. In 2018, Ross Island was renamed Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Dweep, Neil Island became Shaheed Dweep, and Havelock Island was rechristened Swaraj Dweep. In 2024, the capital of the Union Territory, Port Blair, was renamed Sri Vijaya Puram, and 21 islands were named after Param Vir Chakra awardees.
The Rashtrapati Bhavan’s Mughal Garden was renamed Amrit Udyan, and Race Course Road, home to the Prime Minister’s residence, has become Lok Kalyan Marg.
“Through various initiatives, the Central government is dismantling colonial legacies,’’ the official said.

title: Karnataka Assembly adopts GBA amendment Bill to add members
summary: Karnataka Assembly passes GBA amendment Bill to include elected representatives and ex-officio members, enhancing local governance.
content:
The Legislative Assembly on Tuesday adopted the Greater Bengaluru Governance (Second Amendment) Bill, 2025, that seeks to include members of the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha, the Legislative Assembly, and the Legislative Council as members of the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) if they come under its jurisdiction.
Piloting the Bill, Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said names of some of the elected representatives including Rajya Sabha MP Sudha Murthy and Chickballapur MP K. Sudhakar had been left out from the GBA as its members, though they came under the GBA jurisdiction. The proposed amendment would provide for adding their names.
It is also aimed at including Chief Secretary, Additional Chief Secretary to Urban Development Department, and Additional Chief Secretary/Principal Secretary to Finance Department as ex-officio members of the GBA.
The Bill also provides for inclusion of ACS to Urban Development Department as a member of the Executive Committee of the GBA.
It also provides for re-division of wards in respect to newly incorporated local areas to be carried out within a specified period.
The Deputy Chief Minister agreed to the suggestion by the Opposition members to drop the provision for appointing nominated members to the GBA.
Earlier, BJP member S. Suresh Kumar said: “There are 369 members in the GBA. If the government adds one nominated person for every 20,000 population, there would be another 369 members. This would create confusion.”
The Deputy Chief Minister also endorsed the views of Leader of the Opposition R. Ashok that the trend of Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council members frequently changing their addresses to gain voting rights in different local bodies should be discouraged.

title: India–Maldives military exercise concludes in Thiruvananthapuram
summary: India and Maldives conclude military exercise EKUVERIN, enhancing counter-insurgency and counter-terrorism capabilities through joint training in Thiruvananthapuram.
content:
The bilateral military exercise EKUVERIN between the Indian Army and the Maldives National Defence Forces (MNDF) concluded with a joint validation exercise at Thiruvananthapuram on Tuesday (December 16, 2025), marking the culmination of two weeks of intensive training.
The validation phase was witnessed by Major General R.D. Sharma of the Indian Army and Brigadier General Abdulla Ibrahim from the Maldivian side, along with observer delegations from both countries.
The Indian Army said the exercise focused on counter-insurgency and counter-terrorist operations in contemporary operational environments, with the aim of enhancing interoperability, operational synergy and tactical coordination between the two forces in sub-conventional conflict scenarios.
Key training activities included cordon and search operations, room intervention drills, small team tactics, reflex firing and close-quarter battle techniques aimed at improving precision, speed and effectiveness during counter-terror operations. Special emphasis was laid on amphibious drills, intelligence-led operations, real-time decision-making and joint mission planning under dynamic operational conditions.
Both contingents also rehearsed handling of explosives, demolition techniques and advanced field craft, strengthening their capability to neutralise threats and secure sensitive areas.
The culmination exercise successfully validated all laid-down training objectives. Senior officers from both sides expressed satisfaction with the high level of professionalism and operational proficiency displayed by the participating troops.
Exercise EKUVERIN reaffirmed the shared commitment of India and Maldives to strengthening professional military cooperation and contributing to peace and security in the Indian Ocean Region.

title: Govt. considering multiple options to put Rushikonda buildings to use
summary: Andhra Pradesh government explores options for Rushikonda buildings to benefit the public and boost tourism revenue.
content:
The Andhra Pradesh government is considering multiple options to utilise the lavish buildings constructed atop Rushikonda during the YSRCP term in a manner that would benefit the public, while also generating sustainable revenue for the Tourism Department, Ministers Payyavula Keshav, Kandula Durgesh and D.B.V. Swamy said on Tuesday.
The Ministers were speaking after the second meeting of the sub-committee constituted to examine the future use of the buildings that had been built by the previous dispensation, purportedly for use as official residence of then Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy.
Tourism Special Chief Secretary Ajay Jain, Tourism MD and APTA CEO Amrapali Kata, and senior officials attended the meeting. The committee reviewed the public and stakeholder feedback gathered through the Tourism Department’s website.
Officials informed the Ministers that 1,517 members of the public and 44 stakeholders had shared their views. A majority of them had urged the government to quickly rectify, what they described as mistakes of the previous regime, and ensure the asset was put to public use. Suggestions included converting the “palace” into a hotel or resort, museum, art gallery, wellness centre, MICE facility, science planetarium, or even government offices.
The Ministers criticised the previous government for replacing revenue-generating resorts with a palace-like structure spread over nearly 20,000 square metres, resulting in a monthly maintenance burden of ₹25 lakh to ₹30 lakh. They said institutions such as Tata, IHCL and Atmosphere Core, along with some foreign firms, had offered proposals.
The sub-committee said another meeting would be held soon, after which two or three options would be placed before the Cabinet for a final decision, in consultation with Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu.

title: CPI(M) resorting to violence after election setback: KPCC president
summary: The police have remained mute spectators in many incidents, the KPCC president alleged
content:
Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) president Sunny Joseph, MLA, has accused the CPI(M) of unleashing widespread violence against the public following its defeat in the local body elections. He alleged that several incidents have occurred across the State, proving that the party has not accepted the people’s verdict and continues to act with arrogance.
In a statement, Mr. Joseph said a series of “fascist acts” have been reported, including the vandalism of Mahatma Gandhi statues, bomb attacks on the Indira Gandhi statue, armed assaults on houses using swords and machetes and the intimidation of political opponents. Such actions, he added, were a grave insult to the State’s democratic and secular values.
The Congress leader also expressed strong suspicion that the violence taking place in the home turf of the Chief Minister and the CPI(M) State secretary has the tacit support of the party leadership. The police have remained mute spectators in many incidents, he alleged.
The Gandhi statue near the Ramanthali cultural centre in Payyannur was vandalised. The incident, he claimed, is not the first such incident in Payyannur. In addition, the UDF election committee office in Payyannur municipality was vandalised, and a bomb was hurled at the house of UDF candidate P.K. Suresh.
Following the CPI(M)’s defeat in Panoor municipality, UDF workers were allegedly attacked on a large scale. Congress offices were also attacked in other places, including in Ulikkal in Kannur, Eramala in Vadakara, and Thuruthimukku. Congress workers and even police personnel came under attack in Bedadka in Kasaragod.
He also cautioned that the situation could spiral out of control if immediate action is not taken. He added that the Congress is committed to protecting its workers.

title: MP Chamala seeks RRTC for Hyderabad, flags pending Telangana infra projects before Standing Committee
summary: MP Chamala Kiran Reddy advocates for RRTC in Hyderabad and highlights pending Telangana infrastructure projects to the Standing Committee.
content:
Bhongir Congress MP Chamala Kiran Reddy stressed the need to introduce Regional Rapid Transit Corridors (RRTC) in major cities, including Hyderabad, to improve urban liveability, promote sustainable development and strengthen regional connectivity for nearly eight surrounding districts.
He attended a meeting of the Standing Committee on Housing and Urban Affairs, chaired by Magunta Sreenivasulu Reddy, MP from Ongole, in New Delhi on Tuesday.
He informed the Committee that key infrastructure proposals of the Telangana government — the Regional Ring Road, Regional Ring Rail and Metro Rail Phase-II — were pending with the Government of India. The MP said early approvals and coordinated support from the Centre would be crucial for balanced regional growth and decongestion of Hyderabad.

title: Objections aplenty over GHMC ward de-limitation
summary: Objections aplenty over GHMC ward de-limitation
content:
Objections of all hues about various aspects of ward de-limitation, varying from the process to the purpose, from the manner of the exercise to the result, were raised in the Tuesday’s council meeting at the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC).
A total 152 corporators and ex-officio members attended the meeting presided by Mayor Gadwal Vijayalakshmi.
The freshly released map of 300 proposed wards in the now expanded corporation resembled a hibiscus flower, clustered at the centre and expanding towards the edges. The rationale given by the officials, that population was dense at the core, and sparse towards the newly merged urban local bodies, did not seem to have many takers.
Objections were raised about how Turkayamjal with 70,000 population could be made into a single ward, while Jalpally is divided into three, about Exhibition Grounds with 12,000 population as a ward carved out from Goshamahal, and Narsingi holding more divisions than Manikonda despite having fewer voters, Shamshabad holding two wards while Jalpally has three, Ameenpur with 1.2 lakh population having only two wards and Borabanda being kept as a single ward. Allegations flew about insinuating a tacit understanding between ruling party and the MIM, while the members from the latter said the purpose of the exercise was to damage MIM.
Several anomalies raised by the members pertained to name changes. Kallem Navajeevan Reddy representing Hayatnagar pointed out that Hayat Bakshi Begum mosque after which the area was named, went to the High Court Colony division, as also the Hayatnagar depot. Several corporators questioned Baghlingampally ward being renamed after DD Colony. Corporator Mohammed Rashed Farazuddin raised an issue with Shaikpet village being converted into OU Colony ward.
Corporator Vanga Madhusudan Reddy pointed out that in 2009, de-limitation was done after infusion of each of the merged ULBs with funds to the tune of ₹400 to ₹500 crore, and urged the government to follow the example. V.Sravan Kumar representing Malkajgiri division said the boundaries mentioned in the gazette notification were unfamiliar to majority.
MLC Dasoju Sravan Kumar called the de-limitation exercise “undemocratic and unconstitutional”. He questioned the constitutional sanctity of the Centre for Good Governance which carried out the exercise and asked why the CGG report had not been tabled.
MLA Ahmed bin Abdullah Balala appreciated the fact that members’ opinions were being sought for the first time about de-limitation, and flagged the absence of data as the basis for the exercise.
Former minister and current MLA Talasani Srinivas Yadav alleged huge variation in ward-wise voter numbers, ranging between 18,000 and 70,000. The government has done the exercise in an opaque manner with no consultations with the stakeholders, he said.
Another MLA Ch. Malla Reddy cried foul about 220 wards in erstwhile Medchal constituency being reduced to 16 after merger. Comparing GHMC’s extent with metro cities such as Mumbai and global cities such as Tokyo, MLA K.P. Vivekanand reminded that Mumbai has a total of nine municipal corporations and nagar panchayats, while Tokyo has 23 corporations.
MLA Kaleru Venkatesh pointed out that already several authorities such as District Collector, Irrigation department, and HYDRAA did not come under the GHMC Commissioner’s purview, and the citizens are forced to run from pillar to post for permissions. He sought to know how infrastructure, planning and manpower would be handled in expanded GHMC.
Legislator Sabitha Indra Reddy said the peripheral ULBs which had a collective 858 wards have now been reduced to mere 58, saying this would cause problems for citizens.

title: Second phase of Vizhinjam port development to begin in January
summary: Kerala's Vizhinjam port development's second phase begins in January, with ₹9,700 crore investment and new infrastructure for enhanced cargo movement.
content:
With the model code of conduct withdrawn after the local body elections, the Kerala government is planning to hold the inauguration of the second phase development of the Vizhinjam International Seaport in the second week of January.
Speaking to the media after a review of the performance of the Vizhinjam seaport here on Tuesday, Port Minister V.N. Vasavan said the inauguration of the second, third and fourth phases of construction, which would see an investment of ₹9,700 crore by the port concessionaire Adani Vizhinjam Port Pvt. Ltd. (AVPPL), would be held during the second week of January.
Additionally, the approach road to the port from National Highway-66 (NH-66) will also be inaugurated during the second week of January. This would facilitate the gateway cargo movements to and from Vizhinjam International Seaport, facilitating the movements of trailers and heavy vehicles to and from the port. The State government is of the view that the proposed cloverleaf interchange at the NH-66 junction will be helpful in easing the traffic along the route. The work on acquiring land for linking the project with the existing rail network at Balaramapuram railway station through an underground tunnel is progressing, said the Minister.
Around 50 hectares will have to be acquired to set up port-related infrastructure facilities. The land will be used for the development of a yard, security apparatus, customs and police aid posts and so on.
Land will be made available by reclaiming the sea as part of berth construction. The State also has plans to start cruise tourism based at the Vizhinjam port, and discussions are under way to arrange necessary infrastructure facilities for cruise tourism in the port. The land reclaimed from the sea would also be used for cruise tourism purposes, said the Minister.
As part of the second phase development, the existing 800-m berth will be increased by 1,200 meters to 2,000 m, while the 2.96-kilometre breakwater will also be increased by another 920 m. Since the launch of the commercial operations, the port has handled 13.25 lakh TEUs of cargo by facilitating the berthing of 636 ships. The port also contributed around ₹97 crore to the exchequer by way of tax. The port has also become the first port in India to handle cargo with more than 40 ultra-large container ships with a length of 399 m during this period. More than 155 ships with a length of more than 300 m and over 45 ships with drafts of more than 16 m called at Vizhinjam so far, said the Minister. Currently, the port provides direct employment to about 1,000 people, and when the next phases are completed, more than 6,000 people can be directly employed, said the Minister.
The Minister cut a cake on the occasion, celebrating the first anniversary of Vizhinjam International Port, which began commercial operations on December 3, 2024.

title: Krishna Bhaskar takes over as Singareni CMD
summary: D. Krishna Bhaskar assumes role as CMD of Singareni Collieries, driving expansion into power generation and rare earth minerals.
content:
HYDERABAD
D. Krishna Bhaskar, a 2012-batch IAS officer on Tuesday took over as the Chairman and Managing Director of Singareni Collieries Company Ltd (SCCL). He took charge from the outgoing officer N. Balram who is repatriating to his parent cadre IRS after a seven-year stint with Singareni.
Mr. Krishna Bhaskar will hold the post of SCCL CMD as the additional charge as he is officiating as the CMD of the Transmission Corporation of Telangana Ltd (TG-Transco) and also as the Special Secretary to Deputy Chief Minister and Minister for Finance and Energy Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka.
Mr. Balram joined Singareni in 2018 on deputation as the Director (Finance) and was holding charge as the CMD for the last two years after the Congress formed the government in the State. The change of guard in Singareni comes at a time when the State public sector undertaking is planning large-scale diversification and expansion, including exploration of rare earth minerals.
Apart from foraying into thermal and solar power generation within Telangana, the company is planning thermal and solar power generation in Rajasthan and Odisha, where it has taken up mining of coal in the Naini block earlier this year. The company is also planning to enter geo-thermal power generation, exploration of coal and rare earth minerals in other countries.

title: ‘Safe Road Happy Road' project flags alarming gaps in pedestrian safety in Thrissur
summary: Study by St. Thomas College, in collaboration with the MVD, finds only 20% of motorists stop at zebra crossings
content:
Student volunteers and faculty coordinators of the ’Safe Road Happy Road’ project of St. Thomas College (Autonomous) Thrissur have conducted a study on pedestrian safety at zebra crossings in Thrissur city in collaboration with the Motor Vehicles Department.
The study has been conducted in the context where road safety is becoming a serious concern in the State. The study has found that only about 20% of drivers stop their vehicles to let pedestrians cross at zebra crossings. The behaviour of pedestrians also needs to change, according to project coordinator Emmanuel Thomas.
“In the context of study, the ’Safe Road Happy Road’ project is planning a series of interventions to make our roads safe and happy. This will include improvements in foot-path, signage, road markings, and training for students, drivers and general public. Foot over-bridge and pelican zebra crossings are also mooted under the project. The project also has a green component which is expected to earn carbon credits,” he said.
A video created as part of the study was released by the patron of the college, Thrissur Archbishop Mar Andrews Thazhath on Tuesday. The video is available in the social media handles of MVD and the College. Logo of the project was launched by the Deputy Transport Commissioner James M.P. Amrutha A.L., a first year computer science student of the college designed the logo. Project coordinators Emmanuel Thomas, Dr. Rani Sebastian and Jijo Kuruvila briefed about the project at the event. As part of the project, awareness programmes will be conducted for the public, students and drivers.
Safe Road Happy Road project aims to create a replicable model of road safety. As part of the project a Road Safety Audit was conducted in 2024 by the SCMS Institute of Road Safety and Transportation (SiRST) on the one kilometre stretch of road from Swaraj Round to East Fort to transform it into a Model Road.
Subsequently, the project and the audit report were presented before the Mayor of Thrissur Corporation. The project had received the approval of Thrissur Corporation. The project also found mention in the last budget of the Corporation with an outlay of ₹5 Crores for all Model Roads, Mr. Thomas noted.

title: APSRTC scales up promotion of its advance ticket reservation facility on WhatsApp
summary: APSRTC enhances awareness of its WhatsApp advance ticket reservation service to boost passenger engagement and streamline bookings.
content:
The Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (APSRTC) on Tuesday (December 16, 2025) rolled out measures to increase awareness of its advance ticket reservation service on WhatsApp at 95523 00009 (’Mana Mitra’), in both Telugu and English.
Corporation’s Executive Director (Operations) A. Appala Raju issued instructions to the District Public Transport Officers to promote the process. They have been asked to display banners at bus stations, reservation counters, enquiry counters and other prominent locations within bus stations, display stickers inside buses, make announcements through the public address system, and widely publicise the corporations new service.
Pointing to the facility currently available through the “Mana Mitra-WhatsApp" governance initiative launched by the government, Mr. Appala Raju said it can be operated through a few simple steps. Save the WhatsApp number "95523 00009" or scan the provided QR code and send a "Hi” message on WhatsApp, select “Choose Service”, select “APSRTC Services”, select "Ticket Booking”, enter journey details and passenger information, make payment using the available online payment options and receive your confirmed ticket directly on WhatsApp, he said.
The State Transport Corporation currently issues advance ticket reservation through multiple authorised channels such as "B2C franchises" like RedBus, AbhiBus, Paytm, and Authorised Ticket Booking (ATB) agents.
Though the ticket-booking facility was made available through WhatsApp, it has been observed that use of this facility is very low among passengers due to lack of awareness. The APSRTC, therefore, decided to publicise this mode through wide publicity.

title: Forest Minister attributes human-animal conflicts to increase in animal population
summary: Forest Minister Eshwar Khandre links rising human-animal conflicts in Karnataka to the increasing animal population since 1972.
content:
Forest Minister Eshwar Khandre attributed the increase in the human-animal conflict in recent years to the increase in animal population.
Answering a question by D. Thimmaiah in the Legislative Council on Tuesday, Mr. Khandre said after the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, came into effect, the hunting of animals was stopped. Gradually the number of animals increased.
Karnataka stands first in the country considering the elephant population (6395) and second in terms of tiger population. As per the tiger census conducted in 2022, the tiger population was 563 in the State.
“But, when analysed again after the recent incidents of human-tiger conflicts, we understood that the number has gone up to 600 in the State. In the year 1972, the number of tigers in Bandipur was only 12. During our last census the number was 150 and now it has gone to 200,” he stated.
The Bandipur National Park is spread over 1,000 sq. km. “I had asked the officers to study the carrying capacity of the park. According to an estimation, a tiger needs an area of 11 to 12 sq. km. Going by the land available, the park could accommodate around 100-110 tigers. But the current population is around 200, initiating territorial fights among them. We have also studied the population of mammals like deer that tigers require to survive. There is no shortage of such animals,” he said.
The Minister said every year on an average 40-50 human deaths are reported in human-animal conflicts.

title: Govt. to consider bringing aided school teachers under ‘Arogya Sanjivini
summary: Karnataka government plans to include aided school teachers in 'Arogya Sanjivini' for cashless medical treatment in hospitals.
content:
Minister for School Education and Literacy Madhu Bangarappa has said that the government is positive towards bringing the teachers of aided schools under ‘Arogya Sanjivini’ schemes which enables the teachers to get cashless treatment in empanelled hospitals.
He was replying to the disucussion under Rule 330 in the Karnataka Legislative Council on the issues of disparities in the facilities to aided and government schools. Members S.L. Bhojegowda, Puttanna, Shashil Namoshi, S.V. Sankanur, D.T. Srinivas and Ramoji Gowda had raised the issue with a plea to treat the aided school teachers on par with government school teachers.
Mr Bangarappa said that as the issue required approval from the Finance Department, he would consult the Chief Minister and would make honest efforts to extend the facility to the teachers of aided schools. Intervening in the issue, Mr. Puttanna pointed out that Health Minister Dinesh Gundu Rao had also promised to extend the facility to aided school teachers earlier.
On the members’ demand for approving the recruitment process for aided schools in the State, the Minister announced that the calendar of events for the recruitment of teachers would be published within 15 days.
On the issue of contributory pension, the Minister said that as the issue did not pertain to his department, he would take it up with the Chief Minister.
Regarding the demand for allowing promotion of the primary school teachers to the posts of Graduate Primary Teachers, Mr. Gundu Rao said that as there were lot of technicalities included, he would try to address the issue as early possible.
The Minister also said that the department was in the process of further reducing the burden of non-teaching responsibilities pertaining to mid-day meal scheme, including procurement of eggs and bananas and in this regard, attendance through facial recognition was being introduced. By the next academic year the process would be simplified and burden would be reduced, he assured the members.

title: CPI likely to stake claim for chairperson post in Eloor municipality
summary: CPI aims to claim chairperson post in Eloor municipality after LDF's success in recent local body polls.
content:
The Communist Party of India (CPI) is likely to stake claim for the post of chairperson in Eloor municipality where the Left Democratic Front (LDF) emerged as the single largest front amid the sweep by the United Democratic Front (UDF) across municipalities in Ernakulam in the local body polls.
The LDF won 15 seats, while the UDF secured victory in 12 wards. The National Democratic Alliance (NDA) won five wards in the 32-member civic body. Of the 15 seats won by the LDF, four belonged to the CPI. The frontrunners for the post of chairperson in the CPI included Jayasree Sathish and Leela Babu. Both had served as deputy chairperson for an equal term in the previous council, according to party sources. The CPI had implemented a similar plan when it came to power in the civic body in the elections held in 2015.
Ms. Satheesh won from the Elanjikkal ward with a majority of 39 votes. Ms. Babu won from the Hostel ward with a majority of 435 votes. However, CPI(M) sources said it was too early to comment on the probable candidates as talks were yet to achieve a concrete shape. The probable candidates of the CPI(M) include Tisha Venu and Laiji Sajeevan. Ms. Venu won from the Pattupurackal ward with a majority of 270 votes, while Ms. Sajeevan secured victory in the Eloor depot ward with a majority of 54 votes.
The UDF was hopeful of making it through in the final leg, though it fell short of the half-way mark. The rebel menace had impacted its chances in a few wards. In Ward 22, the front candidate lost by two votes to the LDF candidate. The UDF was able to improve its performance this time as it had only seven seats in the previous council. The NDA’s tally came down to five this time compared to the six seats it had won in 2020.

title: Make introspection to check if minority votes drifted away from LDF: CPI
summary: CPI calls for introspection on minority vote loss for LDF amid concerns over secularism and communal identity politics.
content:
The Communist Party of India (CPI) State Executive on Tuesday called for an introspection into whether minority community votes had swung away from the Left Democratic Front (LDF) in the local body elections.
Minority communities were the Left’s natural allies, given the ascendancy of Hindu majoritarian nationalist forces over the past two decades. The LDF should expressly engage in self-criticism to determine whether the minorities have ceased to regard the ruling front as a natural ally and bulwark against the muscular Hindutva. The CPI also stressed that ideological clarity de-alienated the LDF from other political forces.
The critique assumes significance against the backdrop of criticism that the LDF risked losing its secular image among the minorities by seemingly failing to disassociate with and condemn influential leaders of powerful Hindu caste organisations accused of repeatedly and unapologetically bashing minority communities, including Muslims and Christians, in north and central Kerala, respectively.
A CPI insider noted that the LDF had taken a beating in the Christian-settler-farmer-dominated hilly districts despite the government passing a landmark law regularising land-use violations on acres allocated solely for farming and housing, a longstanding demand of the Church.
Similarly, he noted that LDF’s undiluted stance on Palestine, the CAA, the NEP, hijab, minority persecution in BJP-ruled States and related issues, which resonated emotively among the minorities, did not translate into votes, especially in north Kerala.
The CPI, according to some, also weighed whether the “ill-timed” Global Ayyappa Sanghamam and the Sabarimala gold theft scandal had propelled the Hindutva agenda, arguably dominant since the religiously charged Save Sabarimala Campaign in 2018, to the heart of the election debate, overshadowing the LDF’s social welfare and development narrative and, consequently, fuelling communal identity politics, arguably advantaging rival alliances.
The CPI State executive also felt that Hindutva and Islamist forces coalesced into the UDF’s “brazenly” anti-secular and anti-Left narrative stream, signalling a politically expedient nexus between the Congress, the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Jamaat-e-Islami to undermine the LDF.  The CPI said the LDF’s battles against the Union government on fiscal federalism and minority rights did not resonate with voters as expected.
However, the CPI State Council said the LDF was far from a spent political force. It said the ruling front fared better than in the 2010 local body elections. In the 2011 Assembly elections, the LDF restricted the UDF to a razor-thin two-seat majority. The political winds would blow differently in 2026, and the CPI concluded that the LDF would recover lost ground.

title: ECI publishes draft electoral rolls for five States and UTs
summary: ECI publishes draft electoral rolls for five States and UTs, removing over 58 lakh names from voter lists.
content:
The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Tuesday (December 16, 2025) published the draft electoral rolls of five States and Union Territories as part of the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, including West Bengal, which is due to go to the Assembly polls next year.
More than 58 lakh names have been removed from the existing voter lists in West Bengal, nearly 42 lakh in Rajasthan, 10 lakh in Goa, a little more than a lakh in Puducherry and nearly 1500 in Lakshwadweep.
Unlike the SIR exercise in Bihar, voters were not required to submit any of the 11 indicative documents to be included in the draft list under this phase, announced on October 27. Thus, the names of all voters who have submitted the Enumeration Form would be in the draft list.
ECI sources said that notices would be issued to voters whose names are in the draft list in case of any doubt, and they can be asked to produce documents. The draft list also includes names of voters who could not be mapped in the 2002-2003 list when the SIR was conducted, as well as those who might have been wrongly matched.
“Verification of each case will start now,” the sources toldThe Hindu.
In West Bengal, 7.08 crore (92.4 %) voters—out of 7.6 crore on the electoral rolls as of October 2025, before the SIR was announced—have submitted the Enumeration Forms and, as a result, have been included in the draft list. Of the names deleted, 24.16 lakh (3.15 %) were dead, 32.65 lakh (4.26 %) were found to have shifted or were absent, and 1.38 lakh (0.18 %) were found enrolled at multiple places.
In Rajasthan, of 5.46 crore voters in the existing list, 5.04 crore (92.34%) have been included in the draft list. Of the names deleted, 8.76 lakh (0.63%) were deceased voters, 29.6 lakh (5.43%) belonged to those who had shifted or were absent, and 3.44 lakh (0.63 %) were found enrolled at multiple places.
In Goa, 10.84lakh (91.56%), of 11.85lakh names, are in the draft list. Of the names removed, 25,574 (2.16 %) were deceased, 72,471 (6.12 %) were found shifted or absent, and 1,997 (0.17%) had enrolled at multiple places.
In the Union Territory of Puducherry, of the existing 10.21 lakh names, 9.18 lakh (89.87%) are in the draft list. Of the names deleted, 20,798 were deceased, 80,645 were found shifted or absent, and 2,024 were enrolled at multiple places.
Lakshadweep, the other Union Territory, has 56,384 (97.53%) names in the draft list, of the existing 57,813 voters. Of those left out, 705 were dead, 252 were found shifted/absent and 472 belonged to those who had enrolled at multiple places are 472.
The ECI said that the draft rolls, along with a detailed, booth-wise list of deleted voters and reasons for deletion, have been made available on the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) website, the Election Commission’s voter portal and the ECINET application.
The poll body said that if a voter does not find his or her name in the draft voter list, then he or she must fill Form 6 and submit it along with the requisite documents.
During the claims and objections period from December 16, 2025, to January 15, 2026, any existing or prospective elector may file claims or objections for inclusion of eligible electors or deletion of ineligible names. The verification phase will end on February 7. The final rolls will be published on February 14.
The ECI had announced SIR 2.0 in 12 states and Union Territories. But the exercise had to be postponed repeatedly, mainly due to work-related pressure on Booth Level Officers to complete the enumeration phase. Many have allegedly committed suicide or have wanted to quit due to the pressure.

title: SIR form submission: deadline ends on December 18
summary: Submit your SIR form by December 18 to ensure your details are included in the draft electoral roll.
content:
The deadline for submitting enumeration forms under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) 2026 of the electoral rolls ends on December 18. The draft electoral roll will be published on December 23 based on the forms received by the deadline.
District Collector Snehil Kumar Singh has urged eligible voters to ensure that their details are included in the draft list by submitting the forms without fail.
A total of 26,58,847 enumeration forms were distributed across the district, of which 1,96,900 forms, or 7.41%, are yet to be returned. The ‘absentee, shifted or dead’ (ASD) list — comprising voters who are untraceable, permanently shifted, deceased, duplicated, or those who refused to submit forms — is available with the respective Booth-Level Officers (BLOs). The list has also been shared with all booth-level agents, and voters can verify their status if required.
According to the district election department, 3.9% (1,03,806) of the enumeration forms returned could not be mapped with the 2002 electoral roll.

title: With a comfortable win, UDF has  a smooth road ahead in  Kalamassery
summary: UDF's decisive victory in Kalamassery positions Jamal Manakkadan as the likely chairperson, ensuring a smooth council leadership transition.
content:
Senior Congress leader Jamal Manakkadan seems to be the only choice of the Congress for the post of chairperson of the Kalamassery municipality after the United Democratic Front (UDF) registered an impressive win in the local body elections in the 46-member civic body.
Mr. Manakkadan, a former chairperson, had won the Vattekunnam ward with a majority of 17 votes this time. The Congress parliamentary party has almost confirmed his candidature for the post of chairperson after the UDF defeated the Left Democratic Front (LDF) in the local body elections by securing victory in 30 of the total 46 wards. Najeeb Kalamassery, president of the Congress party’s mandalam committee in Kalamassery, said that Mr. Manakkadan would lead the ruling council after the Congress-led UDF came up with a good performance in the local body polls. He said that the post of deputy chairperson would be given to the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) as part of an understanding within the front.
P.M.A. Latheef, president of the IUML’s Kalamassery Town Committee, said that they were considering Shanida Siddique and Shareena Kamaruddin for the post of deputy chairperson. A final decision would be taken soon, he said. Ms. Siddique had won the Mini town hall ward with a majority of 131 votes. Ms. Kamaruddin had won the municipal ward with a majority of 29 votes.
The election to the post of chairperson is expected to be smooth, as the UDF enjoys a majority in the council, while the LDF could manage only 13 wards in the polls. It had a total strength of 20 councillors after the local body elections held in 2020. Luck had favoured the UDF last time after Seema Kannan, Congress councillor, was chosen as chairperson through a draw of lots.
The Bharatiya Janata Party-led National Democratic Alliance was unable to improve upon its performance in the polls, settling for a single win after retaining the Thrikkakara temple ward with a majority of 11 votes.

title: International job fair to be held in February/March, 2026
summary: International Job Fair scheduled for February/March 2026, aimed at enhancing employability through skill development and industry linkage initiatives.
content:
Minister for Medical Education, Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood Sharanaprakash Patil announced in the Legislative Council on Tuesday that an International Job Fair would be held in February/March next year (2026).
Replying to the issue raised by Bharati Shetty on Tuesday, Dr. Sharanprakash Patil elaborated on how the government was preparing the ground for the international job fair including conducting road shows in varous countries.
Dr. Patil said that through Industry Linkage Cell (ILC), the government had changed the training pattern to make the youths including ITI, Diploma and engineering and other degree holders employable in the industires.
The Minister said three skill development centres would be set up at Kalaburagi, Koppal and Mysuru to cater to the changed skill set requirements of the industry.

title: Man held on charge of online fraud in Kozhikode
summary: Kozhikode police arrest Basim Nujoom for online fraud, swindling ₹76.35 lakh through fake investment schemes.
content:
The Cyber police team here arrested Basim Nujoom, 32, of Kayanna, on charge of swindling ₹76.35 lakh from a resident of Kozhikode after promising him profits in online investment plans.
According to police sources, the accused convinced the complainant that he would get profits after depositing money in initial public offerings and the share market. Later, he reportedly made the complainant transfer ₹76.35 lakh through 20 transactions to multiple bank accounts. The police had issued a look-out notice against Nujoom after the episode came to light. He was detained at the Mumbai airport subsequently. The police team went to Mumbai and took him into custody.

title: DGCA assures HC that IndiGo will implement new pilot duty norms before February 10
summary: DGCA assures Delhi HC that IndiGo will implement new pilot duty norms by February 10, despite recent operational disruptions.
content:
The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) on Tuesday (December 16, 2025) told the Delhi High Court that it will ensure IndiGo implements the new pilot rest and duty norms expeditiously, despite the regulator granting the airline an exemption until February 10.
Appearing before a Bench of Justice Amit Sharma in connection with a contempt plea moved by a pilot body seeking proceedings against the regulator for granting relaxations to various airlines, the DGCA said the “exemptions are not granted happily”.
The Bench issued notice to the DGCA and directed its top officials to file their response in the matter. The court listed the case for the next hearing on April 17, 2026.
The plea by the Indian Pilots’ Guild (IPG) argued that the DGCA had granted exemptions to airlines such as Air India and IndiGo despite the court ordering the implementation of the Flight Duty Time Limitation (FDTL), which governs pilot rest and duty hours, in April 2025.
On December 5, the DGCA issued an order exempting IndiGo until February 10 from implementing two specific provisions of the rules on pilot rest and duty hours, including the definition of night duty and the capping of landings to two per night shift, flight time to eight hours per day, and duty time, which includes flight time and pre and post-flight duties, to not more than 10 hours for a night shift. The exemptions were granted after the airline witnessed a disruption in its operations in the first 10 days of December, leading to over 5,000 flight cancellations, which it attributed to “planning gaps” in ensuring pilot availability as per the new norms.
Earlier, ahead of the implementation of certain clauses on November 1, the DGCA had permitted Air India and IndiGo limited variations, allowing up to three landings in a night shift instead of the prescribed cap of two landings, in certain circumstances.
Opposing the contempt plea, the DGCA’s counsel submitted that the court had not frozen the contents of the Civil Aviation Requirement, which constitutes the regulator’s rules. While implementation timelines were binding, the regulator retained statutory powers under the Aircraft Act and Rules to grant temporary, case-specific exemptions, the counsel said adding that DGCA was working to ensure that IndiGo implements the norms before February 10.
The pilot body contended that airlines were misusing the provision for filing FDTL variations, which was intended for post-flight documentation rather than flight planning.

title: Supreme Court refers to three-judge Bench a plea to protect the rights of intersex children
summary: Supreme Court considers a petition for intersex children's rights, emphasizing the need for clear distinctions between sex and gender identity.
content:
The Supreme Court on Tuesday (December 16, 2025) agreed to examine in detail a petition filed by intersex rights activist Gopi Shankar Madurai seeking urgent safeguards for intersex children, including a ban on non-consensual sex-selective surgeries on intersex infants, and comprehensive recognition in official records.
“This is a very good issue. We want to hear this,” Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, accompanied by Justice Joymalya Bagchi, remarked.
The Chief Justice ordered the petition to be placed before a larger Bench of three judges the next time.
The petitioner, represented by advocate Astha Deep, urged the inclusion of intersex infants in India’s population Census, which currently overlooks this diverse group by enforcing binary sex norms.
“This invisibility affects over 25 million intersex individuals (1.7% of the population), denying them access to welfare, healthcare, and identity services. Inclusion of intersex in the national Census is crucial for accurate data collection and policy-making,” the petitioner submitted.
The petition called for intersex recognition alongside the existing male and female options in the Census and other forms, while ensuring accurate recording of births and deaths to enable targeted policies.
The case underscored the vital need for the judiciary and government to distinguish between sex identity and gender identity, and to clarify that intersex persons were not transgender.
“Sex identity referred to innate biological variations, including intersex traits that did not fit typical male or female binaries, whereas gender identity was a personal and social construct often involving a mismatch with assigned sex (as in transgender experiences). The conflation of these terms in laws, identity documents like Aadhaar and passports, and policies leads to forced interventions on infants, discrimination, and erasure. Issuing cards that separately record sex and gender is urged to uphold Articles 14, 15, and 21, fostering dignity and equality,” the petitioner submitted.

title: Udhayanidhi Stalin launches Athlete Management System
summary: Udhayanidhi Stalin launches an Athlete Management System, integrating training, wellness, performance, and medical insights into a digital platform.
content:
Tamil Nadu Deputy Chief Minister Udhayanidhi Stalin on Tuesday launched an Athlete Management System at the Tamil Nadu Sports Conclave in Chennai on Tuesday.
For the first time, the State government was bringing together training, wellness, performance, and medical insights into a single, intelligent digital platform, he said, adding that since 2023, the conclave had emerged as a powerful platform for the exchange of ideas, innovation, and inspiration in sports development.
Listing the steps taken to promote sports in the State, Mr. Udhayanidhi said: “We are constructing the Chief Minister’s Mini Stadium in all constituencies of the State, each at a cost of ₹3 crore, with a minimum of five sporting facilities.”
The Tamil Nadu government was providing financial assistance to players through the Tamil Nadu Champions Foundation even before they were participating in major events. The State government encouraged them with high cash incentives after they win medals, he said. Last year, it gave over 100 jobs to sportspersons in Tamil Nadu, he recalled.
The initiatives taken up by the government are receiving recognition from various quarters, Mr. Udhayanidhi said and added that they remained fully committed to strengthening sports infrastructure, scientific support systems, coaching excellence, and policy frameworks. “We strongly believe that progress in sports is never achieved alone. It’s going to be a team effort,” he added.

title: Changaroth grama panchayat president files complaint against ‘caste slur’
summary: Changaroth panchayat president files complaint against IUML workers for caste slur during a victory celebration in Kozhikode.
content:
Unni Vengeri, incumbent president of Changaroth grama panchayat near Perambra in Kozhikode district, has filed a complaint with the Deputy Superintendent of Police, Perambra, accusing Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) workers of demeaning his caste during a victory celebration taken out on December 13 after the declaration of the local body poll results.
In the complaint filed on Tuesday (December 16), Mr. Vengeri, who is from the Left Democratic Front (LDF), said that after the United Democratic Front (UDF) captured power in the panchayat, five of the IUML workers and 25 others barged into the panchayat office. They erected flags of the Congress and the IUML there and threw away some of the furniture kept in the office. The group later resorted to a clean-up act after spraying cow dung water on the premises, while raising abusive slogans. Visuals of the incident were later circulated on social media.
Mr. Vengeri, who belongs to the Scheduled Caste (SC), claimed that the IUML workers did it to demean him and others belonging to his community and to express their displeasure over his status as the panchayat president. He said that though the UDF had come to power in some other panchayats in Perambra, similar acts were not performed at any of those places. Mr. Vengeri also alleged that a Facebook profile titled Praveen Kumar Wayanad had circulated the video. In the 2020-25 period, the post of panchayat president in Changaroth was reserved for the SC community. Mr. Vengeri is an area committee member of the Communist Party of India (Marxist).
Meanwhile, LDF activists staged a protest against the episode in the evening. However, IUML local leaders denied the allegations and claimed it was a “symbolic protest” to show that the “corrupt LDF was wiped out of power.”

title: 5,757 constables inducted into A.P. Police; monthly stipend hiked to ₹12,500
summary: Andhra Pradesh inducts 5,757 constables into police, raising monthly stipend to ₹12,500, fulfilling job creation promises.
content:
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Tuesday announced a substantial hike in the monthly stipend paid to police constables undergoing training to ₹12,500 from the existing ₹4,500 during a programme in which appointment letters were given away to 5,757 constables inducted into the Andhra Pradesh Police.
Handing over the appointment letters to the newly inducted constables at the APSP 6th Battalion parade ground near the DGP office in Mangalagiri, Mr. Naidu described the moment as a decisive step towards restoring trust, transparency and strength in the State’s law enforcement system.
Addressing the gathering after distributing the appointment letters, Mr. Naidu said the NDA-led coalition government had fulfilled its promise of providing jobs to the youth soon after coming to power.
The long-pending court cases related to police recruitment were resolved after the coalition government assumed office, enabling the issue of appointment letters to the candidates who had waited for nearly four years.
The constables, he said, would join active duty immediately after completing their training.
The Chief Minister asserted that during his tenure, 23,676 police jobs had been provided, including 5,757 constable appointments now. “Our manifesto promised 20 lakh jobs, and we remain committed to that goal,” Mr. Naidu said, adding that 4 lakh jobs had already been generated across departments.
He emphasised that the recruitment process was completed in record time with digital tools and without ‘corruption of a single rupee’ through 31 writ petitions aimed at stalling the process were filed.
Stressing the link between law and order and development, Mr. Naidu said investments flow only where peace prevails. He cited approvals for investments worth 8.5 lakh crore and major industrial proposals, including MoUs signed in Visakhapatnam.
He praised Home Minister Vangalapudi Anitha for efficiently steering the department and warned that crimes against women, cybercrime and drug trafficking would be dealt with firmly.
Reiterating the State government’s commitment towards empowering women, the Chief Minister also announced that women would be recruited as APSRTC bus drivers. Women are already serving APSRTC as bus conductors.
Director General of Police Harish Kumar Gupta was present at the ceremony.
Speaking on this occasion, Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan said over five lakh aspirants appeared for the examinations conducted to fill about 6,100 constable vacancies, calling the selection of 5,757 candidates a ‘moment of pride’.
The NDA government is determined to dismantle the entrenched corruption. It has granted promotions to more than 10,000 Panchayat Raj employees. We cannot give back the years to the candidates, but we stand by them,” he said, urging the new recruits to uphold discipline and integrity.
A newly recruited constable L. Babu Rao sought a road to his village in Alluri Sitharama Raju district. Acting on the Chief Minister’s direction, Mr. Pawan Kalyan announced that a ₹3.98-crore road project would be taken up immediately, drawing applause from the gathering.

title: Applications invited for Green Champion Awards 2025 of TNPCB
summary: Apply now for the Green Champion Awards 2025 by TNPCB, recognizing outstanding contributions to environmental conservation.
content:
The district administration has invited applications for the Green Champion Award 2025 of the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board (TNPCB) from individuals and organisations who have made exemplary contribution to environmental conservation and protection. The award is presented annually to 100 recipients, each receiving ₹1 lakh.
The initiative recognises efforts in environmental education, research, sustainability, waste management, water conservation, climate action, emission reduction, plastic waste control, eco-restoration, and coastal protection. Eligible applicants, include organisations, educational institutions, local bodies, industries, and individuals.
The selection process will be conducted through a District Level Award Committee (DLAC) chaired by the Cuddalore District Collector.
Applications will be assessed based on their impact and contribution to environmental sustainability. The application format is available on the TNPCB website (www.tnpcb.gov.in), and additional details can be obtained from the District Environmental Engineer, TNPCB, Cuddalore. The last date for submission is January 20, 2026.

title: Government tables Bill to replace MGNREGA amid protests
summary: Government introduces VB-G RAM G Bill to replace MGNREGA, facing opposition protests over concerns of weakened employment rights for the poor.
content:
The government on Tuesday (December 16, 2025) introduced the c (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Bill, 2025, which seeks to replace the two-decade-old Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), amid Opposition protests. Members marched from the Lok Sabha chamber to Mahatma Gandhi’s statue on the Parliament premises, demanding the Bill be sent for further scrutiny.
Parliament Winter Session:Follow LIVE updates on December 16, 2025
Introducing the Bill, Union Rural Development Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said, “The (Narendra) Modi government has done more for rural development than previous governments. We not only believe in Mahatma Gandhi but also follow his principles... We will fully develop the village and work to establish a balance between agriculture and labour… This entire Bill is in line with Gandhiji’s sentiments and is meant to establish Ram Rajya.”
Opposition leaders strongly objected with the DMK’s T.R. Baalu saying, “The father of the nation is being ridiculed.”
Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra called MGNREGA a “revolutionary Act” which was unanimously supported by Parliament. “This Bill (VB-G RAM G) is weakening the employment rights of the poor. It is against the Constitution,” she said, accusing the government of dismantling the demand-driven architecture of MGNREGA and replacing it with a pre-decided budget. She also flagged centralisation of decision-making. “The new Bill weakens the right-based structure of the MGNREGA,” she said.
Ms. Vadra warned that reducing the Centre’s share of funding from 90% to 60% would hit State finances already strained by GST compensation delays. Proposing that the Bill be sent to a parliamentary panel, she added, “Mahatma Gandhi was not from my family, but he was from every family in the country.”
ALSO WATCHWatch: G RAM G Bill an assault on MGNREGA’s spirit and philosophical foundation: Shashi Tharoor
Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, in a post onX, alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi has always opposed Mahatma Gandhi’s ideas and sought to weaken MGNREGA since coming to power. “Modijihas a deep hatred for two things — the ideas of Mahatma Gandhi and the rights of the poor,” he said, vowing Congress will oppose any such move.
Congress MP Shashi Tharoor called the Bill a “retrograde step” and “ill-advised”, criticising the removal of Mahatma Gandhi’s name. “It strips the Bill of its moral compass and historical legitimacy,” he said. Quoting a 1971 Hindi film song, he said,“Dekho o deewano ye kaam na karo, Ram ka naam badnaam na karo(don’t do this, don’t malign Ram’s name).” Mr. Tharoor argued that shifting liability to States violated fiscal federalism.
The Trinamool Congress’s Saugata Roy demanded the Bill be referred to a select committee. The RSP’s N.K. Premchandran pointed out technical flaws and said States cannot afford the added financial burden.
Congress general secretary K.C. Venugopal dismissed the promise of 125 days of work as “hollow”. Addressing Mr. Chouhan, he said, “Your name will be remembered as a Minister who removed Mahatma Gandhi’s name.”
Opposition members stormed the Well of the House, holding photographs of Gandhiji. Amid the din, Mr. Chouhan reiterated that the Bill reflects Gandhian ideals and aims to create “Ram Rajya” in villages. After walking out, Opposition MPs marched to the Mahatma Gandhi statue. Women members raised slogans from the old Parliament building’s balcony. Left parties had earlier staged protests before the sitting began.
The Congress announced nationwide protests on Wednesday. In a letter to State presidents, Mr. Venugopal called for demonstrations at district headquarters. “The combined attack on Gandhiji’s legacy, workers’ rights and federal responsibility exposes a larger BJP-RSS conspiracy to dismantle rights-based welfare and replace it with charity controlled from the Centre.” He called it both a “political and moral struggle”.
