Shivakumar pointed out that the Centre was yet to honour its commitment of providing ₹ 5,300 crore to Karnataka for the Upper Bhadra Project and thousands of crores of rupees under MGNREGA and Jaljivan mission. “Can we say that the Centre has not transferred this amount to Karnataka because it is financially bankrupt?” he shot back. Whatever the funds are released by the Finance Department would be transferred to beneficiaries, he said.
He launched a counter attack at the BJP by maintaining that the BJP was winning various state assembly elections by copying the guarantee schemes of the Congress government.
RDPR Minister Priyank Kharge too joined the attack by accusing the BJP of even indulging in vote chori to win polls. This triggered a heated exchange of words between the ruling and the Opposition members.
Finally, the Opposition members staged a walkout expressing dissatisfaction over the Minister not announcing when the installments of February and March would be paid.

title: T.N. government to expand cool roof initiative to 297 green schools: CM Stalin
summary: Tamil Nadu expands its cool roof initiative to 297 green schools, enhancing climate resilience and environmental awareness among students.
content:
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin on Wednesday (December 17, 2025) said that the State government will expand the cool roof initiative to 297 green schools across the State, and the one-day summer and winter special environmental awareness camps for schoolchildren will now be conducted as two-day camps.
Addressing the third meeting ofthe Tamil Nadu Governing Council on Climate Changeat the Secretariat in Chennai, Mr. Stalin recalled the impact of Cyclone Ditwah in Sri Lanka and said the world is witnessing the effects of climate change. Due to various precautionary measures taken by the Tamil Nadu government, the State averted large-scale damage, he said.
Listing various initiatives taken by his government over the past three years, including the Tamil Nadu Wetlands Mission, the Tamil Nadu Climate Change Mission, and the Tamil Nadu Coastal Restoration Mission (TN-SHORE), Mr. Stalin said the State today stands as an example in taking pioneering initiatives to mitigate the impact of climate change.
Under the climate literacy initiative, a total of 4,000 teachers have been selected and programmes will commence soon, he said. To create environmental awareness among schoolchildren, the State government had already initiated one-day summer and winter special camps, conducted twice a year through the District Climate Change Mission. This initiative is now set to be expanded into two-day camps through the School Education Department.
He said the cool roof initiative has been included in the 2025-26 action plan of the Tamil Nadu Climate Change Mission. Under this initiative, classrooms of a government school in Ambattur have been coated with heat-reflective white paint. Monitoring using sensors has shown a reduction in indoor temperature ranging from 1.5 to 3 degrees Celsius. Following this, the State government has planned to implement the initiative in 297 green schools across Tamil Nadu.
Mr. Stalin also highlighted the measures taken by the State government to transform Killai near Pichavaram in Cuddalore district under the climate resilient village programme. He said the mangrove cover in Tamil Nadu has increased from 4,500 hectares to 9,000 hectares.
Research shows that women and girl children are among those most affected by natural disasters worldwide, he said, urging officials to ensure gender equality while formulating climate mitigation and adaptation measures. Women play an important role in combating climate change. Under the climate warriors programme, 100 e-autorickshaws have been provided to 100 women self-help groups to carry out awareness campaigns on climate change and plastic elimination, he said.
He said the transport sector’s share of Tamil Nadu’s total greenhouse gas emissions has increased from 12% to 19%. Considering increasing traffic congestion in metro cities such as Chennai, Mr. Stalin emphasised the need to use public transport. He said that in the first phase, 120 electric buses have been introduced through the Metropolitan Transport Corporation. The State government has planned to introduce another 600 electric buses soon.
He said that with regard to global warming, Tamil Nadu should achieve the target of net zero before 2070, and that the State has been working extensively at both policy and action levels over the past four years. He also said the State government sought ₹24,679 crore disaster relief funds to the Centre, but it only received ₹4,136 crore.
Mr. Stalin also released a technical report on blue carbon wealth of Tamil Nadu and a report on reducing marine litter on Tamil Nadu coast under Tamil Nadu fishnet initiative. Minister for Finance Thangam Thennarasu, Chief Secretary N. Muruganandam, and Additional Chief Secretary, Environment, Climate Change and Forests Supriya Sahu, among others, participated.

title: Mohali Kabaddi player killing: Suspect shot dead in encounter
summary: Police fatally shot a suspect linked to the Mohali kabaddi player’s murder during an encounter in Chandigarh.
content:
A suspect in the killing of a 30-year-old kabaddi player-cum-promoter in Mohali was shot dead by police in an encounter on Wednesday (December 17, 2025).
Harpinder alias Middu, a resident of Naushehra Pannuan in Punjab's Tarn Taran district, was injured in an exchange of fire during a chase and later succumbed to injuries in hospital, police said.
Two police personnel were also injured and were given medical treatment, they said.
Preliminary investigation revealed that the suspect was involved in multiple heinous crimes and has a serious criminal background, the police said.
Kanwar Digvijay Singh, alias Rana Balachauria, was shot after he arrived with his team to take part in a private tournament in Mohali on Monday (December 15). He was critically injured in the attack and was rushed to the Fortis Hospital in Mohali, where he was declared dead.
The assailants fled on a motorcycle after firing from a .30 bore weapon.
The police had earlier in the day termed Harpinder's arrest as a "major breakthrough" and said he was being treated for injuries suffered in the exchange of fire.
"In a major breakthrough, @sasnagarpolice apprehends Harpinder @ Middu, a resident of Naushehra Pannuan, Tarn Taran, in connection with the recent murder of Kanwar Digvijay Singh @ Rana Balachauria in Mohali. The accused was apprehended following an exchange of fire with the police team," it said in a post onX.
Following the killing of the player, the police had had identified two shooters — Aditya Kapoor alias Makhan and Karan Pathak alias Defaulter Karan, both residents of Amritsar.

title: Bangla band, once the voice of a generation, to reunite after 20 years for one evening
summary: Parash Pathar reunites after 20 years, bringing nostalgia and emotion to Kolkata's 1990s college memories in a special performance.
content:
It’s likely to be an emotional moment on Thursday (December 18, 2025) evening for many Kolkatans who were in college in the 1990s when they watch the Bengali band Parash Pathar — a rage at the time — reunite for a performance after 20 years.
This former band will be performing at the Kolkata Centre for Creativity along with another group, Prithibi, which was instrumental in the old bandmates coming together again for a show. The event is a part of the month-long arts festival being held in the city by the centre.
“When we started our journey, in the early 1990s, I was in my teens, most of us were in our teens. I had limited knowledge about music at the time but we had a lot of emotions and dreams to fulfil. Our first album came out in 1996 — we were the first Bangla band to release an album — so there are a lot of emotions, lot of achievements, lot of memories. Lot of great things related to Parash Pathar will remain with us for the rest of our lives. It is a great feeling to come together again,” music director Samidh Mukherjee, a founding member of the band, said.
“We artistes have a fire inside us, and one byproduct of that fire is ego. So naturally, after a point of time, things happen. It is about a balance between the ego and the artiste, sometimes the ego gets priority. This has happened with a lot of bands. Coming back together is like coming back to your own family after a long vacation. It is beautiful to see the simplicity in the guys still intact. All of them are very good souls, who have matured as great musicians. We have shaped up a great arrangement and repertoire for the show, and I am sure people are going to get the old taste in a new bottle,” Mr. Mukherjee added.
As far as Bangla bands go, Moheener Ghoraguli is considered the oldest, set up in 1975, thus considered even the oldest in India; but Parash Pathar was immensely popular in the 1990s, becoming the voice of a generation. “Their songs not only embodied the romantic spirit of youth, but also the insecurities and uncertainties that accompanied one when entering into adulthood. Now, in my 40s, whenever I listen to songs from their albums likeMoney Achhe(1996), I am flooded with memories of a time that changed so very fast. By the early 2000s, the world was a different place with the mobile phone and the spread of the Internet. To me, Parash Pathar is a part of my youth, when one of the coolest places to go was the Archies Gallery, as their songBhalobashasays. I am looking forward to hearing some of the old hits just for a taste of nostalgia,” Anindya Sekhar Majumdar, an ad filmmaker, said.
Suparna Mukherjee, a banker, is another fan eagerly waiting for the show on Thursday. “Parash Pathar’s songs were like love anthems when I was in college. Their songBhalo Lage Swapner Maya Jaal Buntehelped me weave my dreams in those growing up years. A must-listen in college fests, the band’s songs captured the emotions and aspirations of an entire generation. Several of my college friends will be there too,” she said.

title: Here are the big stories from Karnataka today
summary: Karnataka Today newsletter: Minister apologises for ‘wrong’ information on Gruha Lakshmi payment after BJP protest, and more
content:
Women and Child Development Minister Laxmi Hebbalkar on apologised in the Karnataka Assemblyfor giving wrong information to the House on payment of Gruha Laksmi scheme installments, after the BJP members staged a protest demanding an apology. A few days ago, the Minister, in her reply to BJP member Mahesh Tenginakayi, had claimed that the government of Karnataka had cleared all the pending installment towards Gruha Lakshmi scheme till August 2025.
Though the Opposition members had complained that the installments for February and March had not been paid, she had maintained that there were no pending installments. Subsequently, when it turned out that the installments for these two months had not been paid, the Opposition members had urged Speaker U. T. Khader to ask the Minister to clarify.
On December 17, the Opposition members insisted that the minister should clarify to the House immediately and also tender an apology to 1.26 crore beneficiaries. They accused the Minister of misleading the House. Pointing out that the two installments amounted to nearly ₹5,000 crore, they urged her to let the House know where did the money went.
Congress legislators, on December 17,staged a protest in Belagavialleging that the Central Government had targeted its leaders in theNational Heraldcase, and to oppose the Union Government’s move to rename Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme as Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Graman) – VB-G Ram G.
Addressing the gathering, CM Siddaramaiah said that the BJP government at the Centre was engaged in the politics of hatred. “The party is targeting Congress leaders by filing false cases. ...During Mr. Modi’s rule, the debt has increased. Since independence, the country has had total debt of ₹53 lakh crore. However, during Mr. Modi’s rule, total debt has increased to ₹148 lakh crore,” he said.
Minister for Forest, Environment and Ecology Eshwar Khandre has assured Dakshina Kannada-Udupi Local Authorities constituency MLC Kishor Kumar Puttur that the elephant task force sanctioned for Dakshina Kannada districtwill become functional from next week. He also promised to visit Sullia taluk that has been affected by the conflict immediately after the legislature session.
The Minister said he would would strive to find a permanent and scientific solution to end the human-elephant conflict by preparing a comprehensive action plan, covering aspects, namely, elephant movement patterns, hotspot identification, emergency response mechanisms, fencing and barrier systems, lighting arrangements and technology-based surveillance.

title: Nagaswaram player S.R.G. Rajanna no more
summary: Renowned nagaswaram player S.R.G. Rajanna, a key figure in traditional music, passed away at 94 in Chennai.
content:
Renowned nagaswaram player Semponnarkoil S.R.G. Rajanna passed away on Wednesday (December 17, 2025). He was 94.
The son of Semponnarkoil Govindasamy Pillai, he performed alongside his elder brother, S.R.G. Sambandam. Exponents of the Semponnarkoil tradition, which includedrakthi melam, the brothers performed across the country as well as abroad. They wereasthana vidwansof the Dharmapuram, Tirupanandal, and Tiruvavaduturai Adeenams, and of the Kanchi Sankara Math. The duo also performed on invitation at several samasthanams.
Semponnarkoil, a small town, secured a place in Thevaram as the Swarnapuresswarar temple was sung in praise by Gnanasambandar. Their grandfather, Ramasamy Pillai, was the first nagaswaram player to cut a disc, which is still available. Rajanna learnt the nagaswaram from Pandanallur Venugopala Pillai and Govindaswamy Pillai. He lived in Mayiladuthurai before shifting his base to Chennai.
He was conferred the Mumbai-based Sri Shanmukhananda Sabha’s National Eminence Award for nagaswaram to mark the 125th birth anniversary of nagaswaram wizard T.N. Rajarathinam Pillai. Rajanna had also received the Music Academy’s T.T.K. Award for Excellence.

title: State Minorities Commission submits report to CM Stalin
summary: State Minorities Commission presents a comprehensive report on minority grievances to Chief Minister M.K. Stalin in Chennai.
content:
Office bearers of the Tamil Nadu State Minorities Commission on Wednesday called on Chief Minister M.K. Stalin at the Secretariat in Chennai and submitted a report.
The report was drafted after members of the Commission toured all 38 districts and collected grievances pertaining to minorities. State Minorities Commission Chairperson S.J. Joe Arun handed over the report to Mr. Stalin.
Minister for Minorities Welfare and Non-Resident Tamils Welfare S.M. Nasar, the Commission’s Vice-Chairperson Iraianban Kuthoos, and Chief Secretary N. Muruganandam were among those present.
Separately, the pontiff of Kundrakudi Thiruvannamalai Adheenam Ponnambala Adigalar met the Chief Minister at the Secretariat.

title: Bid to protect ‘Rice bowl of Vadakara’ as a community reserve
summary: Efforts to designate Cherandathur Chira as a community reserve aim to conserve its rich biodiversity and support local livelihoods.
content:
The Social Forestry Division of the Forest department has initiated discussions on designating Cherandathur Chira, popularly known as the rice bowl of Vadakara, as a community reserve.
A project report documenting the biodiversity features of the region will be prepared soon and submitted to the local administration and the Forest department authorities for further proceedings and approval.
Forest department officials said the proposed project aims at conserving nearly 600 acres of wetland in Maniyur grama panchayat that serves as a habitat for several migratory birds. A recent bird identification programme has recorded over 80 bid species, including several rare migratory ones, they said.
If local residents and administrators extend their support, a Haritha Samiti (green committee) will be formed with community participation to implement various conservation initiatives. With the community reserve status, priority will be given to promoting ecotourism projects and sustainable livelihood programmes in cooperation with the Union and State governments.
Farmers now engaged in paddy cultivation are also expected to receive better support through integrated farming projects alongside wetland ecosystem conservation. Officials who were part of the initial discussions say the community reserve status will help effectively prevent illegal wetland reclamation activities.
“The Kadalundi community reserve will serve as our model for implementation. The project will be coordinated by the Vadakara range of the Social Forestry division,” said a senior Forest department officer. He said the cooperation of the newly elected local body members in the Maniyur panchayat would be crucial for realising the initiative.
A birdwatcher who participated in the recent identification programme in the area said the sighting of Common Pochard, a medium-sized diving duck facing extinction threats, had attracted State-level attention. Nearly 10 rare varieties of migratory ducks, including the Ferruginous duck and Eurasian wigeon, were also spotted in the area, he said.

title: BJP holds core committee meeting to discuss roadmap for 2026 Assembly poll
summary: BJP's Tamil Nadu core committee meets to strategize for the 2026 Assembly elections, following key discussions in New Delhi.
content:
The Tamil Nadu unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party on Wednesday organised a meeting of its core committee in Chennai to discuss the roadmap for the 2026 Assembly election.
This was the party’s first meeting after its State president Nainar Nagenthran and former State president K. Annamalai met Union Home Minister Amit Shah separately in New Delhi earlier this month. The meeting was held at a private hotel in Guindy, and was attended by senior BJP leaders.
Addressing the media after the meeting, Mr. Nagenthran said the National Democratic Alliance remained strong, and was ready to face the election at any time. He said his State-wide tour would conclude on January 9, 2026. Either Prime Minister Narendra Modi or the Union Home Minister would participate in a public meeting on that day, he said.
According to BJP sources, the leaders discussed the roadmap for next year’s Assembly election, adoption of micro-level strategies at the booth level, and coordination with alliance partners for carrying out election-related activities.
Meanwhile, Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal, who was recently appointed the party’s Tamil Nadu in-charge for the 2026 Assembly election, is likely to visit the State next week. BJP sources said he is expected to hold discussions with the top leadership of the party’s Tamil Nadu unit. The Union Minister is also likely to meet AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami.

title: Speaker dismisses disqualification petitions against five BRS MLAs
summary: Telangana Speaker dismisses disqualification petitions against five BRS MLAs, ruling they remain affiliated with the party.
content:
In a major political development, Telangana Legislative Assembly Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar has dismissed the disqualification petitions filed against five Bharat Rashtra Samiti MLAs.
The Speaker, whodelivered his verdicton the petitions of five BRS MLAs Arekapudi Gandhi, Tellam Venkat Rao, Gudem Mahipal Reddy, T. Prakash Goud and Bandla Krishnamohan Reddy, said there was no truth in the claim that these MLAs shifted their allegiance to the ruling Congress. In the much awaited verdict on the disqualification petitions moved by the BRS leadership, the Speaker said that the petitioners did not submit necessary proofs to substantiate their charge that the MLAs switched sides.
In his report compiled after hearing the arguments of the advocates on behalf of the petitioners and respondent MLAs, Mr. Prasad Kumar, chairing the tribunal constituted under Tenth Schedule of the Constitution dealing with the Anti Defection Law, said the MLAs technically continued to be with the BRS as the petitioners could not prove their arguments.
Faced with the deadline set by the Supreme Court to complete proceedings into the disqualification petitions moved by the BRS against 10 of its MLAs, the Speaker heard arguments in support of and against the disqualification of the MLAs for close to three months.
While the advocates from the BRS side submitted proofs alleging that the MLAs indeed switched loyalties going by the proofs of their close movement with the powers that be in the ruling party, advocates on behalf of the respondent MLAs asserted that they continued in the BRS and that they met Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and other Ministers seeking release of funds and execution of other development works pertaining to their respective constituencies.
Advocates on behalf of Mr. Gandhi argued that their client continued to be the chairman of the Public Accounts Committee, a post traditionally given to the principal Opposition party, and that there was no truth in the claim that he had shifted loyalty to the Congress. The MLAs facing charges of defection claimed that they continued to sit in the seats allotted to them on the basis of the party they represented and that there was no fact in the petitioners’ charges.
The Speaker dismissed the petitions claiming that they were not maintainable and that the MLAs continue to be affiliated to the BRS. The Tribunal is likely to announce its stand pertaining to three more legislators Kale Yadaiah, Pocharam Srinivas Reddy and M. Sanjay Kumar in a day or two and it has to be waited and seen whether the tribunal adopts the same yardstick for these legislators.
Interestingly, two more MLAs Danam Nagender and Kadiyam Srihari did not attend the hearings despite receiving notices more than once. The two MLAs requested the Speaker to grant them some more time to submit their responses to the notices.

title: E-double-deckers soon for Thrissur and Kozhikode
summary: The Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) will introduce electric double-decker buses in Thrissur and Kozhikode, KSRTC  Chairman and Managing Director Pramoj Shankar said on Wednesday.
content:
The Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) will introduce electric double-decker buses in Thrissur and Kozhikode, KSRTC  Chairman and Managing Director Pramoj Shankar said on Wednesday.
Mr. Shankar was speaking at a workshop on ‘Driving E-Truck Ecosystem with PM E-DRIVE Scheme’ organised by the Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) in collaboration with the International Council on Clean Transportation (ICTT).
The transport utility already operates e-double-deckers in Thiruvananthapuram city as part of its 165-strong e-bus fleet. The e-bus-based city services in Thiruvananthapuram has helped to reduce air pollution and traffic congestion on city roads.
The KSRTC has also observed a “sharp increase” in passenger patronage of city circular buses, Mr. Shankar said.
He underscored the need for adequate public-friendly charging infrastructure facilities to boost the e-vehicle ecosystem. Transparency and affordability are also vital for a robust EV ecosystem, he said. Mr. Shankar urged public sector institutions to become early adopters of electric vehicle technology.

title: Self-styled YouTube reporter arrested in Shalibanda extortion case
summary: Self-styled YouTube reporter arrested in Shalibanda extortion case
content:
A man who posed as a YouTube reporter and threatened people in the name of police influence was arrested by the Shalibanda police  on Wednesday.
The accused was identified as Mohammed Bilal. He was arrested following a complaint that he demanded ₹35,000 from a "party" by falsely claiming that he could “manage” their case at the police station and prevent their arrest. According to the police, he threatened that failure to pay the amount would result in their immediate arrest and repeatedly intimidated the complainant using this claim.
Based on the evidence collected during the inquiry, the police booked an extortion case against Bilal and arrested him.
South Zone Deputy Commissioner of Police Kiran Khare said the police are noticing a growing trend where people are masquerading as reporters or media persons and indulging in illegal activities such as case settlement, extortion and the collection of  (bribe). He made it clear that such practices would not be tolerated, and strict legal action would be taken against anyone found involved.
The DCP appealed to people to come forward if they have information about such illegal activities or if they are being threatened or extorted in the name of media influence. He assured that the police would ensure prompt action and extend protection to informants.
Further investigation is under way.

title: Basava International Museum work progressing: Minister
summary: Progress on Basava International Museum confirmed by Minister, with civil works completed and plans for advanced multimedia features underway.
content:
Revenue Minister Krisha Byre Gowda told the Legislative Council on Wednesday that the civil works of blocks A, B, C, and F of Basava International Centre had been completed, and the work on the Basava International Museum would be taken up at a cost of ₹10 crore.
Replying to the question of Hanumanth Nirani on the progress of Basava International Centre, Mr. Krishna Byre Gowda said that process of giving administrative approval for D and E block was under way.
“With the completion of all civil works, work on sound and light programme with 3D imaging, multimedia technology, and animatrics will be taken up,” he said.
So far, ₹64.43 crore had been released for the work from Krishna Jal Bhagya Nigam Ltd., and till date, ₹54.82 crore had been utilised for the works. An amount of ₹9.61 crore is ending with the Koodalasangam Development Board, which would be used for the international museum,” he said.
The Minister said works were being undertaken as per the blueprint prepared by the expert committee in consultation with Siddeshwar Swami. He admitted that there had been a delay in executing the works, it would be expedited.

title: Nightclub fire: Goa court remands Luthra brothers in police custody for five days
summary: Goa court remands nightclub owners Luthra brothers in police custody for five days following a deadly fire incident.
content:
A court in North Goa on Wednesday (December 17, 2025) remanded Gaurav and Saurabh Luthra, co-owners of the ‘Birch by Romeo Lane’ nightclub, in police custody for five days.
The brothers, who were brought to Goa from Delhi earlier in the day after being deported from Thailand in connection with the December 6 fire incident that killed 25 persons, were produced in the court after undergoing health check-ups twice at the District Hospital in North Goa.
Judicial Magistrate First Class Mapusa Puja Sardesai remanded the two brothers in police custody for five days.
A team of the Goa Police, along with the Luthra brothers, arrived at the Manohar International Airport, Mopa, in North Goa at 10.45 a.m.
The duo was initially taken to a Primary Health Centre at Siolim for medical examination. They were later taken to the District Hospital at Mapusa.
After their health assessment, the two were produced in the court.
The court directed that the accused be sent for fresh medical examination. Accordingly, the two were again taken to the District Hospital.
Later, they were produced before Judge Sardesai, who ordered the five-day police custody of the accused.
After the fire tragedy at Arpora village, the Anjuna police had registered a case against the Luthra brothers on various charges, including culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
The brothers were arrested in Delhi on Tuesday (December 16, 2025) after being deported from Thailand. A court there allowed the Goa Police their two-day transit remand.
The duo had fled to Phuket in Thailand early on December 7, hours after the fire at their nightclub, prompting the authorities to issue an Interpol Blue Corner Notice and cancel their passports.
They were detained by Thai authorities at Phuket on December 11 following a request from the Indian government, which later coordinated with officials in Thailand to deport them under legal treaties between the two nations.
Five managers and staff members have already been arrested by the Goa Police in connection with the fire.

title: Karnataka to seek relaxation on Centre’s scrap policy for public transport vehicles
summary: Karnataka seeks Central government relaxation on scrap policy for public transport vehicles over 15 years old but in good condition.
content:
Minister for Transport and Muzrai Ramalinga Reddy informed the Legislative Council on Wednesday that Karnataka intends to request the Central government to relax the scrap policy for the public transport vehicles that are in good condition.
Replying to member Govind Raju’s query on age-barred public transport vehicles in the State, Mr. Ramalinga Reddy said that they were planning to write to the Centre on the issue, seeking relaxation for public transport vehicles that had crossed 15 years but were in good condition to operate. Already such exemption had been given in Tamil Nadu, he said.
On scrapping other government vehicles that had crossed 15 years, Mr. Reddy said he would write to the departments concerned and seize such vehicles.
“In the Vahan portal, the Union government has cancelled the registration of 18,552 government vehicles (barring transport vehicles) that were more than 15 years old. So far, only 1,493 vehicles have been scrapped under the Registered Vehicle Scrapping Policy and 17,059 vehicles are to be scrapped,” he said.
Mr. Reddy said that already 3,212 vehicles of the four transport corporations in the State had been scrapped from April 2023 owards and 579 are due for scrapping.

title: Traffic curbs for President’s visit from December 17 to 22
summary: Traffic curbs for President’s visit from December 17 to 22
content:
In view of visit of President Droupadi Murmu, the Hyderabad Traffic Police issued an advisory on  temporary traffic stoppages and diversions at several key junctions across the city between December 17 and 22.
According to the advisory issued by Hyderabad Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic) D. Joel Davis, vehicular movement may be halted briefly or diverted along VIP and VVIP routes during specific time windows on multiple days, as the President undertakes official movements within the city.
On December 17, traffic restrictions are expected between 2 p.m. and 3 p.m. along the stretch connecting Hakimpet Air Force Station Y Junction, Bollarum Check Post, Kowkoor Road, Risala Bazaar, Lakadawala, Down Town, Alwal T Junction, Lothukunta, Lal Bazaar, Trimulgherry X Roads and Karkhana, extending up to NCC.
Similar restrictions will be in place on the morning of December 19, between 9.30 a.m. and 10 a.m., affecting routes from Bison Signal and RSI Circle through Alwal, Trimulgherry and Karkhana, continuing towards Tivoli Plaza, YMCA, Sangeet and Alugaddabavi.
On December 20, traffic diversions are planned in two phases, from 3 p.m. to 4.30 p.m. and again from 5 p.m. to 6.35 p.m., covering a longer corridor that includes Bison Signal, Alwal T junction, Trimulgherry X roads, Begumpet, Panjagutta flyover, Jubilee Hills check post and Road Numbers 45 and 65.
On December 21, commuters may face restrictions between 5 p.m. and 6 p.m. on Begumpet flyover, Rasoolpura, CTO, Tivoli, Karkhana junction, Trimulgherry X roads, Alwal T junction and Bison Signal.
The final set of diversions is scheduled for December 22 between 4 p.m. and 5 p.m., once again affecting routes passing through Hakimpet, Bollarum, Alwal, Trimulgherry and Karkhana.
The traffic police urged citizens to plan their travel in advance and cooperate with personnel deployed on the ground. Commuters can contact the Hyderabad Traffic Police helpline on 9010203626 for real-time updates, while traffic-related inconveniences may also be reported through the department’s official social media platforms.

title: CPI(M) to organise Janadhani Rally on Dec. 21
summary: CPI(M) to host Janadhani Rally on December 21, advocating for farmers' rights and opposing anti-people government policies.
content:
The Communist Party of India (Marxist) will organise a State-level protest called Janadhani Rally in Bengaluru on December 21, demanding redressal of issues concerning farmers, workers and common people and an end to the anti-people policies of the State and Central governments.
Addressing a press conference here on Tuesday, CPI(M) district secretary K. Neela said that the rally will see the participation of over 30,000 farmers, agricultural workers, landless peasants, unorganised sector workers, youth and victims of land acquisition from across the State.
About 2,500 people from Kalaburagi district are expected to take part.
Ms. Neela said that the party has been conducting an intensive State-wide campaign since November 1, with activists visiting thousands of households daily to distribute pamphlets and explain how the anti-people policies of the BJP-led Union government and the Congress-led State government have adversely impacted livelihoods, employment, agriculture, education and healthcare.
She said that the campaign also highlights the people-centric policies implemented by CPI(M)-led governments in Kerala and earlier in West Bengal and Tripura and stresses the need to strengthen alternative Left politics in Karnataka.
Signature campaigns being carried out have received a positive response from the public, she added.
Ms. Neela said that CPI(M) activists in Kalaburagi district alone have visited over 25,000 households, documenting widespread distress, including unemployment, poor implementation of MGNREGA, agrarian crisis, drinking water shortages, basic amenities, mounting debt, corruption, rising inequality and growing communal tensions.
The charter of demands includes a legal guarantee for Minimum Support Price with 50% profit over cost for all crops, withdrawal of land acquisition and labour laws, protection of farmers land, regularisation of contract workers, social security for unorganised labour, filling of vacant government posts, strengthening public education and healthcare, stopping privatisation of essential services, protection of Dalit and minority rights, curbing corruption and safeguarding federalism and democratic rights.
Senior CPI(M) Polit Bureau member U. Vasuki and other State leaders will address a public meeting on December 21 as part of the agitation.

title: PM E-DRIVE scheme: after passenger vehicles, Kerala eyeing freight electrification
summary: Kerala plans to electrify freight transport by establishing e-truck corridors and high-capacity charging infrastructure under the PM E-DRIVE scheme.
content:
Kerala hopes to develop a model electric truck (e-truck) corridor along the National Highway (NH) 66 as part of the State’s efforts to promote freight electrification under the Centre’s PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM E-DRIVE) scheme.
The Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB), in collaboration with the International Council on Clean Transportation (ICTT), organised a workshop here on Wednesday, ‘Driving  E-Truck Ecosystem with PM E-DRIVE Scheme,’ for positioning the State as a frontrunner in this emerging area.
Kerala has a little over three lakh electric vehicles, mostly passenger vehicles, on its roads at present. The State is now in the process of laying the groundwork for establishing high-capacity charging infrastructure and related facilities for e-trucks along freight corridors. Electricity Minister K. Krishnankutty, addressing the workshop, said electrification of trucks and other freight carriers is imperative for controlling carbon emissions and reducing air pollution.
Puneet Kumar, Additional Chief Secretary (Power), who inaugurated the workshop, described freight and logistics as the “next critical frontier” if the State is serious about decarbonisation and long-term sustainability. The ICTT is closely collaborating with the KSEB and its  EV Accelerator Cell to support evidence-based planning in this area, he said.
“This includes corridor-driven charging requirements, grid integration strategies and early pilot designs. This collaboration ensures that Kerala’s approach is data driven, internationally benchmarked and aligned with global best practices while remaining firmly grounded in local operational realities,” Mr. Puneet Kumar said.
While medium and heavy-duty trucks constitute a small share of the vehicles on road, they represent a disproportionately large share of fuel consumption, leading to greenhouse gas emissions, noise and urban air pollution. Multiple life cycle studies have indicated that e-trucks can reduce total greenhouse emissions. This firmly establishes e-trucks as a cornerstone technology for decarbonising freight transport, he said.
“For Kerala, this transition has immediate and local relevance. Our major freight corridors, the NH 66 and key State highways, pass through densely populated and environmentally sensitive regions,” Mr. Puneet Kumar said. India is projected to require approximately 9 Gigawatts (GW) of installed high-capacity charging infrastructure for electric trucks by 2030 and increasing to about 170 GW by 2050. These figures make it clear that freight electrification is not just peripheral, but foundational to India’s net zero transport pathways, he said.
R. Harikumar, director, Energy Management Centre, urged the KSEB to adopt a differentiated incentive strategy for private e-trucks and  Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) e-buses, based on the quality and certainty of electricity demand, in addition to the incentives offered by the PM E-Drive scheme.
Minhaj Alam, Chairman and Managing Director, KSEB; Transport Commissioner Nagaraju Chakilam; Krithika P.R., programme lead, ICTT; Pramoj Shankar, CMD, KSRTC; and KSEB Director Sajeev G. also spoke.

title: ASVV to hold short film/reel-making competition on millets
summary: Join ASVV's millet-themed short film competition; submit entries by December 22 for a chance to win at Millet Mela 2026!
content:
The Anantha Susthira Vyavasaya Vedika (ASVV) is organising a 60-second short film/reel-making competition on millets.
The reels or short film can be made on the topics — growing millets, value addition of millets, cooking/cuisines of millets, consumption and health benefits of millets, and innovative marketing. They can be made in Telugu, Hindi or English and people of all ages can participate, however, each person can submit only one entry in any one language.
The audio-video file has to be in MP4 format and should be sent to milletmela26@gmail.com as an attachment, a release by the ASVV said. The last date for submission of entries is December 22 and the two top entries in each category will be given a token of appreciation at the third edition of Millet Mela to be held in the second week of January 2026. All the reels and short films will be screened at the venue for three days and widely publicised through social media.

title: 80% of pending cases before AC courts disposed of in two and a half years, says Minister
summary: Revenue Minister reports 80% of pending AC court cases resolved in two and a half years, with plans for further reductions.
content:
Revenue Minister Krishna Byre Gowda informed the Legislative Council on Wednesday that 80% of the cases pending before AC (Assistant Commissioner) courts in the State had been disposed of in the last two-and-a-half years and steps had been taken to dispose of the remaining.
Replying to the question by member Ramoji Gowda in the legislative council on Wednesday in order to address the issue of pending cases, the government had appointed 21 Special Assistant Commissioners.
“When this government came to power, there were 37,787 cases that were pending for over five years and 59,339 cases that were pending for more than one year. Following the measures taken by the department, the number of cases with a history of more than five years has been reduced to 3,372, and those pending for over one year have decreased to 10,889 cases. Similarly, there were 10,774 cases before tahsildar courts and now it has been reduced to 506”, he said.
Mr. Krishna Byre Gowda said that although the rules state that AC courts should not keep cases pending for over six months, their number of pending cases, including those over 10-12 years, is due to those concerned not bothering to look into the issue.
Replying to the question of D.S. Arun over the issue of the server regarding the Kaveri 2.0 software, the Minister said that the technical glitches in the digital linking of Kaveri-2.0 and e-swattu had resulted in server issues, and it would be sorted out soon. He sought to clarify that Aadhaar authentication has been made mandatory to prevent misuse and check frauds.

title: Protest today against neglect of Kalaburagi district
summary: Protest in Kalaburagi against government neglect, demanding urgent development and fair opportunities for residents.
content:
Criticising the State government and elected representatives for their neglect towards the development of Kalaburagi district, members of Kalyana Karnataka Kannadapara Sanghatanegala Okkutta demanded that they take up development works in the district immediately.
Addressing a press conference here on Tuesday, okkutta leaders Manjunath Nalwarkar and Sachin Farhatabad said that despite the Kalyana Karnataka Region Development Board (KKRDB) receiving substantial funds under Article 371(J), Kalaburagi city has not benefited adequately even in terms of basic infrastructure.
Expressing concern over the sudden suspension of flight services from Kalaburagi Airport, Mr. Nalwarkar said that the airport is crucial for trade and industries and questioned the silence of Ministers, MLAs, MPs from the Kalyana Karnataka region over the suspension of flight services and demanded their immediate resumption.
Mr. Nalwarkar said that street vendors in major market areas continued to face hardship due to the failure of the authorities to provide designated vending zones with basic infrastructure.
The okkutta further accused Medical Education Minister Sharanprakash Patil of favouring candidates from Sedam taluk in recruitments to Jayadeva Hospital, Trauma Care Centre and GIMS Hospital and demanded fair employment opportunities for residents of Kalaburagi city.
The okkutta will stage a protest in Kalaburagi city on Thursday demanding that these issues be addressed immediately.

title: National Tourism Mart in Visakhapatnam on February 13, 14
summary: Join industry leaders at the National Tourism Mart-2026 in Visakhapatnam on February 13-14 to boost domestic tourism.
content:
Andhra Pradesh Minister for Tourism, Culture, and Cinematography Kandula Durgesh on Wednesday announced that the State government, in collaboration with the Association of Domestic Tour Operators of India (ADTOI), would organise a two-day National Tourism Mart-2025 in Visakhapatnam on February 13 and 14, 2026.
To facilitate rapid growth of domestic tourism, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed in the presence of senior officials from the Tourism Department and representatives of ADTOI.
The Minister said the proposed event would serve as a platform to showcase the State’s coastal tourism, spiritual circuits, heritage monuments, eco-adventure tourism, and agency (tribal) area tourism at a national level.
Prominent tour operators, hotel owners, destination promoters, tourism stakeholders, and travel experts from across the country would participate in the mart.
Mr. Durgesh said the B2B networking sessions, destination presentations, business meetings, panel discussions, and familiarisation trips to tourist spots would enable the local tourism stakeholders to establish direct business linkages with national level players, and expressed hope that the initiative would help increase tourist footfall, improve local employment opportunities, foster long-term business relations and secure national-level recognition for the State.
Representatives of ADTOI said their mission was to strengthen domestic tourism, promote and bring lesser-known tourist destinations in the State to light, and ensure sustainable tourism growth and employment for local communities.
Expressing happiness for partnering with the Andhra Pradesh government, they said it was committed to working with national associations to achieve responsible and comprehensive tourism growth.
The programme was attended by Special Secretary of Tourism Ajay Jain, Managing Director of AP Tourism Development Corporation and CEO of AP Tourism Authority Amrapali Kata, Deputy CEO of APTA Srinivas, AP State Creativity and Culture Commission Chairperson Tejaswi Podapati, Communication Officer S. Padma Rani, ADTOI president Ved Khanna, vice-president Ashish, Travel Mart CEO Vijay Mohan and others.

title: Palace flower show from December 21; green fireworks to usher in New Year at Mysuru Palace
summary: Experience the vibrant Palace Flower Show at Mysuru Palace from December 21-31, featuring stunning floral displays and cultural events.
content:
The Mysuru Palace will host the Palace Flower Show–2025 from December 21 to December 31, promising visitors a vibrant blend of floriculture, art, culture and heritage. The 10-day event will be inaugurated on December 21 at 4 p.m.
The flower show will be open daily from 10 a.m. to 9 p.m. More than 25,000 ornamental flower pots representing 35 varieties will be displayed, along with nearly four lakh cut flowers, including roses, chrysanthemums, carnations, gerberas, orchids, anthuriums, lilies and other exotic species.
A major attraction will be a grand floral replica of the Sringeri Sharada Peetham, measuring about 50 ft in width, 16 ft in depth and 25 ft in height. Several elaborate floral installations depicting mythological, cultural and contemporary themes will also be showcased.
Special arrangements include floral portraits of erstwhile Mysuru kings and prominent historical personalities, depictions of Krishna and Radha on a swing, displays highlighting India’s sporting achievements, including the victories of women cricketers, and creative installations of birds, animals and cartoon characters to engage children.
An image of environmentalist Saalumarada Thimmakka will be created using flowers and millets, depicting a tree in recognition of her contribution to tree planting. Another highlight will be the Preamble, designed in the form of a book and decorated with flowers.
The entry and exit gates will be artistically decorated using flowers and eco-friendly materials. Classical instrumental music performances will be held during visiting hours, while cultural programmes at the Palace premises are scheduled from December 21 to 25 between 5 p.m. and 9.30 p.m. The palace will be illuminated every evening from 7 p.m. to 9 p.m.
On December 31, a police band performance will be held from 11 p.m. to midnight, followed by a silent, eco-friendly fireworks display to welcome the New Year.
In addition, a photo and video exhibition showcasing the history of Mysuru, Dasara celebrations and the Wadiyar dynasty will be organised within the palace premises. A special bomme (doll) exhibition featuring traditional themes will also be part of the event.
The annual flower show is expected to attract many tourists who usually plan their visits to Mysuru to spend Christmas holidays and celebrate the New Year. In the previous years, the palace attracted a large number of tourists during the flower show, which has become a popular year-end event.

title: Gruha Lakshmi: ₹2,123 crore released to women beneficiaries in Mandya
summary: ₹2,123 crore disbursed to 4,61,599 women in Mandya under the Gruha Lakshmi scheme, ensuring timely support and financial assistance.
content:
A total of ₹2,123 crore has been released to 4,61,599 women beneficiaries in Mandya district under the Gruha Lakshmi scheme through 23 instalments since the launch of the programme.
Chikkalingaiah, chairman of the Mandya District-Level Authority for Implementation of Guarantee Schemes, said that payments  had been credited up to August.
Presiding over a meeting of the district-level authority at the Zilla Panchayat on December 17, he said that ₹92.98 crore was disbursed in August alone. Amounts due from September onwards will be released soon through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), and beneficiaries need not worry about delays, he added.
Mr. Chikkalingaiah clarified that Gruha Lakshmi assistance had not been credited to income tax and GST payers and urged officials to submit representations for the early release of pending payments.
He also pointed out that some beneficiaries had not received funds owing to non-completion of Aadhaar seeding and e-KYC, and asked officials to create awareness among the public to complete the formalities.
Under the Anna Bhagya scheme, Mandya district has 4,47,166 beneficiaries. From July 2023 to December 2024, ₹402.6 crore was paid to beneficiaries as rice had not been procured. From February 2025, rice distribution resumed through fair price shops. More than 8,000 income tax and GST payers in the district have been shifted from the Below Poverty Line to Above Poverty Line category, he said.
Prashanth Babu K.C., vice-chairman of the district-level authority, said that under the Shakti scheme, 18,03,04,248 women had availed free bus travel in the district between June 2023 and November 2025. This incurred an expenditure of ₹492.93 crore. He stressed the need to improve bus services on the Bengaluru–Mysuru route to ensure there are no inconveniences to genuine passengers, students, and college-goers.
As many as 4,98,144 beneficiaries have been covered in the district under the Gruha Jyothi scheme. From August 2023 to November 2025, a total of 549.17 million units of electricity were consumed, with ₹491.19 crore released as subsidy, he added.
Rajendra S.H., vice-chairman of the district-level authority, said that under the Yuva Nidhi scheme, 8,296 beneficiaries had registered in the district, with ₹19.29 crore released up to September 2025. Payments for October will be made soon. Training is also being provided to youth under the Yuva Nidhi Plus scheme.

title: Venkata Ratna Srinivas appointed Managing Director of newly-formed SPV for Amaravati development
summary: Sonti Venkata Ratna Srinivas appointed Managing Director of Amaravati Growth and Infrastructure Corporation to lead key development projects.
content:
The Andhra Pradesh government has appointed retired IAS officer Sonti Venkata Ratna Srinivas as Managing Director of the newly-formed Amaravati Growth and Infrastructure Corporation Limited (AGICL), a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) created to steer high-impact development projects in the Amaravati capital city and region.
The appointment was made through G.O. Rt. No. 1478 issued by S. Suresh Kumar, Principal Secretary, Municipal Administration and Urban Development, on December 16, 2025, along with delegation of powers to enable the corporation to function with operational autonomy.
The AGICL is the third organisation constituted by the State government for the development of futuristic world-class capital city, apart from the existing Andhra Pradesh Capital Region Development Authority (APCRDA), which acts as local urban unit, and the Amaravati Development Corporation (ADC), for infra development.
AGICL has been established under the Companies Act, 2013, in line with the earlier G.O.s aimed at accelerating planned growth in Amaravati. The corporation’s board consists of the Principal Secretary to the MA&UD Department as Non-Executive Chairman and five Directors.
The first board meeting held on December 2, 2025, adopted key resolutions, including the recommendation to appoint a full-time Managing Director to oversee the planning, execution and management of special projects.
Retired IAS officer Sonti Venkata Ratna Srinivas. 
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                File Photo
As per the G.O., the Managing Director has been vested with wide-ranging responsibilities. These include preparing Detailed Development Plans for special projects based on the approved master plan, designing and implementing projects, and operating and maintaining city-level services, subject to APCRDA approval.
The Managing Director is also authorised to select developers, contractors and operators, collect development charges, lease rentals and user charges, and mobilise financial resources from the market in addition to government funding.
The powers further extend to developing trunk infrastructure, providing transport, power, water supply, solid waste management, and ICT services in common areas, either directly or through public-private partnership models on smart city principles.
The AGICL will also facilitate social infrastructure such as healthcare, education, sports and entertainment, engage professional expertise from the market, and build capabilities to function as a world-class public agency for Amaravati’s special projects.
The move signals renewed focus on structured development, say officials.

title: Tripura jailbreak: Most wanted absconder arrested after three months
summary: Tripura Police arrest Sunil Debbarma, the most wanted fugitive from a recent jailbreak, while two inmates remain at large.
content:
Tripura Police have arrested the fourth fugitive three months after the jailbreak in the State in October last. Sunil Debbarma was captured from his home at Melaghar in Sepahijala district late on Tuesday night.
Sunil Debbarma was the most wanted among the escapees as he had been convicted of murder and other serious crimes and was serving a life sentence.
Six inmates, including five undertrials and one convict, had escaped from the Dharmanagar sub-jail in north Tripura district on October 1. One of them, Narayan Chandra Dutta, is a Bangladeshi national.
They fled the jail after assaulting the gate sentry and some jail wardens.
Three of the escapees, including the Bangladeshi national, were arrested within a few days of the incident. After the arrest of Sunil Debbarma, two more jail inmates remain absconding.
Police said Sunil Debbarma was arrested in a raid based on specific tip-offs. He was produced before a court on Wednesday and remanded for interrogation.

title: Preachings in Tirupati govt. polytechnic: students allege they were taken out for prayers
summary: Students at Tirupati Polytechnic allege mandatory religious trips and preachings by faculty, sparking protests and investigations.
content:
New revelations have come out in the recent incidence of a contract lecturer allegedly delivering religious preachings at Sri Venkateswara Government Polytechnic (SVGP) in Tirupati.
After the video of English lecturer G.V. Madhavi writing preachings on the classroom board went viral on social media, Hindu organisations had organised protests in front of the college, which led to the management launching an investigation and placing her under suspension.
In fact, it was less than a month ago that the students had formally submitted a complaint to principal Dwarakanath Reddy against the lecturer, stating that she was not teaching them the subjects. In a letter signed by more than two dozen students, a copy of which is available withThe Hindu, the students also expressed fear of being failed in the ensuing examinations.
The students alleged that the teacher delivering religious preachings was not an isolated incident. They also shared proofs that senior officials were involved in a series of other incidents.
According to sources, a senior government official in the rank of Regional Joint Director had allegedly arranged a bus on December 8 to take nearly 200 students on a mandatory trip to a religious place of worship and reportedly made them participate in the prayers.
“It is a direct attack on the secular spirit of the Constitution and a violation of the basic rights of students. Also, it runs against the code of conduct for public servants and mocks the rules of the Department of Technical Education,” said Cheenepalli Kiran Kumar, president of Sanatana Dharma Parirakshana Samithi, who led a demonstration in front of the polytechnic.
In the representation submitted to the Principal, the Samithi demanded punitive action on the erring teachers and officials to prevent recurrence of such incidents.

title: Carvalho at Lalbagh: R-Day flower show to celebrate the life and works of K.P. Poornachandra Tejaswi
summary: Lalbagh Botanical Garden will host its annual Republic Day flower show from January 15 to 26, with this edition paying tribute to the life and literary legacy of celebrated Kannada writer and thinker K.P. Poornachandra Tejaswi.
content:
Lalbagh Botanical Garden will host its annual Republic Day flower show from January 15 to 26, with this edition paying tribute to the life and literary legacy of celebrated Kannada writer and thinker K.P. Poornachandra Tejaswi.
The theme has been chosen with the objective of familiarising younger audiences and visitors from outside the State with Tejaswi’s work and commemorating more than 45 years since the publication of his iconic novelCarvalho, Horticulture Department officials said.
“To ensure that the theme is reflected meaningfully in the floral installations, the department is reaching out to literary scholars, writers and others closely familiar with Tejaswi’s life and work. Their inputs will help in conceptualising displays that go beyond decorative value and narrate aspects of the author’s ideas, characters and worldview, making the experience more informative for students and first-time readers,” M. Jagadeesh, Joint Director of Horticulture (Parks & Gardens) at Lalbagh Botanical Garden, toldThe Hindu.
Officials highlighted that Tejaswi’s writing continues to resonate across generations because of its creative writing style, scientific temper, and deep engagement with nature and society. His books are still widely read, not just in Karnataka but also by readers from outside the State.Carvalho, in particular, has attracted attention as a Kannada science fiction novel that blends scientific inquiry with the ecology of the Western Ghats. The novel traces a scientist’s search for a flying lizard, a narrative that has remained relevant for its imaginative approach and remains one of Tejaswi’s most discussed works.
Mr. Jagadeesh added that the department is currently finalising the budget and working on new design concepts to avoid repetition and to draw greater interest, particularly from younger visitors. “Along with the traditional display of seasonal flowers, efforts are being made to source new and rare varieties from different parts of the country and select international locations. These will be showcased through innovative layouts and thematic structures so that visitors have a fresh visual experience rather than a mere change in theme,” he said.
This year’s flower show will also be the first to be held after the introduction of electric bicycles and tricycles within Lalbagh. The officials attached to the park said that this is expected to enhance visitor experience while also generating additional revenue for the department.

title: Youth stabbed to death in drunken brawl in Balapur
summary: Youth stabbed to death in drunken brawl in Balapur
content:
A late-night drunken brawl claimed the life of a 20-year-old scrap picker in Royal Colony, Balapur, in the early hours of Wednesday.
The deceased was identified as Murshid Alam, a resident of Royal Colony. Police said Murshid and the accused, 18-year-old Abdullah, who also works as a scrap picker and lives in the same locality, were drunk when an argument erupted over a trivial issue.
According to Balapur Inspector M. Sudhakar, the quarrel quickly escalated, prompting Abdullah to go to his house and return with a knife. He allegedly attacked Murshid, inflicting fatal injuries and killing him on the spot, before fleeing the scene.
The incident was reported at around 1.45 a.m., following which the Balapur police rushed to the spot and shifted the body for postmortem examination.
A case has been registered, and efforts are underway to trace the accused.

title: Zoo tigress ‘Thayamma’ ailing, undergoing treatment
summary: Mysuru Zoo's tigress Thayamma is receiving treatment after exhibiting health issues and refusing food, veterinarians closely monitoring her.
content:
Thayamma, a tigress at the Sri Chamarajendra Zoological Gardens, Mysuru, has been undergoing treatment after showing signs of ill health.
Zoo authorities said on December 17 that the wild cat, aged about four years and 10 months, was rescued from the Bandipur forest and brought to the zoo on March 28, 2021. She had recently stopped taking food and is being closely monitored by the zoo’s veterinary team, they said.
Veterinarians are administering appropriate treatment and keeping a constant watch on her condition, a note from zoo said.

title: Maintenance of RO plants has become difficult in rural areas, says Minister
summary: Minister Priyank Kharge highlights challenges in maintaining popular RO plants in rural areas, urging a systematic solution for sustainability.
content:
Though the RO water plants of the government are becoming popular in rural areas, it is becoming difficult for the government to manage them, according to Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department Minister Priyank Kharge.
Disclosing this while replying to Congress member U.B. Banakar during Question Hour in the Assembly, Mr. Kharge noted that RO plants were being put up by various agencies, including the private ones, through CSR funds. While some of them had made arrangements for their regular maintenance, most of them did not have such arrangements. This had become difficult for the village panchayats who were entrusted with the responsibility of maintaining them, he explained.
He said the RDPR Department was trying to put in a system for their maintenance. A blue print in this regard was being prepared to ensure permanent solution for their maintenance.
“We are talking to several firms that manufacture RO plants to know if they could take up maintenance of the public RO plants in rural areas. While they are ready to sell their products to us, they are not ready to take up maintenance work,” he said.

title: Large parts of North Karnataka may see cold wave-like conditions
summary: North Karnataka faces a cold wave, with temperatures dropping significantly below normal from December 19 to 23, warns KSNDMC.
content:
The Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre (KSNDMC) has forecast cold wave-like conditions across large parts of North Interior Karnataka between December 19 and 23, with minimum temperatures likely to drop significantly below normal levels.
According to an extreme weather index forecast issued by the KSNDMC on Wednesday evening, minimum temperatures across North Interior Karnataka and South Interior Karnataka are expected to be 4 degrees Celsius to 6 degrees Celsius below normal during the period.
Severe cold wave conditions are likely to prevail over some places in North Interior Karnataka, particularly on December 20 and 21.
The alert also stated that some areas in the Malnad region may experience minimum temperatures 4 degrees Celsius to 6 degrees Celsius below normal between December 20 and 23, while coastal Karnataka is likely to see a fall of 2 degrees Celsius to 3 degrees Celsius below normal from December 20 to 22.
Daily weather observations indicate that North Karnataka has already begun experiencing a sharp dip in night temperatures.
Bidar district recorded an average minimum temperature of 11.6 degrees Celsius during the 24-hour period ended at 8.30 a.m. on Wednesday, the lowest in the State.
Parts of Bidar, Kalaburagi, Vijayapura, Raichur, and Koppal districts recorded minimum temperatures in the range of 8 degrees Celsius to 10 degrees Celsius, according to KSNDMC data.
Kalaburagi district recorded a minimum temperature of 12.9 degrees Celsius, while Vijayapura registered 14.4 degrees Celsius and Raichur 16.1 degrees Celsius during the same period.
KSNDMC noted that nearly 80% of the State recorded minimum temperatures between 14 degrees Celsius and 20 degrees Celsius, indicating widespread cooling conditions.
KSNDMC has advised residents, particularly the elderly, children and outdoor workers, to take precautions during the cold spell, including minimising exposure to cold winds and ensuring adequate winter clothing.
Farmers have also been advised to take protective measures for crops and livestock to prevent cold injury during the period.

title: TPCC chief hails GP poll verdict
summary: TPCC chief hails GP poll verdict
content:
HYDERABAD
Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) president and MLC Mahesh Kumar Goud expressed happiness that the Congress party’s dominance continued in the results of the third phase of the 2025 Panchayat elections
In a statement issued here on Wednesday, Mr. Goud stated that the villages once again crowned the Congress party with victory. He opined that the verdict given by the people stands as clear evidence of the performance of the Congress government.
He said that Congress-backed candidates securing massive victories in the highest number of Sarpanch posts across the State in the third phase of elections is a clear reflection of the rural voters’ confidence in the governance of the Congress government.
The TPCC chief remarked that the results of the third phase of Panchayat elections have come as a slap in the face of Opposition parties and are a signal of a clear change in rural politics in Telangana. He clarified that the Congress party took the Panchayat elections very seriously, and that strong, well-coordinated campaign strategies were the main reason behind this victory.
He said that the campaign, which brought ministers, MPs, MLAs and local leaders onto a single platform and extended down to the village level with effective coordination, turned decisively in favour of the Congress party.
The TPCC Chief said that this verdict, which mirrors the aspirations of the people, once again proves the satisfaction among rural citizens with the governance of the Congress government.
He said that the approach of directly engaging with people and striving to resolve their problems is strengthening the party.

title: School’s NSS unit collects coconut shells to support cancer patients
summary: Students from SNDP school collected 500 kg of coconut shells, raising ₹12,500 to aid travel expenses for cancer patients.
content:
Members of the National Service Scheme (NSS) unit of the Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam Vocational Higher Secondary School at Adimaly, Idukki, have completed a novel initiative to extend support to cancer patients. Under the month-long initiative Coconut Shell Challenge, students collected coconut shells and brought them to the school, where they were procured by an Ernakulam-based company. “The challenge aimed at nurturing eco-friendly habits among students while encouraging them to participate in social service. During the period the students collected over 500 kg of coconut shells and earned ₹12,500,” said said NSS Programme Officer Ajai B.
“Travel expense to hospitals is a major burden for cancer patients. The entire amount will be used for travel and other expenses for cancer patients and those under palliative care,” he said.
In 2024, the NSS unit had provided Onam kits to patients under palliative care by selling e-waste.

title: S.N. Hegde, ex-Vice-Chancellor of University of Mysore, passes away
summary: S.N. Hegde, former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mysore, has passed away at 83 in Mysuru.
content:
S.N. Hegde, former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mysore (UoM), passed away in Mysuru on December 17. He was 83.
Mr. Hegde, who was a professor of zoology, served as the Vice-Chancellor for two terms, from 1997 to 2003.
He passed away at a private hospital in Mysuru. His last rites will be held after the arrival of his daughter from abroad, according to sources.
Meanwhile, H.A. Venkatesh, former chairperson of Mysuru Paints and Varnishes, has condoled the demise.
In a statement, he said he had the privilege of serving as a member of UoM’s Senate and Syndicate during Prof. Hegde’s tenure as Vice-Chancellor. “He always expressed well-informed opinions on matters concerning the Karnataka State Universities Act, 2000, and was an effective speaker on public platforms,” Mr. Venkatesh said.
He added that Prof. Hegde had worked as a professor and researcher at Mangalore University.

title: Murder of Constitution and democracy: BJP
summary: Murder of Constitution and democracy: BJP
content:
Telangana BJP has accused the Congress party of ‘murdering’ the Constitution and democracy by influencing the Speaker’s decision on the defection of MLAs’ issue.
Party president N. Ramchander Rao, in a press statement  on Wednesday, said that the Speaker’s decision to dismiss the applications against the defected MLAs has been ‘expected’ as it has been ‘influenced by the party’ and a ‘diktat’ of the party leadership.
“It is against the Constitution which the Congress claims to protect. The decision has exposed the party as it does not even respect their own leader Rajiv Gandhi who brought forth the Anti-Defection Law,” he attested, and pointed out that those leaders moving with Constitution in their pockets had gone against it.
Earlier, Mr. Rao told the media that the Congress party is deliberately creating ‘unnecessary’ political controversy over the change in the name of MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act), even though the scheme is only being strengthened to benefit more poor people.
The Centre is inspired by Mahatma Gandhi’s vision ofGram Swarajand the concept ofRam Rajyain Indian culture, and the BJP-led Central Government has introduced the ‘Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Grameen) OR (VB-GRAM-G) in line with the goal ofViksit Bharat 2047for rural development, he said.
It was the Modi government that made MGNREGA truly beneficial for the rural poor by providing employment opportunities, spending more than ₹8 lakh crore in the last 11 years compared to just about ₹1 lakh crore during Congress rule, claimed the BJP leader. Mr. Rao questioned why the Congress is making a big issue out of the name change when even the Telangana Mother statue was renamed without controversy.
In a separate statement, chief spokesperson N.V. Subash strongly condemned the Congress party for staging protests against the Centre’s new rural development initiative, describing them as “politically motivated, deceptive, and steeped in hypocrisy”.

title: Virajpet schoolboy loses finger in firecracker mishap
summary: A Virajpet schoolboy loses a finger in a firecracker accident.
content:
A schoolboy lost a finger after attempting to light an unexploded firecracker at Kaikeri in Virajpet taluk of Kodagu district.
The injured boy has been identified as 14-year-old Pavan, a Class 7 student and a native of Devarapura Paisari. He was visiting his relatives at Kaikeri when he picked up an unexploded firecracker lying outside and tried to set it off. The firecracker accidentally exploded in his left hand, causing injuries.
Pavan was immediately shifted to the district hospital in Madikeri, where doctors said all his fingers were seriously injured. One finger had to be amputated, while the remaining fingers were surgically treated.
Upon receiving information about the incident, Rajiv Gandhi Panchayat Raj Organisation district president Thenniyar Maina visited the hospital and informed Virajpet MLA and Chief Minister’s Legal Adviser A.S. Ponnanna, who was attending the Belagavi session of the legislature.
Mr. Ponnanna directed officials to ensure that the boy is provided proper treatment free of cost. He also instructed the District Surgeon to refer the child to hospitals in Mysuru or Mangaluru if advanced treatment is required.

title: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu insists on adopting best practices in governance
summary: Chandrababu Naidu emphasizes best governance practices to boost Andhra Pradesh's growth, focusing on water, employment, and agriculture productivity.
content:
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has expressed confidence that the State can achieve 17.11% growth rate, with focus on optimum utilisation of water resources, employment generation, increasing agriculture productivity through adoption of modern technologies wherever required, expanding manufacturing, and realising the full potential of the fisheries sector.
Best practices in governance should be implemented from the district level to provide better administration so that people would be satisfied, Mr. Naidu exhorted the officials while delivering the inaugural speech at the two-day Collectors’ conference that began at the Secretariat on Wednesday.
Proper planning was essential, he said, and noted that Andhra Pradesh, which used to compete with Telangana, had fallen to the last position in South India due to the previous government’s policies.s
Mr. Naidu further said that “speed of delivering governance” was crucial, and the people’s representatives play a significant role in realising the objectives.
He said feedback was being obtained from the public, and unless the issues raised by them were promptly sorted out and their problems solved, the government would not be able to make meaningful progress.
The government was constantly monitoring the Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to make necessary course corrections, the Chief Minister noted, suggesting that this would be possible only when officials from the grassroots level up to the Collectors discharged their duties effectively.
Mr. Naidu stressed the need for a proper work culture in the government, wherein the officials should clear the files promptly so that the administration would be smooth. A situation in which files were forwarded to others without resolving them was prevalent in the Revenue Department. This should change, as otherwise people would face difficulties, he said, and ordered that decisions be taken through data-driven governance.
The government revived several Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) that had become defunct due to the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) government’s negligence, Mr. Naidu said. Central funds given for CSS that remained unspent should be spent by January 15, 2026.
Of the ₹24,513 crore sanctioned for various CSS, ₹6,252 crore was not spent. Notably, only 38% of funds under the PMAY were expended. The Centre would provide an additional ₹5,000 crore to ₹6,000 crore upon full utilisation of the funds under existing schemes, the Chief Minister said, calling upon the Collectors to act as the “government’s ambassadors” and earn good name for it.
Mr. Naidu said the government gave equal importance to development and welfare, and fulfilled all major promises given to the people in the run-up to the 2024 elections. Investments worth ₹11.20 lakh crore were secured at the CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam last month as the State’s brand image had been resurrected by the coalition government, he asserted.
Asserting that the medical colleges being built under the PPP model would function as government colleges and be regulated by the government, the Chief Minister said it was wrong to say that these colleges were in the process of being privatised.
“The YSRCP government had mobilised loans at high interest rates (up to 14%), thereby causing tremendous strain on the State’s finances. We are now easing that burden by rescheduling the loans,” Mr. Naidu pointed out.
Further, he called for preparation of short, medium (five years) and long-term (10 to 15 years) plans for the agriculture sector covering three seasons, and major investments in horticulture for which there was tremendous potential in the Rayalaseema region.
Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan, Ministers N. Lokesh, A. Satya Prasad, K. Atchannaidu, N.Md. Farooq and K. Ravindra, Chief Secretary K. Vijayanand, and Director General of Police Harish Kumar Gupta were among those present.

title: Three-day international conference on interdisciplinary sciences at Newman College
summary: Join the three-day international conference at Newman College, exploring advances in interdisciplinary sciences and fostering global collaboration.
content:
Newman College, Thodupuzha, will host a three-day international conference on “Advances in Interdisciplinary Sciences and Technology” from Friday to Sunday.
A. Ajayaghosh, S.S. Bhatnagar Chair at SRM Institute of Science and Technology and former Director of CSIR-National Institute For Interdisciplinary Science and Technology (NIIST) Thiruvananthapuram, will be the chief guest and keynote speaker. Sabu Thomas, chairperson of the Trivandrum Engineering Science & Technology Research Park and former Vice-Chancellor of Mahatma Gandhi University, will lead a session titled “How to write a high-impact publication.”
The gathering will feature 15 invited speakers from nine countries. Additionally, more than 100 delegates will participate in oral presentations, providing a platform for knowledge exchange and fostering innovation across scientific disciplines.
“The convergence of researchers, academicians, and students from around the world is expected to create valuable opportunities for networking and collaborative research initiatives,” an official said.
The conference is supported by several prominent organisations, including the Government of India’s Department of Biotechnology, Kerala State Council for Science, Technology and Environment, National Academy of Sciences India (Kerala Chapter), American Chemical Society, and the Royal Society of Chemistry.

title: A political parody set to the tune of an Ayyappa devotional song triggers controversy in Kerala
summary: A political parody set to an Ayyappa song ignites controversy in Kerala, prompting police investigation into alleged religious offense.
content:
A political parody set to the tune of a popular Ayyappa devotional song has sparked controversy in Kerala.
The song weaves lyrics lampooning the Left Democratic Front (LDF) government over the Sabarimala gold theft scandal in the tune of a catchy devotional melody profoundly familiar to Ayyappa devotees. During the local body campaign trail, the United Democratic Front (UDF) Opposition had deployed the song as an arguably surefire propaganda tool to cast the government under a harsh light.
The dispute erupted on Tuesday after the Pathanamthitta-based Thiruvabharana Patha Samrakshana Samiti, an organisation closely associated with the tradition of the Sabarimala Ayyappa temple, sought a criminal investigation into, what it termed, a wilful and conspiratorial trespass on faith.
State Police Chief Ravada A. Chandrasekhar forwarded the complaint to Additional Director General of Police, Law and Order and Crime Branch, H. Venkatesh.
An official said, prima facie, the parody song seemed to walk a fine line between artistic freedom and the alleged attempt to outrage religious sentiments.
