The police have reportedly sought legal opinion on the matter and launched a preliminary investigation to verify whether the samiti’s complaint reveals a cognisable offence.
Matters later took a sharp political turn when Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] Pathanamthitta district secretary Raju Abraham endorsed the complaint. He accused the Congress and the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) of using the song to polarise communities on religious lines at the polling booth. He said the CPI(M) would move the Election Commission of India (EC) against the UDF’s alleged bid to use religious symbols to create tensions between people of different faiths for electoral dividends.
CPI(M) leader A.A. Rahim, MP, claimed that the Opposition added insult to injury by rendering the “offending” song outside Parliament. He said the LDF would highlight the UDF’s alleged trespass on the Ayyappa faith at the national level.
In a post on Facebook, Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) vice-president V.T. Balram accused the CPI(M) of weaponising the artists’ identities to stoke communal resentment. He wrote that the CPI(M), resentful of the government’s humbling defeat in the local body polls, was treading a perilous path by injecting communal venom into a run-of-the-mill political parody piece.
Leader of the Opposition V.D. Satheesan riposted that the CPI(M) outmatched the Sangh Parivar in driving divisive religious majoritarian sentiment by casting a harmless parody song as a slur on the Ayyappa faith. He said the CPI(M) had borrowed memorable devotional song tunes to lampoon political rivals in the past.
All India Congress Committee (AICC) general secretary K.C. Venugopal, MP, said the CPI(M) lacked grace in defeat and was creating controversy for political face-saving.

title: Surprise check in Mysuru Central Prison yields mobile phones and SIM cards
summary: A surprise inspection at Mysuru Central Prison uncovers banned mobile phones and SIM cards, prompting police action and further investigations.
content:
A surprise check carried out by officials in Mysuru Central Prison on December 16 has yielded a total of nine mobile phones, 11 SIM cards, two mobile chargers, and one charging cable.
According to Mysuru Central Prison Senior Superintendent V. Seshumurthy, the surprise inspection  was carried out between 10.55 p.m. on December 16 and 1 a.m. on December 17.
Jail officials and staff conducted the inspection under the guidance of the Chief Superintendent.
The seized mobile phones, SIM cards, chargers, and charging cable constituted banned items and were handed over to the jurisdictional Mandi police station. Mr. Seshumurthy said a case has been registered.
Meanwhile, Alok Kumar, Director General of Police (DGP), Prisons and Correctional Services, Bengaluru, arrived at Mysuru Central Prison on December 17 as a surprise visit.
He appreciated the jail staff for conducting a surprise check and announced a prize of ₹30,000 for them, Mr. Seshumurthy said.
Mr. Kumar also led a search operation in the jail premises after his arrival. However, the two-hour search  did not yield anything.
He told reporters that the night search operation on December 16, which had continued till the wee hours of December 17, was part of a special drive taken up by the Prisons Department across the State.
During his visit to Mysuru Central Prison, the DGP said he interacted with inmates as well as the jail staff. Upon hearing their grievances, he promised to make efforts to redress these.
Mr. Kumar’s visit also comes close on the heels of an attempt to supply ganja to a prison inmate by concealing the narcotic substance inside clothes. Ganja, in the form of paste, was packed in carbon paper and placed in two pairs of pants that were to be handed over to the undertrial prison. However, the ganja was detected after Karnataka State Industrial Security Force personnel assigned for security at the entrance examined the clothes.
The DGP also referred to other attempts to supply ganja to inmates and expressed confidence that the local police will investigate the matter and bust the racket involving people inside the jail and outside.
Pointing to the attempts made to throw ganja and other banned items into the jail premises, Mr. Kumar said an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based Intrusion Detection System will be installed in Mysuru Central Prison on a trial basis.
The system will also be installed in the prisons at Bengaluru and Belagavi on a trial basis.

title: Watch | These tribal kids in a 12-hour school will amaze you | Pulse Maharashtra
summary: This exceptional Zilla Parishad school in Hiwali, a tribal hamlet in Tryambakeshwar taluka of Nashik, runs 12 hours a day, 365 days a year, without vacations or weekends. Modelled as a ‘tourism school’, it blends academics with vocational training in agriculture, Warli painting, and computing. Students travel up to 22 km to attend and display extraordinary skills, including ambidextrous writing, reciting the Constitution, advanced math, and strong English reading abilities. With zero dropouts and halted migration, the school has transformed the community. However, water scarcity and electricity outages threaten its progress, prompting urgent appeals for solar power and a small dam.

title: State writes to Centre on electric buses; says trip cancellation 3 times more compared to diesel ones
summary: State raises concerns to Centre over electric buses' performance, highlighting threefold trip cancellations compared to diesel buses.
content:
The State government has raised concerns with the Union government regarding the performance of GCC (Gross Cost Contract) operators who are entrusted with  the deployment and operation of electric buses in Bengaluru.
Replying to member Ivan D’souza in the Legislative Council on Wednesday, Minister for Transport and Muzrai Ramalinga Reddy said that he had already written to Union Minister for Heavy Industries H.D. Kumaraswamy as the poor performance of the electric buses would not only cause hardships to the passengers, but also bring bad name to both the governments and the BMTC.
In his letter to Mr. Kumaraswmay, Mr. Reddy has pointed out that the performance of operators under GCC, predominantly OEMs such as NTPC Vidyut Vyapra Nigam, Tata Motors Limited, Switch Mobility and their associated operating entity, OHM Global Mobility, had fallen significantly short of the standards expected from industry leaders of their stature.
“The operators have failed to address issues such as lack of structural and rigorous driver training, poor maintenance, cancellations, breakdowns, batter issues and insufficient driver preparedness which led to rise in road accidents and repeated flash strikes. This apart, compared to the performance of BMTC’s conventional diesel fleet, the disparity in operational reliability under the GCC electric bus contracts is both stark and deeply concerning. The electric buses operated by the GCC operators are witnessing nearly 3 times the number of cancellations compared with the diesel counterparts,” Mr. Reddy has said in the letter.
BMTC presently operates 65,000 trips each day with 7,067 buses (5,423 powered by diesel and 1,644 representing the electric fleet). However despite operating on a vast scale, the diesel buses had a record of having accidents of  just 0.05 per lakh km of operation , while the electric buses exhibit a higher accident rate of 0.07 per lakh km, resulting in tarnishing the image of the organisation, Mr Reddy said in the letter.
The Minister urged the Union Minister for early intervention to ensure regular performance review of GCC operators, incorporate binding clauses in future tender documents mandating comprehensive and certified driver training protocols and institute a compliance monitoring mechanism jointly undertaken by State transport utilities and the ministry.

title: Rights of MLAs denied in revised protocol, allege BJP legislators
summary: BJP legislators claim revised state protocol undermines MLA privileges, elevating District Ministers and diminishing the Speaker's authority.
content:
Members of the BJP, on Wednesday, took serious exception to the recent changes in the State protocol that they allege take away the privileges of the MLAs.
Suresh Gowda of the BJP raised the issue during the Zero Hour in the Legislative Assembly and alleged that the rights of the legislators had been taken away. “As per the revised protocol, the District Minister will preside over the programmes attended by Chief Minister and DCM. Earlier, MLAs of the respective assembly constituency used to preside over the programmes,” he said.
Further, he pointed out that the revised protocol undermined the position of the Speaker of the House as well. “The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly has been placed below the Chairman of the Legislative Council and the High Court judges in the order of importance,” he said.
Leader of Opposition R. Ashok argued that the MLAs had been reduced to mere ‘guests’. “MLAs are the true representatives of the constituencies. The District Ministers are guests who can be removed anytime at the will of the Chief Minister,” he stated.
Minister for Law, H.K. Patil, responding to the debate, said the issue raised by the MLAs was serious and concerned the privileges of the MLAs. He would discuss it with the Chief Minister and the Chief Secretary and make a statement on the issue in the House on Thursday, he said.

title: Daily commute on Nookampalayam Link Road a headache for motorists
summary: Motorists face daily headaches on Nookampalayam Link Road due to ongoing stormwater drain construction and poor road conditions.
content:
Nookampalayam Link Road, stretching from the Semmancheri Tsunami quarters to Sholinganallur on Rajiv Gandhi Salai, is in a mess. Road users say the stretch has been in this condition for over a year, with stormwater drain (SWD) work in progress.
G. Premnath, a reisdent of the area, said that when he moved to the locality in 2018, “the road was very good.” He added: “Chennai Metrowater carried out some work first. After it was completed, the road was patched up very badly in June, covering all the chutes leading to the drain. One can see the iron bars peeking from under the concrete. Now, a stormwater drain is being constructed, and the sewer line is only half done. For the past three years, we have inhaled a lot of dust. If we complain to local officials, we just get yelled at.”
A.R. Srinivasan, a resident, said that due to the drain project, when a bus or a truck approaches from the opposite side, vehicles proceeding in the other direction get stuck. “Getting stuck on this four-lane road is almost a daily headache. I have approached every possible agency but have not been able to find out when the construction will be completed. It has been progressing very slowly. We don’t have access to our bank or the local hospital because of this work,” he said.
“The road surface has also been damaged at several spots in the recent rains. Sometimes, I prefer to travel an additional 6 km just to avoid this road. But not everyone can afford to do that,” he rued. The road has been experiencing increased traffic, with more buses now operating from Semmancheri and Perumbakkam.
“They keep changing the positions of the barricades, which leaves motorists unsure where to turn to the other side. It can take anywhere from 10 to 45 minutes to cross the road, which is only about 3 km long. Since some stretches have only one lane available, schoolchildren get stuck and end up going to school late. This important road is in very bad shape,” said Lakshmi, a parent of a child studying at a nearby school.
FOMRRA co-founder Harsha Koda recalled that the road had been in good condition for several years and said that these works could have been taken up before it was converted into a cement concrete road. He added that this development is a typical example of the “left hand not talking to the right hand” in government. “Imagine how much better our lives would be if we had a city planner who could do things in the right chronological order,” he said.
Sources in the Greater Chennai Corporation said that the project period was a year and a half, and that repairs would be taken up soon.

title: Man sentenced to seven-year imprisonment in POCSO case
summary: A 53-year-old man received a seven-year prison sentence for sexually assaulting a minor in Nandyal, Kurnool.
content:
A 53-year-old person was sentenced to seven year imprisonment and imposed a fine of ₹50,000 by POCSO Court in Kurnool for sexually assaulting a minor girl. The court also directed the convict to pay ₹1 lakh ex-gratia to the victim.
The accused, Y. Govindu, of Alamuru village in Rudravaram mandal in Nandyal district, sexually assaulted the minor girl on April 25, 2025 at Saijit Colony outskirts in Nandyal. A case was registered against him by the Nandyal Taluk police station under Section 65 (2) of BNS and also POCSO Act.

title: R&B Special CS asks officials to adhere to timelines for completion of new High Court complex
summary: Vikas Raj urges officials and contractors to meet deadlines for the new High Court complex in Hyderabad during site inspection.
content:
Roads & Buildings special chief secretary Vikas Raj directed the officials concerned and the contracting firm to adhere to the timeline set for the completion of the new High Court complex taken up at Rajendranagar.
Mr. Vikas Raj along with the Chief Engineers and other senior officials inspected the site on Wednesday. Representatives of D.E.C Infrastructure Projects, the contracting firm accompanied the official team which assessed the pace, sequencing and quality of works. The special chief secretary informed about the timelines finalised for completion of various components of the project.
The New High Court Buildings Complex, a flagship judicial infrastructure initiative of the State government, was sanctioned at a cost of ₹2,583 crore with a total built-up area of 36.52 lakh square feet. Of the sanctioned amount, ₹1,980 crore has been earmarked for civil, electrical and MEP works, while ₹603 crore has been earmarked for furniture and operative equipment.
Mr. Vikas Raj instructed the consultants to submit detailed construction drawings well in advance to facilitate mobilisation of manpower, materials and machinery and to prevent time and cost overruns. The Chief Engineer (Buildings), consultants and the contractor were directed to jointly prepare a comprehensive programme for completion of the project while the officials were instructed to closely monitor progress through regular reviews.
The contractor was asked to accelerate execution to meet the milestones and the consultants were directed to finalise revised plans in consultation with judicial authorities for securing approvals without delay. The Chief Engineer (Buildings) was asked to expedite all statutory clearances, including forest clearances for Zone-2 areas.
He wanted close collaboration among the department, consultants and contractor to recover delays arising from design changes and ensure timely completion of the project.

title: Trading fraud case: cybercrime police arrest key accused with links to Chinese national
summary: Trading fraud case: cybercrime police arrest key accused with links to Chinese national
content:
A 21-year-old man was arrested by the cyber crimes wing of the Hyderabad police in connection with an online trading fraud in which a city resident was cheated of ₹32 lakh.
The accused, Ansari Mohammed Umar Murad alias Umar, a native of Mumbai, was found to be in direct contact with a Chinese national and played a key role in routing the defrauded money through cryptocurrency channels, police said.
Following the arrest, the police seized a mobile phone and a laptop from the accused. Officials said analysis of the mobile phone revealed Telegram conversations with the Chinese national, including the sharing of bank account credentials, details of USDT conversions and other transaction-related information.
According to the police, a woman identifying herself as Aiyana Joseph, a trade adviser, persuaded him to invest through a fake trading application, which falsely displayed profits and IPO allotments.
In total, ₹32 lakh was transferred before he realised the fraud and reported the matter to the national cybercrime helpline and the local cybercrime police.
Investigations revealed that Ansari Mohammed Umar Murad had sound knowledge of cryptocurrency trading and, along with another accused identified as Rishi Thushar Arothe alias Vikranth, 30, a cricket coach and resident of Vadodara, Gujarat, converted the cheated amount from rupees to USDT before transferring them to wallet addresses supplied by the Chinese national. An amount of around ₹50 lakh was allegedly routed in this manner. Another accused, identified as Inamdar Vinayaka Rajendar alias Nikhil, 25, a private employee, also a resident of Vadodora,  provided bank accounts on a commission basis and arranged additional accounts from associates to facilitate fraudulent transactions.
Two other accused in the case were arrested earlier. The police said the accused persons are collectively involved in at least 12 similar cases across  Telangana, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Kerala, Haryana, Jammu and Kashmir, Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal.
The police urged people to be cautious of investment advertisements on social media claiming links with reputed companies, to avoid joining WhatsApp or Telegram groups promising guaranteed returns or IPO allotments, and to refrain from downloading trading applications shared through unknown links. He also warned against sharing bank accounts for commission, stating that mule accounts are frequently used in cyber frauds.

title: PM Modi arrives in Oman on final leg of three-nation visit
summary: PM Modi arrives in Oman to strengthen ties and finalise a crucial trade deal during his two-day visit.
content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday (December 17, 2025) arrived in Oman on a two-day visit during which he will hold talks with the country's top leadership and is expected to sign an ambitious trade deal.
He was warmly welcomed by Oman's Deputy Prime Minister for Defence Affairs Sayyid Shihab bin Tariq Al Said at the airport, where a guard of honour was accorded to the Prime Minister.
Mr. Modi is visiting Oman at the invitation of Sultan Haitham bin Tarik.
This is his second visit to the Gulf nation and marks 70 years of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries.
India has said that it is "very optimistic" about finalising an ambitious trade deal with Oman during the visit.
The free trade agreement between India and Oman was approved by the Union Cabinet last Friday (December 12, 2025).
Talks for the agreement, officially termed as CEPA (Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement), formally began in November 2023, and the negotiations concluded this year.
"We are all very optimistic about it. The teams from both sides have been working very hard for its early finalisation," Arun Chatterjee, a Secretary in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), had said at a media briefing when asked whether the proposed India-Oman comprehensive economic partnership agreement will be inked during Mr. Modi's visit.
"We have immense faith that this agreement, if signed during this visit, will significantly deepen the economic ties between India and Oman. And it will open up a new chapter in the history of India-Oman trade and commercial relationship," he said.
During the visit, Mr. Modi will also hold discussions with Sultan Tarik on strengthening the Strategic Partnership as well as a strong commercial and economic relationship.
Mr. Modi is also scheduled to address a gathering of the Indian diaspora in Muscat.
"This visit will be an opportunity for both sides to comprehensively review the bilateral partnership, including in the areas of trade, investment, energy, defence, security, technology, agriculture and culture, as well as exchange views on regional and global issues of mutual interest," the MEA said in an earlier statement.
Oman is the third-largest export destination for India among the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries. India already has a similar agreement with another GCC member, the UAE, which came into effect in May 2022.
India-Oman bilateral trade was about $10.5 billion (exports $4 billion and imports $6.54 billion) in 2024-25. India's key imports are petroleum products and urea. These account for over 70% of imports. Other key products are propylene and ethylene polymers, pet coke, gypsum, chemicals, iron and steel, and unwrought aluminium.
The main items of India's exports to Oman include mineral fuels, chemicals, precious metals, iron and steel, cereals, ships, boats and floating structures, electrical machinery, boilers, tea, coffee, spices, apparel, and food items.

title: New integrated Collectorate complex in Kallakurichi all set for inauguration
summary: Kallakurichi's new Integrated Collectorate complex, featuring 40 departments, is ready for inauguration on December 26.
content:
The integrated Collectorate complex at Veeracholapuram near Kallakurichi is all set for inauguration. 
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT
The construction of an integrated Collectorate complex for Kallakurichi district has been completed by the Public Works Department and the complex at Veeracholapuram near Kallakurichi is all set for inauguration soon.
The civil works have been completed and only the peripheral works, including landscaping and laying of approach roads are under way. The works are scheduled to be completed soon. Chief Minister M.K. Stalin is expected to inaugurate the building on December 26, a senior official said.
In 2019, the then AIADMK government announced the formation of Kallakurichi district by bifurcating the erstwhile Villupuram district. After Kallakurichi officially came into existence as the 33rd district of the State, efforts to split the administrative machinery from the composite Villupuram district gained pace and many government departments started functioning separately.
The Collectorate complex was temporarily accommodated at the Agricultural Marketing Committee office. Arrangements were also made to accommodate other departments, including Revenue and the Treasury at adjacent government buildings.
The State government initiated steps to identify land to construct the integrated Collectorate complex. Officials identified 35 acres of land belonging to the Arthanareeswarar temple at Veeracholapuram for constructing the Collectorate.
Though the construction of the eight-storey building began in 2020, the Madras High Court ordered the suspension of the construction on a petition filed by activist Rangarajan Narasimhan, who said the court had permitted the State to commence only preliminary work but the government had begun construction itself, without obtaining statutory clearances.
However, the court permitted the government to go ahead with the construction in May 2023, after the government submitted before the court that it had decided to take the land on lease at a monthly rent of ₹1.6 lakh, to be increased by 15% once in three years.
An undertaking was also given to the court that after taking 34.817 acres on lease, the balance of 5.003 acres of the temple land would be fenced properly and developed for purposes, such as putting up a ‘nandavanam’ (flower garden) and ‘goshala’ which would be consistent with the purpose for which the land had been endowed eons ago.
Official sources said the construction of the building had been completed and the final phase of work was under way which would be completed in a week’s time. The building is slated for inauguration on December 26.
Spread over 35.18 acres, the Collectorate complex will comprise at least 40 departments, including revenue, rural development, animal husbandry, agriculture, social welfare, labour, tourism, and Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments.
Three separate halls have been constructed for conducting review meetings, weekly grievance redressal meetings, and for distribution of welfare measures to the beneficiaries.
The complex will also have separate cabins for officials of various departments, conference room equipped with LED lights, and CCTV cameras. The Collector’s office will be on the third floor.

title: Kanimozhi to head DMK’s Assembly election manifesto committee
summary: Kanimozhi leads DMK's manifesto committee, gathering public input for the upcoming Assembly election in Tamil Nadu.
content:
The ruling DMK on Wednesday constituted a committee under the chairmanship of the party’s Parliamentary Party leader, Kanimozhi, to prepare the manifesto for the Assembly election scheduled for next year.
A press release issued by DMK general secretary Duraimurugan stated  the committee would tour the State and elicit opinions and views from welfare associations, traders’ associations, trade unions, farmers’ associations, alliance partners and the general public.
Other members of the committee include former MP T.K.S. Elangovan, Higher Education Minister Govi Chezhiaan, IT Minister Palanivel Thiaga Rajan, Industries Minister T.R.B. Rajaa, NRI wing secretary M.M. Abdulla, spokesperson Constantine Ravindran, environment wing secretary Karthikeya Sivasenpathy, MLA Dr Ezhilan Naganathan, women’s wing vice-pesident Tamilarasi Ravikumar, former IAS officer G. Santhanam, and Suresh Sambandam, convenor of Dream Tamil Nadu.

title: Activists demand action against Bihar CM over niqab incident
summary: Activists demand action against Bihar CM over niqab incident
content:
Taking strong exception to Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar purportedly pulling down a niqab (veil) of a woman, activists from Hyderabad submitted complaints to the city police, seeking FIRs to be registered against him.
Avideo clip surfaced online whichshowed Mr. Kumar pulling the veil of a Muslim woman at a government-organised event. He was handing over appointment letters to AYUSH doctors when he pointed out at a woman and pulled her niqab. The video clip was widely shared on social media, and drew criticism from various quarters.
Hyderabad-based activist Lubna Sarwath wrote to the Osmania University police seeking a Zero FIR against Mr. Kumar. Relying on media reports, she said that the incident happened on December 15. The act, she maintained, was in full public view and led to the woman being humiliated. She sought a case againt Mr. Kumar under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
She also wrote to the National Commission for Women urging them to take cognizance of the incident, direct Bihar Police to book a case, and take up an investigation, and ensure the protection of the woman, and provide counselling to her.
Another activist, Khalida Parveen, submitted a complaint against Mr. Kumar at the Langar Houz police station. She said that pulling or touching any piece of a woman’s clothing without her consent is a crime. “Mr. Kumar’s act had emboldened anti-social elements. He pulled the niqab by force. This is wrong, and a Chief MInister has done this,” she said, adding that the incident had hurt the sentiments of women, and had gravely belittled their dignity.
Emphasising that women should not feel frightened, she urged the Telangana police to file a case against the Bihar CM and take action. “A person occupying such an important position should never indulge in such things. He should have respect for the chair in which he is sitting,” she said.

title: Police officer suspended on charge of sexually harassing colleague
summary: Kollam police officer suspended after allegations of sexually harassing a colleague, breaching professional standards and workplace safety.
content:
The District Police Chief (Kollam City) has suspended a Senior Civil Police Officer (SCPO) following a sexual assault allegation involving a female colleague.
The move follows a preliminary probe that found that his behaviour violated the force’s professional standards. The suspension order was issued to SCPO M. Navas, who was working on deputation at the Neendakara Coastal Police Station from Alappuzha at the time of the incident.
The alleged assault took place in the early hours of November 6 and as per the complaint, the woman CPO was molested and verbally abused by Navas. Since the incident occurred on the station premises, it had sparked grave concerns about the breach of workplace safety and professional ethics.
The Chavara police had started investigating the incident based on the statement of the CPO and a case was registered under Sections 74 and 75 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for outraging the modesty of a woman and sexual harassment.
The suspension order issued by District Police Chief Kiran Narayanan observed that the involvement of a member of the force as an accused in such a case constitutes a grave breach of discipline and gross misconduct, tarnishing the reputation and dignity of the police department.

title: BMTC shifts bus stops closer to Yellow Line metro stations to improve last-mile connectivity
summary: After repeated complaints by commuters that bus stops are not near metro stations on the newly operational Yellow Line, Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. (BMRCL), in coordination with the Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation, has finally shifted and added several bus stops closer to metro stations.
content:
After repeated complaints by commuters that bus stops are not near metro stations on the newly operational Yellow Line, Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. (BMRCL), in coordination with the Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC), has finally shifted and added several bus stops closer to metro stations.
Metro services on the Rashtreeya Vidyalaya Road–Delta Electronics Bommasandra corridor began on August 11, 2025. Following joint inspections by BMRCL and BMTC, bus stops have been relocated or newly provided to ensure smoother interchange between buses and metro services, improving commuter convenience, according to BMRCL officials.
New BMTC bus stops have been established near metro stations at Biocon Hebbagodi, Beratena Agrahara, Singasandra, Hongasandra, Central Silk Board, and R.V. Road. In addition, existing bus stops at Electronics City, Hosa Road, and Ragigudda have been shifted closer to the respective metro stations.
Officials said that at Jayadeva, BTM Layout, Bommanahalli, Kudlu Gate, and Infosys Foundation Konappana Agrahara, bus stops are already available within 100 metres of metro stations, ensuring easy access for passengers.
“However, relocation of bus stops at Huskur Road and Delta Electronics Bommasandra could not be undertaken due to space constraints,” official added.

title: MoU signed to develop international township in Tirupati
summary: MoU signed for ₹35,000 crore international township in Tirupati, featuring luxury residences, adventure parks, and a unique Living Exhibition.
content:
In partnership with the State government, Della Townships will develop the Vasudev Kutumbakam International Township in Tirupati, envisaged as a landmark cultural and tourism-led development of global scale.
A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed on Wednesday to this effect.
The project will span 1,400 acres and be anchored by what is being described as the world’s first 5,000-year Living Exhibition on Hinduism and Hindutva. The initiative is being undertaken under the leadership of Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and founder of Della Townships Jimmy Mistry.
The project is envisioned as a long-term cultural institution that seeks to document, preserve, and present the civilisational journey of Hinduism with scholarly depth and authenticity. By bringing together diverse knowledge systems, traditions, philosophies, and lineages from across India, the project aims to create a comprehensive and immersive representation of Hindu civilisation, positioning Tirupati as a global centre for cultural learning and experiential tourism.
From an economic perspective, the project carries a gross development value of approximately ₹35,000 crore and is expected to generate around 20,000 jobs, with nearly 80% of the employment opportunities reserved for local residents.
The project will be developed in close collaboration with the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) and the Andhra Pradesh Tourism Department, strengthening the State’s position as a premier spiritual and cultural destination, said the statement.
The project will include a 300-acre ‘Living Exhibition’ that will feature 25 large-scale immersive pavilions, each covering approximately one lakh square feet. Luxury residences and private villas, along with five-star resorts offering more than 600 keys across various formats, also feature in the project. Destination wedding venues, extreme adventure parks, offering experiences such as bungee jumping, human catapult rides, zip biking, and quad ziplines, are also planned.
A Della Design District, housing 25 to 30 international luxury brands, and a European Medical Wellness Pavilion, an 18-hole international standard golf course with a business club, equestrian sports facilities with an international polo club, and a dedicated senior living hub aimed at promoting holistic and dignified ageing also include in the project plan.

title: Razor blades worth ₹1.20 crore donated to TTD
summary: Vertice Global donates ₹1.20 crore worth of razor blades to TTD, easing operational costs for tonsuring services.
content:
Razor blade manufacturers Vertice Global Private Limited of Hyderabad, on Wedenesday, donated Silver Max half blades worth ₹1.20 crore to the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD), sufficient to meet the temple body’s requirement for an entire year.
The donation was formally handed over by the company’s director Sridhar Boddupalli to TTD Chairman B.R. Naidu at the latter’s camp office in Tirumala.
Speaking on the occasion, Naidu said that the TTD spends approximately ₹1.16 crore annually on blades for use at its Kalyanakatta and other tonsuring centres, and that the contribution would substantially ease the operational expenditure of the institution. Nearly 40,000 half blades are used regularly at various tonsuring centres by the TTD to facilitate the devotees offering hair as a vow, he added.
Meanwhile, Mr. Sridhar Boddupalli claimed that Vertice Global Private Limited was the first company in the world to introduce half blades that have a great demand across 52 countries. They are also the manufacturers of the internationally acclaimed 7 O’Clock blades, he added.

title: Telangana issues health advisory as chilly weather raises seasonal flu risk
summary: Telangana issues health advisory to combat seasonal flu risk amid colder weather, urging precautions for vulnerable groups.
content:
The Telangana government on Wednesday (December 17) issued a health advisory cautioning residents against the spread of seasonal flu, following forecasts of dry weather and a drop in minimum temperatures across the State.
According to the advisory issued by Dr B. Ravinder Nayak, Director of Public Health and Family Welfare, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has predicted dry weather conditions over Telangana for the next 5 days, with minimum temperatures likely to remain below normal by 2°C to 3°C at isolated locations. The advisory warned that lower environmental temperatures could lead to an increase in acute respiratory infections, including seasonal flu.
Seasonal flu is described as an acute and highly contagious respiratory infection marked by symptoms such as fever, cough, sore throat, body ache and fatigue. It spreads easily from person to person through coughing or sneezing. “Most people recover on their own within a week if they rest at home and consume adequate fluids,” the advisory said.
The advisory said vulnerable groups, including pregnant women, children under five years, senior citizens above 65 years of age and individuals with chronic medical conditions face a higher risk of severe illness. These groups have been advised to consult a doctor if they develop flu-like symptoms.
People experiencing warning signs such as high fever, breathing difficulty, bluish discoloration of the skin or lips, blood in sputum or altered behaviour have been urged to seek immediate medical attention at the nearest government health facility without delay.
The advisory listed several dos and don’ts for the public. These include covering the mouth and nose with a handkerchief or tissue while coughing or sneezing, frequent handwashing with soap and water, avoiding public places when symptomatic, drinking sufficient water, eating nutritious food, ensuring adequate ventilation in indoor spaces and getting enough sleep.
“As part of precautionary measures, the government has made elaborate arrangements by providing special beds and essential medicines at all the public health facilities,” the advisory said.

title: Progress of Sonia, Rahul, Vadra only concern of Congress: BJP on protests against rural employment Bill
summary: BJP criticises Congress protests, claiming their focus lies solely on the Gandhi family's progress, not India's empowerment.
content:
The BJP slammed the Congress on Wednesday (December 17, 2025) over its protest against the Centre's rural employment bill, VB-G RAM G, that seeks to replace the MGNREGA, alleging that the opposition party is only concerned about the progress of Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi and Robert Vadra, not the country.
Irrespective of the obstructions put up by the Congress and its leaders, India will become a developed country before 2047, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi taking a vow to achieve the goal with the support of the people, BJP's national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia said.
"The Congress hates everything positive. The biggest worry of the Congress is Prime Minister Narendra Modi's resolve for Viksit Bharat (making India a developed country) and the steps he is taking to fulfil it," Mr. Bhatia told a press conference at the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) headquarters here, when asked about the opposition party's protest against the rural employment bill.
"For us, the goal is the empowerment and progress of the 140 crore people of the country. On the contrary, their goal is to ensure the progress of Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi and Rovert Vadra," he alleged.
The BJP spokesperson said the Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Bill brought in Parliament for its consideration and passage seeks to increase the number of working days and transparency in the implementation of the programmes.
However, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi would have understood that had he studied it, he said.
"The Gandhi family will not understand these things because (American investor) George Soros and uncle Quattrocchi have taken them under their control. Therefore, they will oppose any step taken to fulfil the Viksit Bharat dream," Mr. Bhatia added.
Quatrochhi's name figured in the Bofors scam when Rajiv Gandhi was the Prime Minister.

title: 103-year-old road overbridge dismantled at Solapur Yard
summary: Central Railway dismantles a 103-year-old overbridge at Solapur Yard, ensuring minimal disruption to passenger services during the operation.
content:
The Solapur Division of Central Railway successfully carried out a major special traffic block to dismantle a 103-year-old road overbridge at Solapur Yard, completing the complex operation with minimal disruption to passenger services.
The 19.7-metre road overbridge, constructed in 1922, was dismantled during a 13-hour 30-minute traffic block on December 14 as part of infrastructure modernisation and implementing safety measures.
Despite unforeseen challenges typically associated with decommissioning old structures, the division completed the dismantling work in 12 hours and 45 minutes and restored normal rail operations at Solapur Yard ahead of schedule.
Railway officials said that the ageing bridge had become structurally vulnerable due to heavy vehicular movement and posed operational constraints for rail traffic.
The restricted clearance under the bridge had limited train speeds to 15 kmph, affected track maintenance and forced stoppages of trains at Solapur, a key node on the Mumbai-Chennai section of Indian Railways Golden Quadrilateral.
The low clearance also created safety concerns for overhead traction lines, particularly in view of increased petroleum movement through the IOCL siding at Pakni near Solapur.
The dismantling was executed by the National Highways Authority of India in close coordination with Indian Railways, with extensive safety precautions in place to protect tracks, overhead equipment and signalling assets.
Overhead traction wires were temporarily dropped and restored using tower wagons, while tracks and points were shielded with steel channels, sandbags and protective planks to prevent damage from falling debris.
The operation involved the deployment of heavy machinery, including high-capacity hydraulic cranes, excavators and specialised breakers, and was closely monitored on-site by divisional officers.
A total of 691 personnel, comprising railway staff and contractual workers, were engaged to ensure round-the-clock execution and coordination.
Railway authorities said that the block was meticulously planned to minimise passenger inconvenience. Most major trains running to, from and via Solapur continued to operate with little or no disruption, ensuring connectivity to key destinations such as Mumbai, Pune and the southern and northern parts of the country.
Advance information on diversions, rescheduling and short terminations was disseminated through press releases, railway apps, social media platforms and SMS alerts.
To assist passengers during the block period, help desks were set up at Solapur, Kalaburagi, Pandharpur and Kurduvadi stations. Special arrangements were made for diverted and short-terminated services, including road transport assistance, for affected passengers.
In addition to dismantling the bridge, the Solapur Division optimally utilised the traffic block to carry out essential maintenance works through 21 shadow blocks across the Solapur-Wadi section. These included several safety-related works aimed at reducing the need for future traffic interruptions.
Officials said that the successful execution of the operation reflected the effective inter-departmental coordination, advance planning and the division’s commitment to safety, infrastructure upgradation and passenger-centric services.

title: DISCOMs threatening to disconnect services if consumers resist installation of smart meters: CPI(M)
summary: CPI(M) warns consumers face service disconnection if they resist smart meter installation, criticising government pressure tactics and private partnerships.
content:
CPI(M) State secretariat member Ch. Babu Rao on Wednesday (December 17) said DISCOMs were serving notices on consumers, insisting that they have smart meters installed or face disconnection of services. At a press meet, which he addressed along with party leader Donepudi Kasinath, he displayed one such notice served on a consumer in Vijayawada by the CPDCL.
Mr. Babu Rao recalled that the government had previously assured the consumers that it would not forcefully install smart meters, but it clearly did an about-turn, going by the notices given recently. He said that in the specified notice, the DISCOM sought valid reasons for not letting the IRDA devices replaced by smart meters, thereby putting pressure on the consumer.
It was evident from these tactics that the government was bent on installing the smart meters provided by Adani Energy Solutions Limited, to the detriment of about two crore consumers. The installation of smart meters entailed a burden of ₹25,000 crore on the public exchequer at a time when the State was purportedly struggling with a shoestring budget, he observed.
Mr. Babu Rao said leaders of the TDP, the Jana Sena Party and the BJP had opposed the smart meters before the elections but were now maintaining a stoic silence even as DISCOMs were creating illusions about the smart meters and mounting pressure on people to allow the installation of the devices. The DISCOMs were also in the process of imposing true-up charges amounting to over ₹12,000 crore.
​The Union and the State governments conspired to hand over the entire electricity distribution system to private companies, of which the installation of smart meters was a significant move, Mr. Babu Rao said, adding that the Left parties would organise Statewide protests if the government did not stop the installations forthwith.

title: Local body polls: voting in three wards on January 12
summary: Local body polls for three wards, including Vizhinjam, will be held on January 12, with voting from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.
content:
Special elections to three local body wards in the State, including Vizhinjam in the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation, will be held on January 12.
The local body polls to the three wards had been postponed following the deaths of candidates.
The State Election Commission (SEC) has issued the election notification. Polling will be held from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. on January 12. The votes will be counted on January 13.
Apart from Vizhinjam, the Payimbadam ward of the Moothedam grama panchayat in Malappuram district, and the Onakkoor ward in the Pambakkuda grama panchayat in Ernakulam district will see elections on January 12.
Candidates can file their nomination papers till December 24. The scrutiny of the papers will be held on December 26. December 29 is the deadline for withdrawing the nominations. Individuals who were candidates of the December 9 and 11 elections in the wards need not file nominations afresh.

title: Govt. Whip faults BRS reaction to disqualification petition verdict
summary: Govt. Whip faults BRS reaction to disqualification petition verdict
content:
HYDERABAD
Government Whip Adi Srinivas said that the decision of Assembly Speaker G. Prasad Kumar on the disqualification petitions filed against certain MLAs has to be abided by all.
Addressing a press conference at the media point in Assembly on Wednesday, after the Speaker gave his ruling, Mr. Srinivas said, “The Speaker heard arguments from both sides and delivered a judgment based on merit. Everyone must respect this decision.”
He condemned the personal attacks against the Speaker and other Congress leaders. He wondered how the BRS could criticise the Speaker’s decision when it had blatantly encouraged defections during its regime.
“It is surprising that the BRS is speaking about defections. Did they forget that TDP MLA Talasani was inducted into the Cabinet? Did they forget that Congress MLA Sabitha Indra Reddy was taken into the ministry? Over the past 10 years, 39 Opposition MLAs were welcomed into BRS,” he said.
He reminded the BRS leaders that earlier, when the Opposition parties had complained to the presiding officers on the issue of defections, no action was taken. “Even the present MLA from Quthbullapur, Kuna Vivekananda Goud, defected from TDP to TRS (now BRS). Former BRS MLA from Korutla, Kalvakuntla Vidyasagar Rao, engaged in cross-voting during MLC elections and was suspended. Today, his son and MLA Sanjay is speaking about defections,” Mr. Srinivas observed.
He said that if BRS was aggrieved by the Speaker’s decision, they could approach the High Court or even SC.

title: Srisailam temple EO asks devotees to utilise online services
summary: Srisailam temple EO encourages devotees to use online services for hassle-free darshan and accommodation bookings.
content:
Srisailam temple executive officer (EO) M. Srinivasa Rao asked the temple staff and employees to publicise the online services provided by the temple for the convenience of the devotees. Mr. Srinivasa Rao held a review on the implementation of the online services of Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Swamy temple with the heads of department and supervisors of the temple, on Wednesday.
He also urged the devotees to utilise the online services for darshan and accommodation, adding that the services were made online following the directions of the State government. “The Sparsha Darshan, ₹300 Athi Sheegra Darshan and ₹150 Sheegra Darshan tickets and also 14 Arjitha Sevas like Garbhalaya Abhisekham, Kumkumarchana, Ganapathi Homam, Rudra Homam, Maha Mrutyunjaya Homam, Kalyanotsavam, Annaprasana, Aksharabyasam and other seva tickets can be booked online,” he said.
“Every employee and officer should create awareness about the online services intended to provide hassle-free darshan and accommodation to the devotees. The volunteers, Shiva Sevaks, should also be made aware of the online services to give wider publicity,” Mr Srinivasa Rao said. He asked the Engineering officials to make a separate queue line for the devotees who book tickets online and instal boards on the available online services.
Online services shall be availed only through www.aptemples.ap.gov.in or www.srisailadevasthanam.org or Mana Mithra WhatsApp governance number 9552300009. Those who book online Sparsha Darshan and Arjitha Sevas have to bring a printed copy of the ticket, along with a xerox copy of Aadhar card, and produce original Aadhar card while scanning the QR code on the ticket.
As the Arjitha Sevas and Sparsha Darshan are performed at a specific time mentioned on the ticket, the EO asked the ticket holders to report 15 minutes in advance at the Arjitha Seva queue line.

title: State govt. committed to developing Belagavi, says Shivakumar
summary: Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar emphasizes the state government's commitment to developing Belagavi, mirroring Bengaluru's progress.
content:
The State government is committed to developing Belagavi on the lines of the State capital, Bengaluru, Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said in Belagavi on Wednesday.
“I feel happy every time I arrive in Belagavi. At times, I feel its climate is better than in Bengaluru. We are committed to ensuring the all-round development of Belagavi,” he said.
He was speaking after flagging off a Swachchata Run near the Fort Lake.
Urban Development and Urban Planning Minister Byrathi Suresh said that the State government has implemented several projects for the development of Belagavi.
He was speaking during the inauguration ceremony of the cleanliness run organized by the Urban Development Department and the Municipal Administration Department.
It was the dream of Mahatma Gandhi that the environment around us should be clean. He said that it is the duty of every citizen to make his dream come true. “Our government has given priority to cleanliness in urban areas. Waste disposal is being done scientifically in cities,” he said.
“It is a matter of joy that cities in our State are also getting a place in the top list of cleanest cities in the country. We are working towards a scenario where more cities, including Belagavi, joined this list in the coming days,” he said.
A large number of people, young and old, men and women participated in the run.

title: Draft anti-ragging legislation to be finalised in 45 days, govt. tells Kerala HC
summary: Kerala government to finalize anti-ragging legislation within 45 days, following High Court directive amid rising concerns over student safety.
content:
The State government has informed the Kerala High Court that the draft of the legislation meant to end ragging in educational institutions and hostels will be finalised in 45 days.
A draft Bill in this regard has been forwarded by the Law department to the General Administration department. In addition, the file concerned has been sent to the Chief Minister. The State Cabinet would take a call on the draft legislation and it will be placed before the Legislative Assembly. The matter has been posted for hearing on January 6.
The High Court had on October 30 directed the State government to complete within four weeks all steps for tabling the Kerala Prohibition of Ragging (Amendment) Bill, 2025, before the Assembly.
This was after a public interest litigation (PIL) was filed by the Kerala Legal Services Authority (KeLSA), seeking stronger laws to combat ragging in the wake of a spree of ragging-related incidents in the State, including one in which a student died.
The draft of the Bill had proposed anti-ragging committees, squads and mentoring cells in all educational institutions, and also anti-ragging cells in all police stations.

title: NIA attaches properties of accused involved in transnational human trafficking, cyber frauds
summary: NIA attaches properties of accused in human trafficking and cyber fraud, revealing a transnational criminal syndicate's operations.
content:
The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has attached two immovable properties of an accused involved in transnational human trafficking and cyber frauds, officials said on Wednesday (December 17, 2025).
One flat inMaharashtra'sThane and a piece of land inBihar'sSiwan purchased by the wanted accused, Anand Kumar Singh, in his wife's name using money earned illegally from human trafficking activities have been attached, a statement issued by the NIA said.
Singh, a Cambodia-based Indian national, was involved in trafficking Indian youths to Cambodia for forced criminal cyber fraud, NIA investigations revealed.
The special NIA court in Patna established the two properties to be proceeds of crime and ordered their attachment on December 10. It directed that the money obtained after their auction-sale be forfeited.
According to the NIA's investigation, the accused was part of a syndicate engaged in luring vulnerable youths from India with false promises of helping them get well-paying legitimate jobs in foreign countries.
Once the victims reached the foreign country, their passports were seized by the syndicate and they were sold to scam companies. Refusal to work for these companies led to mental and physical torture, the agency found during its investigation.
Efforts are in progress to unearth and dismantle the complete transnational nexus involving the syndicate, the statement said.

title: Kerala SIR house-to-house enumeration phase to end on December 18
summary: Kerala's house-to-house enumeration phase of the electoral roll concludes Thursday, with the draft roll published on December 23.
content:
Kerala is moving into the next phase of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll with the house-to-house enumeration phase coming to a close on Thursday (December 18).
Once the draft electoral roll is published on December 23, the booth-wise list of individuals who are not included on the list will be displayed on the notice boards of the electoral registration offices. This list will be available for scrutiny on the website of the Chief Electoral Officer (Kerala) and copies will be provided to recognised political parties. Booth-level officers (BLO) also have the list with them.
“This will allow the public to inspect the list and know the reasons why names have not been included,” CEO Rathan U. Kelkar’s office said on Wednesday. The BLOs have already handed over the list containing the names of absent, shifted and dead (ASD) voters to the booth-level agents appointed by the political parties, the CEO’s office said.
As per the latest updates, the number of ‘uncollectable’ enumeration forms (untraceable and ASD voters) stands at 24.95 lakh.
The draft electoral roll will be published on December 23. Claims and objections can be filed from that date to January 22. Voters who could not submit their enumeration forms on time can enroll in the voters’ list by filing their application using Form 6 with an affidavit. (Form 6 for new enrollment, Form 6A for overseas electors, Form 7 for removal of names on account of death, shifting, duplication of names and Form 8 for change of address and other corrections. Forms are available on https://voters.eci.gov.in).
Those who have not provided sufficient information would be summoned for hearings by the EROs. If a voter whose name is on the draft roll is excluded after the hearing, the first appeal can be filed before the District Election Officer within 15 days of the ERO’s order. The second appeal, if needed, can be filed before the CEO within 30 days of the order on the first appeal being issued.
Mr. Kelkar urged the voters to make use of these opportunities to ensure the accuracy of the voter roll.
Following the SIR, the final electoral roll will be published on February 21. Nonetheless, citizens will be able to add their names or make changes to the rolls until the last date for submitting nomination papers for the 2026 State Assembly elections, Mr. Kelkar said.

title: Unsafe preservative levels in cakes: Food Safety department starts crack down
summary: Food Safety department cracks down on cake manufacturers after finding unsafe preservative levels in 10 out of 32 samples.
content:
The Food Safety department has initiated strict measures to curb the use of excessive preservatives in cakes, aimed at increasing their shelf life.
Legal proceedings have been launched and cases were registered against manufacturers after 10 out of 32 samples were found to be unsafe, said Assistant Commissioner of Food Safety A. Sakeer Hussain on Wednesday.
“Food safety laws permit the use of potassium sorbate and sodium benzoate within prescribed limits. When these limits are exceeded, the test results will be marked as adverse, and prosecution proceedings will be initiated against the manufacturers. During the last financial year, 67 cake samples were tested and based on reports, 32 cases were filed in court,” he said.
The permissible limit for potassium sorbate and sodium benzoate is restricted to a maximum of 10 grams per 10 kilograms of cake. Small-scale manufacturers have been instructed approach Food Safety officers to clarify any doubts regarding the usage and regulation of preservatives.
Additionally, they are advised to attend free training programmes, such as Food Safety Training and Certification (FoSTaC), and obtain the required certification. “All manufacturers must ensure the safety of their products by conducting laboratory tests every six months. Home-based bakers are also required to obtain registration from the department and the fee for a five-year registration is ₹500,” said the official.
“Trading food products without a valid registration or license is an offense punishable by a fine of up to ₹10 lakh. In view of the Christmas and New Year season, strict inspections will be conducted and five squads have been formed in the district for sample collection,” added the official.

title: Rainbow Children’s Hospital opens in Rajamahendravaram
summary: Rainbow Children’s Hospital opens in Rajamahendravaram, offering specialized healthcare services for children and mothers in the region.
content:
PHOTOS IN DCX IN KAKINADA
Heritage Foods Private Limited executive director Nara Brahmani on Wednesday inaugurated the Rainbow Children’s Hospital in Rajamahendravaram city. The hospital aims to offer comprehensive child and mother care services with advanced neonatal, paediatric, obstetrics, gynaecology, and fertility care.
Ms. Brahmani said that with specialised access to paediatric and maternity care will make a meaningful difference to families in the city and the Godavari region districts.
Paediatric specialties, including neonatology, paediatric intensive care, general paediatrics, paediatric sub-specialties, foetal medicine, gynaecology, fertility and high-risk pregnancy care are few services available at the Rainbow Children’s Hospital, said Dr. Ramesh Kancharla, Rainbow Children’s Hospitals founding chairman.
Dr. Ramesh Kancharla claimed that the hospital aims to cover families within the 200 kilometre radius.
Rainbow Children’s Hospital is currently operating a network of hospitals across Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Delhi.

title: Democracy murdered in Assembly: BRS
summary: Democracy murdered in Assembly: BRS
content:
HYDERABAD
BRS working president K.T. Rama Rao lashed out at the Congress, stating that they have murdered democracy on the floor of the Assembly on Wednesday.
Reacting to the Speaker’s decision regarding the defected MLAs, KTR remarked that once again it’s been proved that Rahul Gandhi and the Congress have absolutely no respect for the nation’s highest courts or the Constitution.
KTR ridiculed the Congress leadership, stating that merely posing for photos holding a copy of the Constitution is not enough. “Rahul Gandhi will go down in history as an incompetent leader who failed to respect the very Anti-Defection Law brought in by his own father, late Rajiv Gandhi,” he said. KTR termed it a clear display of double standards by Rahul Gandhi and the Congress party to protect MLAs who have openly admitted to defecting for ‘development’.
The BRS has decided to take a legal recourse seeking application of Anti-Defection Law against its 10 MLAs who allegedly switched loyalty to the ruling Congress after winning on the BRS ticket.
The BRS has alleged that Assembly Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar delivered his verdict dismissing the disqualification petitions filed against five of its MLAs allegedly at the behest of Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy. The Speaker’s unilateral decision dismissing the disqualification petitions was tantamount to ridiculing the Constitution and judiciary.
The order copy (dismissing disqualification petitions in a single line) is apparently prepared at the Jubilee Hills mansion of the Chief Minister, who assured protection to the defected legislators, BRS MLAs K.P. Vivekanand and Kalvakuntla Sanjay said recalling the Chief Minister’s claim that there was no scope for byelections in the near future.
In a statement, former Minister T. Harish Rao and former MP B. Vinod Kumar termed Speaker’s ruling a “serious blow to democracy.” He demanded constitutional reforms: “The Tenth Schedule must be amended. Parliament should immediately enact a special law to deal with defections.” He said:“By today’s judgment, the Speaker has rendered Rajiv Gandhi’s law useless. The Congress Party itself has shown the nation that the anti-defection law is ineffective.”
Mr. Harish Rao said: “Rahul Gandhi’s slogan of ‘Save the Constitution’ has been fully exposed today by the Speaker’s verdict. This incident has gravely damaged the democratic principles and amounts to a violation of the Constitution by the Congress government.”

title: Do not restrict CUET-PG test to English and Hindi: OBC students association
summary: The All India OBC Students Association on Wednesday urged the Centre to conduct CUET-PG in all Scheduled Languages, instead of limiting it to English and Hindi.
content:
The All India OBC Students Association (AIOBCSA) on Wednesday urged the Centre and the National Testing Agency (NTA) to conduct the Common University Entrance Test for postgraduate courses (CUET-PG) in all Scheduled Languages instead of restricting it to English and Hindi.
In a media statement, the association said the current CUET-PG language policy was creating barriers for non-Hindi-speaking students, particularly those from rural backgrounds who have completed their schooling and undergraduate education in regional languages. It maintained that these students were being forced to compete in languages that were neither their medium of instruction nor their primary language of academic learning.
The association said the restriction affects students from Other Backward Classes, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, minority communities as well as first-generation learners. The exclusion of Scheduled Languages from the entrance examination was akin to a violation of constitutional principles.
The AIOBCSA demanded that the CUET-PG be conducted in all Scheduled Languages to ensure a level-playing field for students across the country and to uphold the spirit of inclusive education.

title: New MD for Kerala Paper Products Limited
summary: Prasad Balakrishnan Nair appointed as Managing Director of Kerala Paper Products Limited, bringing over 35 years of experience.
content: The State government has appointed Prasad Balakrishnan Nair, Special Officer, Kerala Paper Products Limited, as Managing Director of the company. He has over 35 years of experience in manufacturing, project management, and technology management. Mr. Nair has also served as the chief executive officer of the Maker Village.

title: Bill to set up higher education panel will destroy State’s institutions: Minister
summary: Minister R. Bindu warns that the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill could undermine Kerala's higher education institutions and autonomy.
content:
The Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025, that seeks to regulate higher education institutions has the potential to create a severe crisis in the higher education sector, Minister for Higher Education R. Bindu has said.
Addressing a press conference here on Wednesday, the Minister said the Bill went against federal principles and brought higher education, which was on the Concurrent List, fully within the purview of the Union government.
The Bill would take forward centralisation of powers that was seen in other sectors in the higher education sector too. Union government policies would be imposed on the State government and the higher education sector.
According to two clauses – 45 and 47, higher education councils had to work according to the Union government policies and decisions. This could lead to loss of autonomy, the Minister said.
Earlier, grants were limited but now all would be channelled through the Union Education Ministry, Dr. Bindu said.
She expressed apprehension that the Bill provided for uniformity in curriculum and syllabus and other academic matters even in universities funded and monitored by the State government, leading to far-reaching consequences.
The Minister said the Bill gave the VBSA umbrella commission punitive powers to impose penalties ranging from ₹10 lakh to ₹2 crore on higher education institutions for violations.
Dr. Bindu said activities to create public awareness of the Bill would be organised. Kerala would continue to lead protests against the Bill, similar to that organised against the UGC Draft Regulations.
Responding to questions on whether the long delay in appointment of Vice-Chancellors to two State-run universities could have been avoided, Dr. Bindu said the government had taken the initiative for truce many times.
Minister P. Rajeeve and she had visited the Governor earlier too. Now, the Chief Minister had met the Governor and held conciliatory talks. The Supreme Court too had asked the Governor and the Chief Minister to reach a consensus.
Asked whether the appointment of Ciza Thomas as the V-C of APJ Abdul Kalam Technological University would lead to disagreements and stalemates, Dr. Bindu said there was no need for discord if one worked objectively.
Dr. Bindu denied that the government had to compromise on the issue of V-C appointments. “This will be of relief to the State’s higher education sector. The uncertainty that existed could not continue any longer. Appointment of V-Cs to other universities also needs to be done. The hope is that the best candidates will be selected through mutual understanding.”

title: Community balance emerges as key factor for Mayor selection in Thrissur Corporation
summary: Community balance influences Mayor selection in Thrissur Corporation as Congress deliberates candidates ahead of upcoming elections.
content:
Deliberations within the Congress over who should become the next Mayor and Deputy Mayor of the Thrissur Corporation have gathered momentum. With the Assembly elections approaching, the party is keen to ensure community balance in the Mayor and Deputy Mayor posts. At present, the names of Subi Babu and Laly James are leading the race.
The party’s strategy is to divide the tenure into two or three terms and give the mayoral post to members of the majority or minority communities in alternate terms.Former Deputy Mayor Ms. Babu has been elected councillor for the fourth time, while Ms. James, who defeated the CPI(M)’s Mayor candidate, is also serving a fourth term as councillor.
For the Deputy Mayor’s post, the name of Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee secretary A. Prasad is under active consideration. The final decision will be taken after consulting senior leaders in the district as well as All India Congress Committee general secretary K.C. Venugopal, Leader of the Opposition V.D. Satheesan, and senior leader Ramesh Chennithala.
The newly elected councillors will take oath on December 21. The decision on the Mayor and Deputy Mayor will follow, with elections to both posts scheduled for December 26.

title: IFFK 2025: A useful ghost is more than just a ghost story
summary: A vacuum cleaner haunted by a ghost is the kind of one-liner which can draw in a festival audience looking for a little light-hearted fun to fill the time slots available between the “heavier” films which require much closer attention. A useful ghost, the debut feature of Thai filmmaker Ratchapoom Boonbunchachoke being screened in the world cinema category at the 30th International Film Festival of Kerala (IFFK), even appears so in the initial hour. Until, the film becomes something more, with strong undercurrents of Thailand’s contemporary political history.
content:
A vacuum cleaner haunted by a ghost is the kind of one-liner which can draw in a festival audience looking for a little light-hearted fun to fill the time slots available between the “heavier” films which require much closer attention.A useful ghost, the debut feature of Thai filmmaker Ratchapoom Boonbunchachoke being screened in the world cinema category at the 30th International Film Festival of Kerala (IFFK), even appears so in the initial hour. Until, the film becomes something more, with strong undercurrents of Thailand’s contemporary political history. 

A person who has just purchased a new vacuum cleaner is woken up at night by the machine’s loud coughing. As it turns out, the vacuum cleaner is haunted by a factory worker who had died on the job. The loud coughs are his expression of anger against the vacuum cleaner company, which he believes had caused his death. It is not the only haunted vacuum cleaner in town. The company owner’s son appears to be in love with a vacuum cleaner possessed by Nat, his dead wife. All this is fodder for much humour which punctuates the initial half of the film.

In a way, this treatment also lulls the viewer into assuming that the love story between man and machine might be intended as a backdrop for the filmmaker’s take on air pollution induced by the constant stream of development projects. That is until we learn about the existence of the “useful” ghosts and the inconvenient ghosts. Nat, now considered a useful ghost, is approached by the political and military establishment to read the dreams of the inconvenient ghosts who have been haunting the political leaders for the cruelties of the past. 

The film reveals its contemporary connections at this juncture, when we realise that the inconvenient ghosts are those of the ‘Red Shirt’ protesters who faced intense repression from the Thai military in 2010. According to news reports from that time, around 90 mostly unarmed civilians who were protesting raising demands for timely elections were killed in the crackdown, while thousands sustained injuries. The military crackdown was also accompanied by the closure of media seen to be supportive of the protesters. 

Boonbunchachoke’s film, which blends multiple genres in the service of its sweeping theme, expects the viewer to submit to its internal logic. This involves not just ghosts possessing machines, but also the possibility of reading others’ dreams as well as the ghosts disappearing when their memory is wiped away from the minds of the living. The last possibility is at the heart of the film’s potent message, that of the struggle of memory against forgetting, to keep alive even the recent historical memories when it is being erased and rewritten in real-time. 

The screenwriter squeezes in quite a few elements which at times makes the film a bit unwieldy and meandering. It also strives a little too much in driving home the point, when a final reveal about the underlying theme could have done the job far more effectively. Yet, the film stands out for its inventiveness in using a humourous ghost story to coat what is a difficult story to tell. The film is Thailand’s official entry for the Best International Feature Film category at the Academy Awards this year.

title: Thief arrested, ₹4 lakh in cash recovered in Chitradurga
summary: Thief arrested in Chitradurga with ₹4 lakh cash recovered; police continue search for accomplices.
content:
The Molakalmur Police have arrested a thief who used to siphon off money from bank customers after diverting their attention. The police have recovered ₹4 lakh in cash from the accused.
According to a release issued by Chitradurga Police, the 19-year-old accused has been identified as N. Surya alias Ganesh of Bhadravati Town.
After cases of money being stolen from people while returning from banks were reported, Superintendent of Police Ranjitkumar Bandaru constituted a team led by Molakalmur Police Sub-Inspector Mahesh Laxman Hospet, under the guidance of Additional Superintendent of Police Shivakumar R., Deputy Superintendent of Police Satyanarayan Rao and Circle Inspector of Police Nagaraj.
The team has succeeded in arrested the accused. It has now launched a manhunt for the accomplices of the accused.

title: 46 scrub typhus cases identified in Annamayya district
summary: Health officials report 46 scrub typhus cases in Annamayya district, prompting awareness campaigns and sanitation efforts to prevent spread.
content:
Medical and Health officials identified as many as 46 cases of scrub typhus across Annamayya district, which included 11 cases within Madanapalle Assembly constituency limits.
The first scrub typhus case in the Madanapalle division was confirmed on Wednesday. A medical officer said that a native of Cheruvu Mundara Palli village of Kollabayalu panchayat had been tested positive for the disease. The panchayat secretary, along with senior medical officials from Madanapalle, inspected the area and created awareness among locals about preventive measures.
The officials also took up a sanitation drive in the panchayat. Bleaching powder was sprayed in the surrounding areas, and residents were advised to remain alert and maintain hygiene to prevent further spread of the infection.
A special team from the District Medical and Health department stepped up surveillance in vulnerable villages in Rajampeta, Rayachoti and Madanapalle divisions, besides planning a series of awareness campaigns to educate people on symptoms and early treatment. The district officials urged the public not to panic and seek medical attention if symptoms such as fever, headache or body pain persist.

title: Digitisation of inscriptional estampages commences at Epigraphy Directorate in Mysuru
summary: Digitisation of inscriptional estampages begins at ASI's Mysuru Directorate, enhancing research access and preserving historical artifacts.
content:
The digitisation of inscriptional estampages at the Directorate of Epigraphy, Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), Mysuru, has commenced under Bharat Shared Repository of Inscriptions (BharatSHRI) in a boost to research and scholarship.
The project was accorded budgetary approval in the Union Budget 2023-24. The digitisation of inscriptional estampages is already under way at different branches of ASI across the country.
Estampages are replicas of original inscriptions created using inked paper, and the Directorate of Epigraphy has a repository of nearly 76,000 estampages of inscriptions — generally on stone or copper plates — from across India, dating back to several centuries and hence being an important source of history.
The digitisation exercise was inaugurated at the Directorate of Epigraphy in Mysuru on December 17. Munirathnam Reddy, director, (Epigraphy), ASI, said it will help create a comprehensive digital repository of India’s inscriptions under the BharatSHRI project.
“We will upload and update the digital database of the scanned material every week. Scholars and the general public will have access to the inscriptional material, complete with metadata, transcriptional details, and so on,” he added.
Explaining the benefits of the project, Dr. Reddy said it will significantly boost epigraphical research and for scholars, it will obviate the need to physically visit epigraphy offices or museums to study them, thus helping them save time.
Since the inscriptions can be accessed digitally, it will help preserve the original estampages, some of which are more than 100 years old and in Dravidian languages including Kannada, Telugu and Malayalam. The Tamil estampages have been shifted to Chennai.
The digitisation work is being carried out by Bengaluru-based Crystal Infosystems and Services Pvt. Ltd., which has initiated the scanning process using a specialised high-resolution scanner.
The project entails making high-resolution images with a scanning ratio of 1:1 that can provide a print of the actual size of the original, said Dr. Munirathnam.
“Some estampages  are 20 ft long and can be accessed without loss of clarity,” he added, saying that the digitisation is expected to be completed in six months and will provide scholars with access to digital archives at the click of a button.”

title: Court finds Mohanlal-starrer Karmayodha plagiarised, orders ₹30 lakh compensation
summary: Court rules Karmayodha plagiarized, orders ₹30 lakh compensation to Reji Mathew for exclusive rights to story and screenplay.
content:
In a significant order, the Commercial Court in Kottayam has ruled that Reji Mathew of Kottayam is the sole and absolute owner of the authorship and copyright of the story, script, and screenplay ofKarmayodha, a Malayalam movie directed by Major Ravi and starring Mohanlal.
Considering a complaint filed by screenplay writer Reji Mathew, Principal Sub Judge Manish D.A. has held that the film, released in December 2012, was produced using his story, screenplay, and dialogues without permission. Declaring that the story, screenplay, and dialogues ofKarmayodhaare the exclusive original works of Reji Mathew, the court directed the defendants, including Major Ravi, to pay ₹30 lakh as compensation. In the event of default, Mr. Mathew would be entitled to recover the amount with interest at 6% per annum from the date of the decree until payment.
The court also ruled that Reji Mathew alone holds complete rights over the story, screenplay, and dialogues under the Indian Copyright Act. These rights include publication in book form, film production, remakes in other languages, and all forms of broadcasting and exploitation through satellite television, OTT platforms, and other visual media.
The court also prohibited the publication, screening, or broadcast ofKarmayodha, or any films made in other languages using the same story, screenplay, or dialogues, including the publication of the visual screenplay in book form, without Reji Mathew’s consent and proper title credit.
About a month before the film’s release in 2012, Mr. Mathew had approached the court seeking a stay on its release. At that time, the court permitted the release of the film on the condition that ₹5 lakh be deposited with the court.
